Let C be a smooth projective connected curve over k and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree four. Call gamma simply branched when every geometric fibre has at most one ramification point and that point, if present, has ramification index two; equivalently, every local monodromy permutation in S_4 is a transposition. (a) No such gamma that factors nontrivially through an intermediate smooth projective curve is simply branched. A nontrivial factorization is a pair of finite morphisms C -> Y -> P^1 each of degree at least two (necessarily both of degree two); equivalently, k(C)/k(P^1) is composite of two proper extensions and the monodromy representation of pi_1^et(P^1 minus the branch locus of gamma) in S_4 is imprimitive. Two independent reasons. First: a simply branched connected degree-four cover has all local monodromies transpositions, so its monodromy group G <= S_4 is transitive and generated by transpositions. A transitive subgroup of S_n generated by transpositions equals S_n, because the undirected graph on n letters with those transpositions as edges is connected and the transpositions of a connected graph generate S_n. Thus G = S_4, which is primitive on four letters. A nontrivial factorization supplies a G-invariant partition of a general fibre into two blocks of size two, so G lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_2 of order 8, contradicting G = S_4. (The wreath product contains the two within-block transpositions, but those generate an intransitive Klein subgroup; transitivity of an imprimitive degree-four group requires a block-swapping element, necessarily a double transposition or a 4-cycle.) Second, without invoking S_4: any degree-two morphism q : Y -> P^1 from a smooth projective connected curve Y is ramified, since Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g_Y-2 = 2(-2)+deg R_q, hence deg R_q = 2g_Y+2 >= 2. Over each branch value of q the fibre of gamma = q o psi is of type (2,2) if psi is etale over the unique point of Y above it, or of type 4 (local monodromy a 4-cycle; locally the composition of two simple ramified double covers is z |-> z^4) if psi is ramified there; neither fibre is a transposition. Then the branch locus of gamma consists of exactly fourteen points of P^1: ten of fibre type 2+1+1 (local monodromy a transposition, over q(b) for b in B) and four of fibre type (2,2) (local monodromy a double transposition, over the four branch values of q, because psi is etale above each q-ramification point so both of its preimages acquire ramification index two). This agrees with Riemann-Hurwitz 2g_C-2 = 4(2g_{P^1}-2)+deg R, i.e. 10 = -8 + deg R. If B meets Ram(q), the corresponding fibre of gamma is a single point of ramification index four, with local monodromy a 4-cycle. If B contains a sigma-pair, the two would-be transposition fibres over q(b) and q(sigma(b)) coincide as a single extra (2,2) fibre. - `FND-0159` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'characteristic': 0, 'cover': {'degree': 4, 'genus': 6}, 'does_not_assert': ['closedness of the composed or type-(ii) locus', 'irreducibility or equidimensionality of the balanced Hurwitz scheme', 'regularity of the coarse space at points with finite residual automorphisms', 'absence of stacky points', 'smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient', 'any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion'], 'hypotheses': ['k algebraically closed of characteristic zero', 'C smooth geometrically connected projective of genus g', 'gamma finite of degree d (hence separable)', 'target P^1 held fixed'], 'objects': ['unrestricted fixed-target Hurwitz stack of all finite degree-d genus-g covers', 'Hurwitz normal sheaf N_gamma'], 'target': 'fixed P^1, not modulo Aut(P^1)'}]: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree d from a smooth geometrically connected projective k-curve C of genus g, with the target P^1 held fixed (not taken modulo Aut(P^1)). Then the differential d(gamma) : T_C -> gamma^* T_{P^1} is injective as a map of line bundles, so the Hurwitz normal sheaf N_gamma := coker(d(gamma)) is a torsion coherent sheaf supported on the ramification locus of gamma. Its length equals deg(gamma^* T_{P^1}) - deg(T_C) = 2d + 2g - 2, independently of the ramification profile, and equivalently equals sum_p (e_p - 1) by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula. A coherent sheaf of zero-dimensional support on a Noetherian curve has vanishing H^1, so H^1(C, N_gamma)=0. Consequently the deformation functor of C as a finite P^1-scheme (equivalently, of the pair (C, gamma) with varying source and fixed target, modulo automorphisms of the source over P^1) is unobstructed, with tangent space H^0(C, N_gamma) of k-dimension 2d+2g-2. Therefore the Deligne-Mumford stack of finite degree-d covers of a fixed P^1 by smooth connected genus-g curves -- equivalently the smooth-domain open of the Kontsevich stack M_{g,0}(P^1, d) -- is smooth of dimension 2d+2g-2 at every such point, independently of the ramification profile. For (d,g)=(4,6) this dimension is 18. This is a statement about the unrestricted stack of all ramification types. It is distinct from the classical Hurwitz space of covers with a fixed number r of distinct branch values (or a fixed ramification profile), which is etale over the configuration space of r points and has dimension r; that dimension equals 2d+2g-2 if and only if the cover is simply branched. In particular the unrestricted smoothness statement applies at composed or imprimitive points, which are never simply branched. Finite residual automorphisms, such as the deck involution of a composed cover, give Deligne-Mumford inertia with vanishing Lie algebra and do not change the stack dimension. The statement does not assert closedness of the composed or type-(ii) locus, irreducibility or equidimensionality of the balanced Hurwitz scheme, regularity of the coarse space at stacky points, smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient (dimension 2d+2g-5), or any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion.

(S1) Ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type DM stacks over C carries functorial mixed Hodge structures with H^m of weights at least m. (S2) The purity (Gysin) long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures for a smooth closed substack of pure codimension c in a smooth DM stack. (3) For every admissible chain, A_j/A_{j+1} = 0 when n_j <= 7, because the ordinary degree 2n_j - 16 is negative; A_j/A_{j+1} = 0 when n_j >= 17, because then 2n_j - 16 > n_j = dim S_j = dim S_j^c and (S3) followed by (S4) on the affine coarse space kills H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q); and A_j/A_{j+1} is a finite direct sum of Q(8), possibly zero, when n_j = 8, being a subquotient of H^0(S_j;Q)(8) and hence such a sum by (S6). (5) T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if, for one admissible chain -- equivalently, by (4), for every admissible chain -- every graded piece A_j/A_{j+1} with 9 <= n_j <= 16 is a finite direct sum of Q(8). 119:- `FND-0155` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'coefficients': 'not applicable (permutation representation, not cohomology)', 'does_not_assert': ['Any Tate, Hodge, weight, or purity conclusion', 'The exact monodromy image in type (ii) beyond containment in S_2 wr S_3', 'Applicability to algebraic stacks with inertia', 'H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component', 'Any statement about Aut(C,Gamma), moduli inertia, or stack-level full faithfulness', 'Any morphism to M_{6,6} or its properties'], 'hypotheses': ['Algebraically closed base field of characteristic zero', '(CE): standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution', '(N): O_X(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)', '(BAL): F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)', 'Type (i): phi_L birational onto a plane sextic (or a connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base meeting the type-(i) locus)', 'Normality, integrality, and local Noetherianity of U_alpha for the irreducibility upgrade and FND-0152 identity'], 'objects': ['|L|^{rs}', 'Ord(|L|^{rs})', 'H_alpha', 'Z_alpha', 'X_L (plane sextic)', 'X_L^vee (dual curve)'], 'subproblem_id': 'C66-GEO-COMP'}]: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre (satisfying (CE)+(N)+(BAL) at (g,n)=(6,6) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero), the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6. 122:- `FND-0158` [corroborated; {'case': {'degree': 4, 'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'does_not_assert': ['that the conclusion of ATT-0111 CLM-0111-9 (every type-(ii) point of the ambient fixed-target balanced Hurwitz scheme lies on a component meeting type (i)) is false', 'closedness of the composed locus in the Hurwitz scheme', 'any analysis of intermediate genus two or three beyond the general part (a)', 'any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, stack-inertia, or RED-0001 conclusion'], 'ground_field': 'algebraically closed of characteristic zero', 'hypotheses': ['k algebraically closed of characteristic zero (tame ramification d_x=e_x-1)', 'C smooth projective connected', 'nontrivial factorization means both maps finite of degree at least two, necessarily 2 then 2', 'simply branched means every geometric fibre has partition type 2+1+1+1, i.e. local monodromy a transposition', 'part (b) additionally: B reduced, B disjoint from Ram(q), and sigma(B) cap B empty'], 'part_a': 'any connected finite degree-four cover of P^1 from a smooth projective curve over k; not restricted to genus six', 'part_b': 'the FND-0154 balanced type-(ii) family: Y elliptic, q of degree two, psi a double cover branched along a reduced divisor B of degree ten, gamma=q o psi'}]: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let C be a smooth projective connected curve over k and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree four. Call gamma simply branched when every geometric fibre has at most one ramification point and that point, if present, has ramification index two; equivalently, every local monodromy permutation in S_4 is a transposition. (a) No such gamma that factors nontrivially through an intermediate smooth projective curve is simply branched. A nontrivial factorization is a pair of finite morphisms C -> Y -> P^1 each of degree at least two (necessarily both of degree two); equivalently, k(C)/k(P^1) is composite of two proper extensions and the monodromy representation of pi_1^et(P^1 minus the branch locus of gamma) in S_4 is imprimitive. Two independent reasons. First: a simply branched connected degree-four cover has all local monodromies transpositions, so its monodromy group G <= S_4 is transitive and generated by transpositions. A transitive subgroup of S_n generated by transpositions equals S_n, because the undirected graph on n letters with those transpositions as edges is connected and the transpositions of a connected graph generate S_n. Thus G = S_4, which is primitive on four letters. A nontrivial factorization supplies a G-invariant partition of a general fibre into two blocks of size two, so G lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_2 of order 8, contradicting G = S_4. (The wreath product contains the two within-block transpositions, but those generate an intransitive Klein subgroup; transitivity of an imprimitive degree-four group requires a block-swapping element, necessarily a double transposition or a 4-cycle.) Second, without invoking S_4: any degree-two morphism q : Y -> P^1 from a smooth projective connected curve Y is ramified, since Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g_Y-2 = 2(-2)+deg R_q, hence deg R_q = 2g_Y+2 >= 2. Over each branch value of q the fibre of gamma = q o psi is of type (2,2) if psi is etale over the unique point of Y above it, or of type 4 (local monodromy a 4-cycle; locally the composition of two simple ramified double covers is z |-> z^4) if psi is ramified there; neither fibre is a transposition. (b) Specialise to the FND-0154 balanced type-(ii) family: Y a smooth genus-one curve, P in Pic^2(Y), q = phi_{|P|} : Y -> P^1 the associated finite flat degree-two morphism (four ramification points), M in Pic^5(Y), B a reduced divisor in |M^{otimes 2}| of degree ten, psi : C -> Y the double cover with psi_* O_C isomorphic to O_Y direct-sum M^{-1} branched along B, and gamma = q o psi. Assume in addition that B is disjoint from Ram(q) and that sigma(B) cap B is empty for the unique nontrivial deck involution sigma of q. Then the branch locus of gamma consists of exactly fourteen points of P^1: ten of fibre type 2+1+1 (local monodromy a transposition, over q(b) for b in B) and four of fibre type (2,2) (local monodromy a double transposition, over the four branch values of q, because psi is etale above each q-ramification point so both of its preimages acquire ramification index two). In characteristic zero the different has multiplicity d_x = e_x-1 at each ramification point, so the total ramification is 10*1 + 4*2 = 18. This agrees with Riemann-Hurwitz 2g_C-2 = 4(2g_{P^1}-2)+deg R, i.e. 10 = -8 + deg R. If B meets Ram(q), the corresponding fibre of gamma is a single point of ramification index four, with local monodromy a 4-cycle. If B contains a sigma-pair, the two would-be transposition fibres over q(b) and q(sigma(b)) coincide as a single extra (2,2) fibre. In particular the set of simply branched type-(ii) points is empty, so no deformation argument that requires eighteen distinct simple branch values, or etaleness of the fixed-target Hurwitz scheme over Conf_18 at a type-(ii) point, can apply to any point of the FND-0154 parameter space. This statement asserts neither that every type-(ii) point of the ambient fixed-target balanced Hurwitz scheme lies on a component meeting type (i), nor any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, stack-inertia, or RED-0001 conclusion.
123:- `FND-0159` [corroborated; {'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'characteristic': 0, 'cover': {'degree': 4, 'genus': 6}, 'does_not_assert': ['closedness of the composed or type-(ii) locus', 'irreducibility or equidimensionality of the balanced Hurwitz scheme', 'regularity of the coarse space at points with finite residual automorphisms', 'absence of stacky points', 'smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient', 'any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion'], 'hypotheses': ['k algebraically closed of characteristic zero', 'C smooth geometrically connected projective of genus g', 'gamma finite of degree d (hence separable)', 'target P^1 held fixed'], 'objects': ['unrestricted fixed-target Hurwitz stack of all finite degree-d genus-g covers', 'Hurwitz normal sheaf N_gamma'], 'target': 'fixed P^1, not modulo Aut(P^1)'}]: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree d from a smooth geometrically connected projective k-curve C of genus g, with the target P^1 held fixed (not taken modulo Aut(P^1)). Then the differential d(gamma) : T_C -> gamma^* T_{P^1} is injective as a map of line bundles, so the Hurwitz normal sheaf N_gamma := coker(d(gamma)) is a torsion coherent sheaf supported on the ramification locus of gamma. Its length equals deg(gamma^* T_{P^1}) - deg(T_C) = 2d + 2g - 2, independently of the ramification profile, and equivalently equals sum_p (e_p - 1) by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula. A coherent sheaf of zero-dimensional support on a Noetherian curve has vanishing H^1, so H^1(C, N_gamma)=0. Consequently the deformation functor of C as a finite P^1-scheme (equivalently, of the pair (C, gamma) with varying source and fixed target, modulo automorphisms of the source over P^1) is unobstructed, with tangent space H^0(C, N_gamma) of k-dimension 2d+2g-2. Therefore the Deligne-Mumford stack of finite degree-d covers of a fixed P^1 by smooth connected genus-g curves -- equivalently the smooth-domain open of the Kontsevich stack M_{g,0}(P^1, d) -- is smooth of dimension 2d+2g-2 at every such point, independently of the ramification profile. For (d,g)=(4,6) this dimension is 18. This is a statement about the unrestricted stack of all ramification types. It is distinct from the classical Hurwitz space of covers with a fixed number r of distinct branch values (or a fixed ramification profile), which is etale over the configuration space of r points and has dimension r; that dimension equals 2d+2g-2 if and only if the cover is simply branched. In particular the unrestricted smoothness statement applies at composed or imprimitive points, which are never simply branched. Finite residual automorphisms, such as the deck involution of a composed cover, give Deligne-Mumford inertia with vanishing Lie algebra and do not change the stack dimension. The statement does not assert closedness of the composed or type-(ii) locus, irreducibility or equidimensionality of the balanced Hurwitz scheme, regularity of the coarse space at stacky points, smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient (dimension 2d+2g-5), or any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion.
124:- `FND-0160` [corroborated; {'base': 'reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme S, possibly reducible and non-normal; Grauert/P^2-bundle clauses use reducedness; absolute dimension dim(S_beta)+2 requires S locally of finite type over k', 'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'does_not_cover': ['algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144)', 'nonreduced bases', 'the unmodified identification Irr(Z)=pi_0(Z) for a general finite etale cover of a non-normal base', 'exact type-(ii) geometric image W as a packet-adjudicated input', 'Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, Borel-Moore, or RED-0001 conclusions'], 'ground_field': 'characteristic zero; geometric single-fibre monodromy is taken on U after base change to an algebraic closure of kappa(eta)', 'hypotheses': ['scheme-level (no stack inertia)', '(CE)+(N)+(BAL) on geometric fibres so that U is a nonempty open of a relative P^2-bundle and Z is finite etale of degree 720', 'S_ii closed type-(ii) degeneracy locus when a global block system is used'], 'objects': ['AJ = P_S(pi_*L)', 'U = distinct-support open', 'Z = Ord(U) finite etale right S_6-torsor', 'S_beta reduced irreducible component', 'U_eta generic fibre', 'H_gen', 'H_pi1', 'H_geom'], 'subproblem_id': 'C66-GEO-COMP'}]: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let S be a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme, possibly reducible and non-normal, carrying a balanced (CE)+(N)+(BAL) genus-six degree-four family so that U is the distinct-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle AJ=P_S(pi_*L) and Z->U is the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. 125:- `FND-0161` [corroborated; {'base': 'a single geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; scheme-level only', 'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'does_not_assert': ['any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, Borel-Moore, or RED-0001 conclusion', 'applicability to algebraic stacks with inertia', 'H_alpha on a connected component that meets type (i)', 'non-emptiness of type (ii) beyond FND-0154', 'arithmetic monodromy over a non-algebraically-closed field'], 'hypotheses': ['k algebraically closed of characteristic zero', '(CE) the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution', '(N) O_X(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)', '(BAL) F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)', 'type (ii) in the sense of FND-0153: phi_L is a degree-two cover of a smooth plane cubic'], 'objects': ['|L|^{rs}', 'Ord(|L|^{rs})', 'W=S_2 wr S_3', 'Y^vee', 'reduced branch divisor B of degree ten'], 'subproblem_id': 'C66-GEO-COMP'}]: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After a block-compatible trivialization of the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs})->|L|^{rs}, the geometric monodromy image G=im(pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6) equals this W, not merely a proper subgroup of a conjugate of W. in characteristic zero the wild inertia of a discrete valuation ring is trivial, hence tame/Kummer inertia is cyclic of order two and interchanges exactly those two sheets, so G contains a within-block transposition; 138:- `FND-0177` [corroborated; {'H_S_index_disambiguation': 'fibre degree 2j for j=0,1,2 versus (H-S) j=8 for the first summand', 'case': {'g': 6, 'n': 6}, 'coefficients': 'Q', 'excluded': ['transport of non-Tateness by the FND-0167 injection itself', 'compact-support Leray with nonconstant coefficients on non-product families (FND-0164)', 'RED-0001', 'T_16 of a dimension-17 model over a dimension-15 atlas of Hbar^bal', 'S_6-isotypics other than S_6-invariants of the product model'], 'fibre_degrees': [0, 1, 2], 'ground_field': 'C', 'hypotheses': ['S reduced separated finite-type over C', 'Delta_0 closed in P^2 of dimension at most 1', 'constant or product (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family so A is the trivial P^2-bundle', 'Q-coefficients and mixed Hodge structures'], 'objects': ['Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q)', 'Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q)', 'Gr^W_14 H_c^{14}(S;Q)(-1)', 'Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2)', 'product families U=S x U_0 with U_0=P^2 minus Delta_0']}]: Work over C with Q-coefficients. A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve admits a nonzero global section if and only if it is trivial, so\n\nH^0(C, \u03c9_C \u2297 W_5^\u2228(\u0393)) \u2260 0  \u27fa  O_C(\u0393) \u2245 W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}.\n\n## Identification W_5 \u2245 \u03c9_C^{\u22972}(\u2212D)\n\nRelative duality for \u03b3 gives \u03c9_{C/P^1} \u2245 \u03c9_C \u2297 \u03b3^* O_{P^1}(2). In the Casnati\u2013Ekedahl embedding the tautological restriction satisfies O_{P(E^\u2228)}(1)|_C \u2245 \u03c9_{C/P^1}, hence\n\nO_{P(E^\u2228)}(2)|_C \u2245 \u03c9_C^{\u22972} \u2297 \u03b3^* O_{P^1}(4).\n\nTwisting by \u03b3^* O(\u2212f) produces W_f \u2245 \u03c9_C^{\u22972} \u2297 \u03b3^* O(4\u2212f). Poincar\u00e9 duality for smooth Deligne\u2013Mumford stacks identifies this with the ordinary pure-weight piece\n$$W_{26}H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6};\\mathbb{Q})(21),$$\nwhose untwisted form is $W_{26}H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6})$ of expected type $\\mathbb{Q}(-13)$ (Chow codimension $13$).\n\nThe published CKgP range (THM-0005) only reaches $n\\le c(6)=5$, so $\\mathcal{M}_{6,6}$ lies strictly outside CKgP. The base-case inequality of THM-0004 applies: $n=6\\ge 2$ and $k=16=2g-2+n$, so the open stratum is not absorbed by vanishing ranges and must be treated directly. We prove only the weaker pure-weight Tate statement for this open input, without establishing CKgP, algebraicity of the full Chow ring, or tautological generation.\n\n## Pure-weight vanishing without CKgP\n\n**Step 1 (duality).** By the packet identity FND-0001,\n$$W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6})\\ \\cong\\ W_{26}H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6})(21)$$\nas mixed Hodge structures. In particular, vanishing of the ordinary group $H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6};\\mathbb{Q})$ implies vanishing of the Borel\u2013Moore pure-weight target.\n\n**Step 2 (orbifold/group cohomology).** For $g\\ge 2$, the rational cohomology of the moduli stack agrees with the rational group cohomology of the mapping class group:\n$$H^i(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6};\\mathbb{Q})\\ \\cong\\ H^i(\\mathrm{Mod}_{6,6};\\mathbb{Q}).$$\n(This is the standard identification via contractible Teichm\u00fcller space; it is not among the dependency-closed packet theorems and is recorded as an external input below.)\n\n**Step 3 (Harer virtual cohomological dimension).** Harer's theorem supplies\n$$\\mathrm{vcd}(\\mathrm{Mod}_{g,n})=4g+n-5\\qquad(g\\ge 2).$$\nSpecialising to $(g,n)=(6,6)$ yields\n$$\\mathrm{vcd}(\\mathrm{Mod}_{6,6})=4\\cdot 6+6-5=25.$$\nConsequently $H^i(\\mathrm{Mod}_{6,6};M)=0$ for every $\\mathbb{Q}[\\mathrm{Mod}_{6,6}]$-module $M$ and every $i>25$. Taking trivial coefficients,\n$$H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6};\\mathbb{Q})=0.$$\n\n**Step 4 (pure-weight Tate).** The zero mixed Hodge structure has $W_{26}H^{26}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6})=0$, hence\n$$W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\\mathcal{M}_{6,6})=0.$$\nThe zero object is a direct sum of zero copies of $\\mathbb{Q}(8)$, so the open input is pure Tate of the expected type. No cycle-class surjectivity, no CKgP extension from $n=5$ to $n=6$, and no point-count is used: the pure-weight piece is empty for degree reasons.\n\n## Relation to the compactified statement\n\nBy THM-0003, the boundary long exact sequence realises $H_{16}(\\overline{\\mathcal{M}}_{6,6})$ as an extension of the open pure-weight quotient by a boundary contribution. The vanishing just proved means that, for this single open stratum, the pure-weight quotient contributes nothing. Under the global inductive package of RED-0001 (boundary strata assembled from products of lower $\\overline{\\mathcal{M}}_{g_i,n_i}$, already pure Tate in even degree $16$ by THM-0002 and the inductive hypothesis on smaller dual graphs), the $(6,6)$ open input is therefore discharged.\n\nThis does **not** by itself prove CONJ-0001 for all $(g,n)$: the remaining RED-0001 pairs must still be treated, and the boundary induction is taken from the published reduction rather than re-derived here.\n\n## Why CKgP is avoided\n\nCKgP for $\\mathcal{M}_{6,5}$ (THM-0005) controls pure-weight cohomology of the base of the forgetful map $\\mathcal{M}_{6,6}\\to\\mathcal{M}_{6,5}$, but is not needed once ordinary cohomological vanishing in degree $26$ is available. (N) is the packet's undischarged weak relative-canonical normalization (FND-0105); it is carried as a hypothesis of every clause that uses it and is never asserted.\n\n**Verified dependencies (cited, used inside their stated scope).** ATT-0065 (C66-GEO-Z), dual-confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109: CLM-0065-1, CLM-0065-3, CLM-0065-4, CLM-0065-5, CLM-0065-9 give the filtered CE reduction and the identification of the evaluation-failure scheme with the relative Abel-Jacobi incidence O(Gamma) = W_5 tensor omega^{-1}, scheme-theoretically and under arbitrary base change, on a base carrying six pairwise-disjoint sections. where a packet adjudicated finding (FND-0105, FND-0125, FND-0130, FND-0134, FND-0139, FND-0142) records the same conclusion, it is quoted only as corroboration. No finite computation is used to prove any universal claim; the two explicit families in Section 6 are used only for existence statements, where a single verified instance is a proof.\n\n## 1. The relative-canonical graded module\n\nWrite A_C := omega_{C/P1} = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2), of degree 10+8 = 18. SRC-0004 records deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 18, while (N) gives degree 18 + 4 deg(A); hence deg(A) = 0 and, since Pic(P1) = Z, A = O. Therefore\n\n  O_X(1)|_C = A_C,  W_f = A_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(-f),  W_4 = omega_C^2, W_5 = omega_C^2(-D), L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D),\n\nwith deg W_4 = 20, deg W_5 = 16, deg L = 6 and chi(L) = 1. This is (A0) first part and reproves ATT-0088/CLM-0088-1.\n\nEuler characteristics fix the two ranks and degrees. From gamma_*O_C = O + E^vee and chi(O_C) = -5 one gets 1 + (3 - deg E) = -5, so deg E = 9. Fibrewise monodromy in case (a): the full symmetric group\n\nAssume (BAL), (H3) and case (a). By ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5 the non-reduced locus Delta of |L| is a closed curve and U_C = |L| - Delta is a nonempty dense open of the plane |L|; the ordering scheme Z_C->U_C is a finite etale S_6-torsor, and G_C denotes the image of pi_1(U_C) in S_6 acting on the six points of the universal divisor. By the invariance of the geometric fundamental group under extension of algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, we may take k = C. Write J = {(x,l) : x in C, l in |L|, x in psi_L^*l}, a P1-bundle over C, hence irreducible and smooth of dimension two; J -> |L| is the six-sheeted universal divisor, finite etale exactly over U_C.\n\n**Transitivity.** J is irreducible, hence so is the open subset lying over U_C; therefore G_C is transitive.\n\n**2-transitivity.** Let J_2 -> U_C be the cover of ordered pairs of distinct points of the divisor, finite etale of degree 30 over the smooth surface U_C, hence smooth of pure dimension two. Consider the locally closed subset of J_2 where psi_L(x_1) is not equal to psi_L(x_2). On it the projection (x_1,x_2,l) -> (x_1,x_2) is injective, because l is then the unique line through the two distinct image points; so this subset is isomorphic to an open subset of C x C and is irreducible, and it is nonempty (choose a general line). Its complement in J_2 lies over the finitely many pairs of points of C with the same image (psi_L is birational, so those are finitely many), and hence has dimension at most one. A pure two-dimensional scheme with an irreducible dense open subset is irreducible, so J_2 is irreducible and G_C is 2-transitive; in particular G_C is primitive.\n\n**A transposition.** In characteristic zero psi_L is generically immersive, so let q run over the dense open of C where the differential is nonzero and let l_q be the tangent line of the branch at psi_L(q). For general q: the contact order at q is exactly two (flexes are finite because X' is not a line); l_q is tangent at no other point (by reflexivity the conormal map is birational onto the dual curve X'^*, so multiply tangent lines are finite in number); l_q passes through none of the finitely many points where psi_L fails to be immersive or is not injective (for each such point x_0, the tangent lines through x_0 correspond to finitely many q); and l_q is a general, hence smooth, point of the reduced irreducible dual curve X'^*, and lies on no other component of Delta (the remaining components are the finitely many lines dual to the non-immersive points). Thus psi_L^*l_q = 2q + p_1 + ... + p_4 with five distinct points, Delta is smooth at l_q, and near l_q the cover J -> |L| is the disjoint union of four unbranched sheets and a degree-two map of smooth surfaces branched exactly along the smooth Delta, which is locally the standard double cover; the meridian of Delta at l_q therefore acts as a single transposition, which lies in G_C.\n\nBy Jordan's theorem a primitive subgroup of S_6 containing a transposition is S_6, so G_C = S_6. (This agrees with, and reproves in the case at hand, the classical uniform position theorem for a nondegenerate irreducible plane curve.) A finite etale S_6-torsor with full monodromy is connected; Z_C is smooth of dimension two over k, hence normal, so Z_C is irreducible of dimension two. This proves the first half of (A4).\n\n## 8. Stabilizers, pencil recovery and faithfulness\n\n**(A5) fibrewise.** Assume (BAL) and (H3), and let Gamma be effective with O_C(Gamma) = L. Then omega_C(-Gamma) = omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D), whose complete linear system is the base-point-free pencil |D| of degree four defining gamma (h^0(D) = 2 by Section 2, and |D| is base-point-free because it is the pencil of fibres of gamma). Hence gamma is canonically reconstructed from the pair (C,Gamma) as the morphism attached to |omega_C(-Gamma)|, up to a unique automorphism of P1. If sigma in Aut(C) satisfies sigma(Gamma) = Gamma then sigma preserves omega_C(-Gamma), hence permutes |omega_C(-Gamma)| = |D|, hence there is a unique tau in Aut(P1) with gamma o sigma = tau o gamma. Therefore Aut(C,Gamma) = Aut(C,gamma,Gamma). This proves the equality rather than transporting a PGL_2 argument for one group to the other, which is exactly what the recorded stabilizer constraint forbids: the two groups are here shown to coincide, and the identification is what licenses using either.\n\n**Nontrivial inertia does occur.** In case (b), every member of |L| is phi^*(a member of |N'|) and is therefore invariant under the bielliptic involution sigma, so sigma lies in Aut(C,Gamma) for every Gamma in |L|; on a reduced Gamma it acts as a product of three disjoint transpositions (a reduced Gamma misses the ramification divisor), so it does not fix any ordered point. For ordered points the situation is different, and nontrivial stabilizers exist inside the balanced locus. Let C'' be a general genus-two curve with hyperelliptic class A' = omega_{C''}, let delta in Pic^3(C'') be general (so delta - A' is not effective, hence |delta| is base-point-free of degree three), let B be a general reduced member of |delta^2| (degree six), let phi:C->C'' be the double cover branched along B, and let gamma = phi_{|A'|} o phi have degree four. Exact theorem and outcome\n\n**Exact theorem.** *The exact group `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)`, equivalently `W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)`, is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.*\n\n**Outcome: the theorem is true.** We prove the sharp form\n\n> `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0`,\n\nand `0` is the direct sum of the empty family of copies of `Q(8)`. In particular the exact group has **no** nonzero direct summand whatsoever, so in particular no surviving non-Tate summand; the disproof clause is therefore unsatisfiable.\n\n**Reading of the phrase 'is a direct sum of Q(8)'.** A Q-mixed Hodge structure `V` *is a direct sum of Q(8)* means `V` is isomorphic to `\u2295_{i\u2208I} Q(8)` for some index set `I`. The case `I = \u2205` gives `V = 0`. This is the standard reading, and it is exactly the reading forced by the packet's own dichotomy: the packet states that the theorem is falsified precisely by exhibiting *a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group*. The zero object has no nonzero summand, hence no non-Tate summand, hence lies on the Tate side of the packet's dichotomy. (Nothing in the packet asserts that the exact group is nonzero: `FND-0005` asserts nonemptiness of a geometric locus `Z \u2282 M_{6,6}`, which is a statement about a codimension-4 subvariety and carries no implication about the cohomology of `M_{6,6}` in degree 26; see \u00a76.3.)\n\nThroughout, all (co)homology has `Q`-coefficients; `Q(m)` is the Tate Hodge structure of weight `-2m`; `M_{g,n}` is the moduli stack of smooth `n`-pointed genus-`g` curves with **ordered** distinct markings, a smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack over `C` of pure dimension `d = 3g-3+n`; `W_\\bullet` is Deligne's weight filtration.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Numerical setup\n\nFor `(g,n) = (6,6)`:\n\n- `d := dim_C M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 18-3+6 = 21`.\n- `2d-16 = 42-16 = 26`.\n- `vcd(M_{6,6}) = 4g-4+n = 24-4+6 = 26`.\n- Tate-twist bookkeeping: `Q(-13)(21) = Q(-13+21) = Q(8)`.\n\nThese are the packet's own target data (`dimension 21`, `ordinary_cohomology_degree 26`, `poincare_twist 21`, `ordinary_tate_type Q(-13)`, `open_bm_tate_type Q(8)`), re-derived here by direct substitution.\n\n**The decisive numerical coincidence.** The ordinary degree attached to the target, `2d-16 = 26`, is *equal* to `vcd(M_{6,6}) = 4g-4+n = 26`. The packet's `FND-0035` records exactly this and correctly observes that vanishing *strictly above* the virtual cohomological dimension therefore proves nothing here. The present proof does **not** use vanishing strictly above vcd. It uses vanishing **exactly at** vcd, which is a strictly deeper and logically independent statement (it fails, for instance, for `g = 1`: `vcd(M_{1,11}) = 11` and `H^{11}(M_{1,11};Q) \u2260 0`). See \u00a77 for the audit of this point against the packet's blocked routes.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Step 1: Poincar\u00e9 duality for `M_{6,6}` as an identification of mixed Hodge structures\n\nThis step re-derives, in the exact case at hand and without appeal to the adjudicated finding, the identification recorded as `FND-0001`.\n\n**Lemma 2.1 (global quotient presentation by a smooth quasi-projective variety).** Fix an integer `l \u2265 3`. Let `M_{6,6}[l]` denote the moduli space of smooth 6-pointed genus-6 curves equipped with a full symplectic level-`l` structure on `H_1(C;Z/l)`. Then `M_{6,6}[l]` is a smooth quasi-projective complex variety of dimension 21, the forgetful morphism `M_{6,6}[l] \u2192 M_{6,6}` is finite \u00e9tale and Galois with deck group `G := Sp(12, Z/l)`, and `M_{6,6} \u2245 [ M_{6,6}[l] / G ]`.\n\n*Proof.* By Serre's lemma, a nontrivial automorphism of a smooth projective curve of genus `g \u2265 1` acts nontrivially on `H_1(C;Z/l)` for `l \u2265 3`. Hence a 6-pointed genus-6 curve with level-`l` structure has no nontrivial automorphisms, so the level-`l` moduli stack is representable by a scheme; it is smooth because `M_{6,6}` is smooth and the level cover is \u00e9tale, and quasi-projective by standard GIT/Hilbert-scheme constructions of level moduli. The level-`l` structures on a fixed curve form a torsor under `Sp(12,Z/l)`, whence the finite \u00e9tale Galois property and the quotient presentation. \u220e\n\n**Lemma 2.2 (invariants).** For every `k`, `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^k(M_{6,6}[l];Q)^{G}` and `H^{BM}_k(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{BM}_k(M_{6,6}[l];Q)^{G}`, both as mixed Hodge structures.\n\n*Proof.* For a finite group `G` acting on a variety `Y`, the (co)homology of the quotient stack `[Y/G]` with `Q`-coefficients is the `G`-invariant part of that of `Y`; this is the standard Leray/descent computation for the finite \u00e9tale Galois cover `Y \u2192 [Y/G]`, valid with `Q`-coefficients because `|G|` is invertible. The `G`-action is by algebraic automorphisms, hence acts by morphisms of mixed Hodge structures, and taking `G`-invariants is an exact functor on `Q`-mixed Hodge structures (it is a direct summand cut out by the idempotent `|G|^{-1} \u03a3_{g\u2208G} g`), so it commutes with `W_\\bullet` and preserves the mixed Hodge structure. \u220e\n\n**Lemma 2.3 (Poincar\u00e9 duality).** `H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)` as mixed Hodge structures, and consequently\n\n`W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 ( W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) )(21)`.\n\n*Proof.* Let `Y := M_{6,6}[l]`, a smooth complex variety of pure dimension `d = 21`. Poincar\u00e9 duality for a smooth complex variety gives a natural isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures `H^{BM}_k(Y;Q) \u2245 H^{2d-k}(Y;Q)(d)` (Deligne; the duality between Borel-Moore homology and cohomology of a smooth oriented manifold, upgraded to mixed Hodge structures by the standard functoriality of Deligne's construction). It is natural, hence `G`-equivariant. Taking `G`-invariants and applying Lemma 2.2 on both sides gives `H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)`. Since the weight filtration is functorial and `V \u21a6 V(21)` shifts weights by `-42`, the weight-`(-16)` part on the left corresponds to the weight-`(-16+42) = 26` part on the right, giving the displayed consequence. \u220e\n\nLemma 2.3 is precisely the packet's exact-target identification `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21)`, now proved rather than assumed. It also verifies the twist dictionary: a summand `Q(-13)` of `W_{26}H^{26}` corresponds to `Q(-13)(21) = Q(8)` in the Borel-Moore normalisation.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Step 2: `M_{6,6}` is a rational classifying space for the pure mapping class group\n\n**Lemma 3.1.** For every `k` there is an isomorphism of `Q`-vector spaces `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^k(Mod_{6,6};Q)`, where `Mod_{6,6}` is the pure mapping class group of a genus-6 orientable surface with 6 punctures (orientation-preserving mapping classes fixing each puncture).\n\n*Proof.* The Teichm\u00fcller space `T_{6,6}` is a contractible complex manifold of complex dimension 21, `Mod_{6,6}` acts on it properly discontinuously with finite stabilisers, and the analytification of the stack `M_{6,6}` is the quotient orbifold `[T_{6,6}/Mod_{6,6}]`. For a group `\u0393` acting properly discontinuously with finite stabilisers on a contractible space `X`, the natural map `H^*(\u0393;Q) \u2192 H^*(X/\u0393;Q)` is an isomorphism (the Borel construction `X \u00d7_\u0393 E\u0393 \u2192 X/\u0393` has `Q`-acyclic fibres `B\u0393_x` for finite `\u0393_x`, and `X \u00d7_\u0393 E\u0393 \u2243 B\u0393` since `X` is contractible). Finally the comparison `H^*(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^*(M_{6,6}^{an};Q)` holds for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack `M_{6,6}`. \u220e\n\n(Only the underlying `Q`-vector-space statement is used below; no Hodge-theoretic content is claimed for Lemma 3.1.)\n\n---\n\n## 4. Step 3: virtual cohomological dimension\n\n**Theorem 4.1 (Harer).** For `g \u2265 1` and `n \u2265 1`, `Mod_{g,n}` is a virtual duality group of dimension `4g-4+n`; in particular `vcd(Mod_{g,n}) = 4g-4+n` and `H^k(Mod_{g,n};Q) = 0` for `k > 4g-4+n`. (For `g \u2265 2`, `n = 0`, the value is `4g-5`.)\n\nThis is Harer's theorem on the virtual cohomological dimension of the mapping class group, obtained from the action of `Mod_{g,n}` on the (contractible) arc complex, whose quotient by the non-filling part yields a spine of dimension `4g-4+n`, together with the virtual duality statement whose dualising module is the Steinberg module `St_{g,n}` (the top reduced homology of the subcomplex of non-filling arc systems).\n\n**Corollary 4.2.** `vcd(Mod_{6,6}) = 4\u00b76-4+6 = 26`, so `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) = 0` for `k > 26`, and `26` is the top degree in which `H^*(M_{6,6};Q)` can be nonzero.\n\nBecause the exact target lives in degree `26 = vcd`, Corollary 4.2 alone is inert \u2014 this is precisely the content of `FND-0035`. Step 4 supplies the extra input.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Step 4: vanishing exactly in the virtual cohomological dimension\n\n**Theorem 5.1 (Church-Farb-Putman).** Let `g \u2265 2`. Then\n\n- `H^{4g-4+n}(Mod_{g,n};Q) = 0` for every `n \u2265 1`, and\n- `H^{4g-5}(Mod_{g};Q) = 0`.\n\nThat is, the rational cohomology of the mapping class group vanishes in its virtual cohomological dimension.\n\n*Source and status.* T. Church, B. Farb, A. Putman, *The rational cohomology of the mapping class group vanishes in its virtual cohomological dimension*, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN **2012**, no. 21, 5025-5030. (The unpunctured case `n = 0` was obtained independently by Morita-Sakasai-Suzuki.) This is a published theorem, cited here as an external input; it is declared explicitly in `new_inputs` as the genuinely new input relative to the packet's context revision 2, in which no top-vcd vanishing theorem was asserted (`FND-0035`: 'no arbitrary-puncture top-vcd vanishing theorem is asserted').\n\n*Structure of the input, for auditability.* By Harer's virtual duality (Theorem 4.1) with dualising module the Steinberg module `St_{g,n}`, one has `H^{vcd}(Mod_{g,n};Q) \u2245 H_0(Mod_{g,n}; St_{g,n} \u2297 Q) = (St_{g,n} \u2297 Q)_{Mod_{g,n}}`, the module of coinvariants. Theorem 5.1 is the statement that these rational coinvariants vanish; the proof proceeds by exhibiting a generating set of `St_{g,n}` consisting of classes each of which is negated by some element of the mapping class group, so that each generator dies in the rational coinvariants.\n\n*Sharpness / non-triviality of the hypothesis `g \u2265 2`.* The hypothesis is essential and marks the theorem as strictly stronger than any 'degree exceeds vcd' vanishing: for `g = 1` one has `vcd(Mod_{1,11}) = 4\u00b71-4+11 = 11` and `H^{11}(M_{1,11};Q) \u2260 0` (it carries the weight-11, non-Tate motive attached to the cusp form of weight 12). Thus the top-degree vanishing is a genuine theorem about genus at least two and not a formal consequence of the dimension bound.\n\n**Corollary 5.2.** `H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0`.\n\n*Proof.* Apply Theorem 5.1 with `g = 6 \u2265 2` and `n = 6 \u2265 1`: `4g-4+n = 26`, so `H^{26}(Mod_{6,6};Q) = 0`. By Lemma 3.1, `H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{26}(Mod_{6,6};Q) = 0`. \u220e\n\n---\n\n## 6. Step 5: conclusion, and consistency with the packet\n\n### 6.1 The exact group\n\n**Theorem 6.1.** `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0`. Equivalently, `W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) = 0`. In particular the exact group is the direct sum `\u2295_{i\u2208\u2205} Q(8)` of the empty family of copies of `Q(8)`, and it possesses no nonzero direct summand; a fortiori it possesses no surviving non-Tate summand.\n\n*Proof.* By Corollary 5.2, `H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0`. Every subquotient of the zero vector space is zero, so `W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0` and hence `W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) = 0`. By Lemma 2.3, `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 (W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q))(21) = 0`. (Alternatively and even more directly: by Lemma 2.3 the whole group `H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)` vanishes, hence so does any weight-graded piece of it.)\n\nA direct sum decomposition `0 = \u2295_{i\u2208I} V_i` in the abelian category of `Q`-mixed Hodge structures forces `V_i = 0` for all `i`; therefore the exact group has no nonzero summand of any kind, Tate or non-Tate. Taking `I = \u2205` and `V_i = Q(8)` exhibits the exact group as a direct sum of copies of `Q(8)`, which is the assertion of the exact theorem. \u220e\n\nThis resolves the exact target `RED-0001` for `(g,n) = (6,6)` in the affirmative, i.e. as a **proof**, not a disproof: the disproof clause requires exhibiting a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group, and Theorem 6.1 shows no such summand can exist.\n\n### 6.2 Consistency with `FND-0036` (and a corollary)\n\n`FND-0036` records that for the forgetful map `p : M_{6,6} \u2192 M_{6,5}` the term `H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q)` vanishes (since `26 > 25 = vcd(M_{6,5}) = 4\u00b76-4+5`) and that, fibre cohomology being concentrated in `q = 0,1`, no Leray differential enters or leaves total degree 26. Our Corollary 5.2 is therefore *equivalent*, along this route, to `H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1p_*Q) = 0`, which is what Theorem 5.1 delivers after transport. There is no conflict: `FND-0036` is a reduction, and Theorem 5.1 is the input that closes it. The degree arithmetic of `SRC-0004` Lemma 10.6 is correct and we reproduce it: `deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f`, so for `g = 6`, `deg(W_5) = 4\u00b76+12-20 = 16` and `deg(W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{-1}) = 16-(2\u00b76-2) = 6`; and `deg(\u03c9_C \u2297 W_f^\u2228(\u0393)) = 4f+n-2g-14` equals `-4` for `f = 4` and `0` for `f = 5` when `n = 6, g = 6`. In particular `FND-0005` (nonemptiness of `Z`) is entirely compatible with our result.\n\nThe key point is that **nonemptiness of a positive-codimension locus `Z \u2282 M_{6,6}` implies nothing about `H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)`**. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0025.json:170:  "summary": "Proof. The exact target sits in ordinary cohomological degree 26, which is exactly the virtual cohomological dimension 4g-4+n = 26 of M_{6,6}. The whole group H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) vanishes: M_{6,6} is a rational classifying space for the pure mapping class group Mod_{6,6}, Harer's virtual duality gives vcd(Mod_{6,6}) = 26, and the Church-Farb-Putman top-degree vanishing theorem (g >= 2, n >= 1) gives H^{4g-4+n}(Mod_{g,n};Q) = 0. Poincare duality on the smooth 21-dimensional Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6} (realised via a level-l cover and finite-group invariants, so that the identification is one of mixed Hodge structures) transports this to H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) = 0. Hence W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0, which is the direct sum of the empty family of copies of Q(8); in particular no summand at all, and a fortiori no non-Tate summand, survives in the exact group. The tetragonal Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure apparatus of the packet is not needed and is shown to be consistent with (not contradicted by) this outcome. The proof does not use vanishing strictly above the virtual cohomological dimension; it uses vanishing exactly at the virtual cohomological dimension, which is declared as new input.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0121.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, interface, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) after base change to C. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of dimension d = 21. The target T := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q) is identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincare duality (FND-0001; established working-context fact). Thus T is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight -16. Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m and W_m are exact.\n\nThe C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum is the verified attempt ATT-0120, dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170, and recorded as FND-0180. Its claims CLM-0120-1 through CLM-0120-7 are used exactly as confirmed. In particular T_Z is not the compactly supported cohomology of a standalone model Z, and there is no map from H_c^{16}(Z) to T.\n\nNo blocked route is used: no vcd-only vanishing, no undecorated CGP top-weight graph complex, no point count, and no forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. No Gysin map, regular immersion, lci hypothesis, closed embedding of Z, or support-exhaustion T_Z = T is assumed (FND-0052, FND-0168(5), ATT-0120 Section 8). Rational irreducibility of S_6-representations is not used to create Tate structure (working-context constraint; FND-0053, FND-0054).\n\n## 1. The named subquotient T_Z (imported from ATT-0120)\n\nBy ATT-0120/CLM-0120-1, each ordered reduced-support scheme Z_beta of ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 carries a tautological smooth genus-six curve with six pairwise-disjoint sections, hence a classifying morphism f_beta: Z_beta -> X by the universal property of X. By CLM-0120-2, the union of geometric images is constructible and atlas-independent; its Zariski closure is the underlying space of a unique reduced closed substack Y of X. By CLM-0120-3, U_Y := X minus Y is smooth of dimension 21, restriction r: H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, both groups have weights at least 26, and Poincare duality supplies r_T: T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21). By CLM-0120-4,\n\nT_Z := K_Z := ker(r_T),\n\nwith phi the inclusion K_Z -> T. Thus T_Z is a subobject of T, hence a specified subquotient, of Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, and Poincare twist (21). Exactness of Gr^W_{26} identifies T_Z with the classes in T that vanish on U_Y, equivalently with the image of the degree-26 supports map in the sense of FND-0168(3a) (REV-0169, REV-0170: the loose parenthetical equating T_Z with the supports group itself is not used; only the kernel/image form is used). By CLM-0120-5 the accounting is one-sided: every class supported on a closed subset of Y lies in T_Z, and extra support inflates rather than omits. By CLM-0120-6 the datum is atlas-independent, including passage to etale atlases of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2]. By CLM-0120-7 no Tate type is asserted by the interface.\n\nThis is the unique canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient named by the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum. Complementary terms in im(r_T) are excluded from T_Z by definition and are not assembled here.\n\n## 2. Purity of T_Z\n\nT is pure of weight -16. The kernel of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures out of a pure object is a subobject, hence itself pure of weight -16 and polarizable. Therefore T_Z is a pure polarizable rational Hodge structure of weight -16. Semisimplicity of that abelian category (established working-context fact) implies that T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if every Hodge type of T_Z is (-8,-8). This tautology is recorded only to fix the type dictionary; it is not a geometric input.\n\n## 3. Dimension of Y\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-2, H^bal is smooth of pure dimension 18. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7, Hbar^bal is smooth of pure dimension 15, and the M_{6,6}-valued point attached to (C, Gamma) is PGL_2-invariant. ATT-0120/CLM-0120-6 therefore realises the same closed substack Y from any etale atlas of Hbar^bal.\n\nLet S be a connected component of a smooth finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal. Then S is reduced of dimension 15. Pulling back the universal balanced family, ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 (Grauert over a reduced base; h^0(L)=3 identically) supplies a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle AJ, a reduced-support open U of pure relative dimension two, and a finite etale S_6-torsor Z = Ord(U) of the same dimension. Hence dim Z = 15+2 = 17. The classifying morphism f: Z -> X is of finite type, so the constructible geometric image has dimension at most 17, and its Zariski closure Y satisfies dim Y <= 17.\n\n(The coarser bound dim Y <= 20 of FND-0181, from the H^bal-level source of dimension 18+2, is compatible and not used. Equality dim Y = 17 is not claimed.)\n\nBy FND-0181, Y is a proper closed substack of the 21-dimensional stack X, so U_Y is a nonempty dense open and T_Z is a genuine proper-support kernel rather than an unnoticed exhaustion T_Z = T.\n\n## 4. Degree-16 vanishing on sources of dimension less than 8\n\nLet W be a separated scheme of finite type over C of dimension delta. Then H_c^k(W; Q) = 0 for k > 2 delta. In particular, if delta < 8 then H_c^{16}(W; Q) = 0, and dually H^{BM}_{16}(W; Q) = 0. This is the ordinary vanishing of compactly supported cohomology above twice the dimension; no Gysin map and no regularity hypothesis appear.\n\nConsequently, if Y' is any closed substack of X admitting a finite-type scheme atlas of dimension less than 8, the image of W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Y'; Q) in T vanishes. By FND-0168(3a) as applied in ATT-0120/REV-0169 (Poincare duality on the smooth pair intertwines Borel-Moore corestriction with ordinary open restriction), the kernel-form term attached to Y' is zero. By FND-0182 this kernel-form term injects into T_Z, so Y' contributes nothing to T_Z.\n\n## 5. Constant and product clause-(E) models have zero image in T_Z\n\nLet (C_0, gamma_0) be a geometric type-(i) fibre of H^bal (nonempty by ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and FND-0154). Let Z_0 be the ordered reduced-support fibre over this point: an open in a P^2, of dimension 2, with classifying morphism f_0: Z_0 -> X whose geometric image Im_0 lies in a single Abel-Jacobi P^2 and therefore satisfies dim Im_0 <= 2. Let Y_0 be the reduced closure of Im_0; then dim Y_0 <= 2 < 8.\n\nLet B be any reduced separated finite-type C-scheme, and let Z_B = B x Z_0 be the constant clause-(E) family (the FND-0176/FND-0178 setup). The classifying morphism f_B: Z_B -> X is f_0 composed with projection pr: B x Z_0 -> Z_0, because the marked curve is constant in the B-direction. Hence the geometric image of f_B equals Im_0, and the closed support of f_B is contained in Y_0.\n\nCompact-support pushforward therefore factors as f_{B,!} = f_{0,!} o pr_!. For a Kunneth summand H_c^a(B) tensor H_c^b(Z_0) with a+b = 16, the fibre-integration pr_! is the pairing of H_c^a(B) against H_c^{a-2 dim B} of a point. In the FND-0178 witness one has B of dimension 8 and the surviving class in H_c^{12}(B) tensor H_c^4(U_0), so a = 12 < 16 = 2 dim B, and pr_! of that summand is zero. Independently of Kunneth, Section 4 already gives W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Y_0) = 0, so every class supported on Y_0 has zero image in T. Therefore f_{B,!} vanishes on H_c^{16}(Z_B), and the FND-0178 Hodge type (10,6) class does not survive in T_Z.\n\nThis is the exact exclusion in the theorem: non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof. For every constant or product clause-(E) model the target image in T is proved zero, not merely unproved.\n\nThe same vanishing applies to any source whose classifying image has dimension less than 8.\n\n## 6. What would be needed to conclude Tate type, and what is not available\n\nT_Z is the image of W_{26} of the supports map H^{26}_Y(X; Q) -> H^{26}(X; Q), twisted by (21). A Gysin identification of that supports group with a cohomological degree shift of Y would require a closed regular embedding of Y (or a stratification by regularly embedded strata) of known codimension, which FND-0052 and FND-0168(5) record as undischarged and which ATT-0120 explicitly does not supply. The working-context constraint forbids inferring lci, regularity, purity, or Gysin from expected determinantal codimension or from a 17-dimensional constructible image.\n\nA map H_c^{16}(Z) -> T would likewise require proper pushforward along a compactification of f or a Gysin map, neither of which is constructed. REV-0169 records this as a limit on usefulness of the interface, not a defect in its naming of T_Z: the interface transmits no CE-geometric cohomology that can be tested for Tate type inside T.\n\nFND-0167 reduces T_16(Z) to hypotheses (H-S) and (H-C) on a named base, and FND-0178 shows those hypotheses fail for some allowed bases. That computation concerns standalone Z and, by Section 5, does not migrate into T_Z.\n\nThus the Hodge type of the named kernel T_Z is not determined by the available inputs. In particular the statement that T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) is not proved, and no non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z is exhibited.\n\n## 7. Blocked routes\n\n- vcd-only-vanishing: unused. The argument never invokes vcd(M_{6,5}) or vanishing above virtual cohomological dimension.\n- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: unused. No graph complex, arc complex, or depth-zero weight spectral sequence is opened.\n- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: unused. No finite field count is used.\n- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: unused. The forgetful map X -> M_{6,5} is not used, and no local system is declared Tate by renaming.\n\nThe complementary target terms im(r_T) are not assembled, as the theorem requires.\n",

Position relative to the working context\n\nThe primary working-context file lists as **frontier obligations** (open gaps, not inputs):\n\n1. \"An explicit scheme-theoretic proof that J subset I_e on Pic^0 over arbitrary (possibly nonreduced) locally Noetherian bases, via restriction of Phi along e and vanishing of Fit_0(coker(e^* Phi))=Fit_0(R^1 pi_* omega_{C/S}).\"\n2. \"Independent scheme-structure comparison establishing Z_CE=a_N^{-1}(e(S)) as closed subschemes (both inclusions of Fitting ideal versus section ideal), not merely fibrewise geometric-point equality.\"\n3. \"Justification that the balanced CE bundle ... either splits as W_4 oplus W_5 or that the Fitting reduction is rewritten in filtered form so that the split hypothesis is not required.\"\n4. \"Smooth-local/atlas descent extending the scheme-base CE/Abel-Jacobi identification to the corresponding algebraic stack.\"\n\nThe extended working-context file records the corresponding statements only as **candidate ideas requiring proof** (WORKING-EXT lines 69-71), and there under the *stronger* hypotheses of a characteristic-zero base and a **split** bundle W = W_4 oplus W_5. Packet findings FND-0096, FND-0097 and FND-0099 are consistent with the result and are cited below only for orientation; **every step used in the proof is proved here from standard inputs**, so no corroborated-finding sketch is load-bearing.\n\n### 1. Standard inputs used (textbook, not campaign-specific)\n\n- **(S1)** Grothendieck representability of the relative Picard functor. Since n >= 1, O_C(Gamma) is pi-ample, so pi is projective; with geometrically integral fibres and the section x_1, Pic_{C/B} is representable by a separated B-scheme locally of finite type, Pic^0_{C/B} is open and closed in it, smooth and proper over B of relative dimension g with identity section e, and a Poincare bundle Poin exists on C x_B Pic_{C/B}, unique up to twist by an invertible sheaf pulled back from Pic. If moreover R^1 f_*F = 0 for F flat over the base, then f_*F is locally free and commutes with arbitrary base change.\n- **(S4)** Relative duality trace isomorphism R^1 pi_* omega_{C/B} = O_B for a smooth proper curve fibration with geometrically connected fibres.\n- **(S5)** Serre duality over a field kappa: for C smooth proper geometrically connected over kappa, the cup pairing H^0(omega) x H^1(O) -> H^1(omega) = kappa is perfect, and H^0(O_C) = kappa.\n- **(S6)** Fitting formalism. Step 1: ranks, and the cokernel of the universal evaluation\n\nWork in the setting (Sigma), (F), (D1), (D2) of the theorem.\n\nFrom (D1), d_4 > 2g-2+n > 2g-2; from (D2), d_5 = 2g-2+n > 2g-2 since n >= 1. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0034.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Argument\n\n### 0. Notation and target dictionary\nLet M_{g,n} denote the moduli stack of smooth n-pointed genus-g curves over C, and \\overline{M}_{g,n} its Deligne\u2013Mumford compactification. Write d_{g,n}=3g-3+n. All cohomology is singular cohomology with Q coefficients, equipped with its mixed Hodge structure. Tate twists are denoted Q(m); pure Hodge\u2013Tate summands of weight \u22122m are written Q(m) when the sign convention matches the packet (so Q(\u221213) has weight 26).\n\n### 1. Poincar\u00e9 duality and the exact target\nThe stack M_{6,6} is smooth of pure complex dimension d=3\u00b76\u22123+6=21. Poincar\u00e9 duality for smooth Deligne\u2013Mumford stacks of pure dimension d identifies Borel\u2013Moore homology with ordinary cohomology by\nH^{BM}_k(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{2d\u2212k}(M_{6,6};Q)(d)\nas mixed Hodge structures. Specialising to k=16 yields\nH^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21).\nThe weight filtration is compatible, so\nW_{\u221216}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21).\n(The packet adjudicated finding FND-0001 records the same identification for all pairs with d=3g\u22123+n.) Tate-twist arithmetic gives Q(\u221213)(21)=Q(8). Consequently it is equivalent to prove\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 \u2295 Q(\u221213)\n(as mixed Hodge structures). The empty direct sum is allowed and is pure of the asserted type.\n\n### 2. Deligne edge image\nLet j:M_{6,6}\u21aa\\overline{M}_{6,6} be the open immersion into the smooth proper compactification, with boundary D=\\overline{M}_{6,6}\\setminus M_{6,6}. Deligne\u2019s weight filtration on the cohomology of a smooth variety (or DM stack) realises the lowest-weight graded piece as an edge image: for every k,\nW_k H^k(M_{6,6};Q) = im( j^* : H^k(\\overline{M}_{6,6};Q) \u2192 H^k(M_{6,6};Q) ).\nIn particular,\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = im( H^{26}(\\overline{M}_{6,6};Q) \u2192 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) ).\nThe source H^{26}(\\overline{M}_{6,6}) is pure of weight 26. The image is therefore pure of weight 26; it remains only to prove it is of Hodge\u2013Tate type (13,13), i.e., a direct sum of copies of Q(\u221213).\n\n### 3. Forgetful Leray identification\nLet p:M_{6,6}\u2192M_{6,5} be the morphism forgetting the last marked point. The fibre is a smooth genus-6 curve minus five marked points, so the only nonzero higher direct images are R^0 p_*Q \u2245 Q and R^1 p_*Q. Virtual cohomological dimension gives vcd(M_{6,5})=4\u00b76\u22124+5=25, so H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q)=0. The Leray spectral sequence for p therefore has only two rows in total degree 26, and no differential can enter or leave that total degree (packet FND-0036). Degeneration yields a canonical isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures\nH^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* Q),\nand likewise on every weight piece, in particular on W_{26}.\n\n### 4. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0130.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Conventions, imported datum, and standard inputs\n\nWork over C with Q-coefficients. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of pure dimension d = 3*6-3+6 = 21 (established working-context fact). By Poincare duality (established fact; packet FND-0001) the target\n\n  T := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21). Since X is smooth, H^{26}(X; Q) has weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26 and T is pure polarizable of weight -16. The arithmetic is 2*21-16 = 26 and 26-2*21 = -16.\n\nFrom the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE attempt ATT-0120, dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170, import only the following. Y is an atlas-independent reduced closed substack of X (CLM-0120-2, CLM-0120-6). U_Y := X minus Y is a smooth open of dimension 21; restriction r : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, both sides have weights at least 26, and r_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) is the induced map of pure weight -16 Hodge structures (CLM-0120-3). T_Z := K_Z := ker(r_T) is a subobject of T, with phi the inclusion (CLM-0120-4). Every class in T supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y lies in T_Z (CLM-0120-5). The datum uses no Tate assertion, no Gysin map, no closed embedding of Z, and no support-exhaustion (CLM-0120-7). Nothing below uses a dimension, purity, irreducibility, regular-immersion, or lci property of Y, nor any map from the cohomology of Z to T.\n\nStandard inputs, already in the register of ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3 as confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170.\n\n(S1) Mixed Hodge structures on ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, functorial for open immersions. For such a stack V, H^m(V; Q) has weights at least m.\n\n(S2) Purity for a smooth pair. If V is a smooth separated finite-type DM stack over C of pure dimension D and S is a smooth closed substack of V of pure codimension c, then there is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures\n\n  ... -> H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) -> H^m(V; Q) -> H^m(V minus S; Q) -> ...\n\nobtained from the purity isomorphism H^m_S(V; Q) isomorphic to H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) together with localization for the closed-open pair (S, V minus S). Equivalently, after passage to an etale scheme atlas of the smooth pair, this is the classical purity sequence for a closed immersion of smooth schemes of codimension equal to the dimension difference, followed by Q-descent. This is precisely the route the working-context lci constraint itself prescribes (a closed immersion between objects both smooth over the base). It is not a Gysin map, fundamental class, regular immersion, or codimension shift for Y, nor for any model of Z inside X: every pair used below is (X minus Y^{(j+1)}, S_j) with S_j smooth and closed in the smooth ambient by construction of the chain.\n\n(S3) Coarse comparison for ordinary Q-cohomology. If S is a separated finite-type DM stack over C with finite inertia and coarse space c : S -> S^c, then R c_* Q = Q, because geometric fibres are classifying stacks of finite groups, whose Q-cohomology vanishes in positive degree. Hence H^*(S; Q) = H^*(S^c; Q). This is used only to import Artin vanishing; no integral or moduli-theoretic coarse-space statement is made.\n\n(S4) Artin vanishing. For an affine complex variety A of dimension n, H^k(A; Q) = 0 for k > n (Andreotti-Frankel when A is smooth; Hamm/Karcjauskas in the possibly singular affine case).\n\n(S5) Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for W, so W_m and Gr^W_m are exact functors.\n\n(S6) The category of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight is semisimple abelian. Every subobject or quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is again a finite direct sum of Q(8) (established working-context fact; packet FND-0033 at this corner).\n\nNo virtual cohomological dimension, graph complex, point count, or forgetful map X -> M_{6,5} is used.\n\n## 1. Existence of an admissible chain, with no dimension bound for Y\n\nLemma 1. Let Y be a reduced closed substack of X. There exist an integer N >= 0 and reduced closed substacks\n\n  Y = Y^{(0)} superset Y^{(1)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty\n\nsuch that, writing S_j := Y^{(j)} minus Y^{(j+1)} and n_j := dim Y^{(j)}, each S_j is smooth of pure dimension n_j, has affine coarse space, and is closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)}, and n_0 > n_1 > ... > n_{N-1} >= 0 whenever N >= 1.\n\nProof. If Y is empty, take N = 0. Now suppose Y^{(j)} is a nonempty reduced closed substack of X, of dimension d_j. Let C_1, ..., C_r be its irreducible components of dimension d_j. In characteristic zero the singular locus of a reduced finite-type DM stack is a proper closed substack. Set\n\n  O := Y^{(j)} minus (the union of components of dimension < d_j, the pairwise intersections C_a cap C_b for a != b, and Sing(Y^{(j)})).\n\nThen O is open in Y^{(j)}, smooth, of pure dimension d_j, and dense in each C_a, with the pieces O cap C_a pairwise disjoint. The coarse space |X| of M_{6,6} is a quasi-projective variety, so the coarse space of the reduced closed substack Y^{(j)} is quasi-projective, and O^c is a locally closed (hence quasi-projective) subscheme of |X|. Choose a nonempty affine open A_a of each (O cap C_a)^c; such opens exist because a quasi-projective variety admits a dense affine open obtained as the complement of a hypersurface in a projective closure, and finitely many prescribed points on distinct components can be avoided. Let A := A_1 disjoint union ... disjoint union A_r, a finite disjoint union of affine schemes, hence affine. Let S_j be the open substack of O lying over A. Then S_j is smooth of pure dimension d_j with affine coarse space, and is dense in each top-dimensional component C_a.\n\nPut Y^{(j+1)} := (Y^{(j)} minus S_j)_{red}. This is closed in Y^{(j)}, hence closed in X. It is the union of the lower-dimensional components of Y^{(j)} with the sets C_a minus S_j, each a proper closed subset of the irreducible C_a, so dim Y^{(j+1)} <= d_j - 1. Finally S_j = Y^{(j)} cap (X minus Y^{(j+1)}) is closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)} because Y^{(j)} is closed in X. Strict decrease of a nonnegative integer dimension forces termination at the empty stack after finitely many steps. No upper bound on dim Y is used: the only comparison is dim Y^{(j)} <= dim X = 21, which is automatic for a closed substack. This is (i).\n\nBecause the n_j strictly decrease, each integer occurs as a stratum dimension at most once.\n\nAffineness of S_j is constructed by choosing an affine open of a quasi-projective coarse space. The archive constraint that an open subset of an affine stack is automatically affine is not used.\n\n## 2. The support filtration and its graded pieces, for every admissible chain\n\nFix an arbitrary admissible chain as in Lemma 1 (or any other admissible chain: the arguments of this section and the next use only the defining properties). Write V_j := X minus Y^{(j)}. Each V_j is open in X, hence smooth of pure dimension 21. Then V_0 = U_Y, V_N = X, V_j is contained in V_{j+1}, and V_{j+1} minus S_j = V_j. Define, for 0 <= j <= N,\n\n  A_j := ker( T -> W_{26} H^{26}(V_j; Q)(21) ),\n\nthe map being W_{26} of ordinary restriction H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(V_j; Q), twisted by (21). Each A_j is a kernel of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures out of the pure object T, hence a sub-Hodge structure of T, pure polarizable of weight -16.\n\nA_0 = T_Z by CLM-0120-4, because V_0 = U_Y and the map is r_T. A_N = 0, because V_N = X and the restriction is the identity on T. If j increases then V_j enlarges, so restriction to V_j factors through restriction to V_{j+1}, and therefore A_{j+1} is contained in A_j. This is a finite decreasing filtration of T by sub-Hodge structures with A_0 = T_Z and A_N = 0.\n\nLemma 2. For each j, the graded piece A_j / A_{j+1} is a subquotient of the pure polarizable weight -16 Hodge structure W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(n_j).\n\nProof. Apply (S2) to the smooth ambient V_{j+1} of pure dimension 21 and its smooth closed substack S_j of pure dimension n_j, hence of pure codimension c_j := 21 - n_j, at cohomological degree m = 26. The identity m - 2 c_j = 26 - 2(21 - n_j) = 2 n_j - 16 holds, so exactness at H^{26}(V_{j+1}) gives\n\n  ker( H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) -> H^{26}(V_j; Q) ) = image( H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) -> H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) ).\n\nBy (S5) the functor W_{26} is exact, so\n\n  ker( W_{26} H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) -> W_{26} H^{26}(V_j; Q) )\n\nequals W_{26} of that image, which is a quotient of W_{26}( H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) ). No identification of a supports group with its image in T is used: every object here is a kernel of an open restriction. (The connecting map from H^{25}(V_j) need not vanish in weight 26, which is why the graded piece is a subquotient rather than an isomorphism.)\n\nThe restriction A_j -> W_{26} H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q)(21) has kernel A_j cap A_{j+1} = A_{j+1}, and its image lies in the displayed kernel twisted by (21), because every class in A_j already restricts to zero on the smaller open V_j. Hence A_j / A_{j+1} embeds into that kernel, and is therefore a subquotient of W_{26}( H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) )(21).\n\nBy (S1), S_j being smooth, H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) has weights at least 2 n_j - 16. The Tate twist (-c_j) shifts weights by +2 c_j, so H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) has weights at least (2 n_j - 16) + 2(21 - n_j) = 26. Therefore W_{26} of it equals W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j). The further twist (21) uses (-c_j) + 21 = n_j, and the resulting weight is (2 n_j - 16) - 2 n_j = -16. This is (ii).\n\nNo Gysin map for the pair (X, Y) or (X, Z), no closed embedding of Z, no fundamental class of Y, no regular immersion of Y, and no degree shift by twice a codimension of Y or Z appears. The only purity sequence is (S2) for the smooth pair constructed in Lemma 1.\n\n## 3. Endpoint vanishings and the dimension-8 piece\n\nLemma 3. With notation as above:\n\n(a) If n_j >= 17, then H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) = 0, hence A_j / A_{j+1} = 0.\n\n(b) If n_j <= 7, then H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) = 0, hence A_j / A_{j+1} = 0.\n\n(c) If n_j = 8, then W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(n_j) = H^0(S_j; Q)(8), which is a finite direct sum of Q(8), and therefore so is A_j / A_{j+1}.\n\nProof. (a) For n_j >= 17 one has 2 n_j - 16 = n_j + (n_j - 16) >= n_j + 1 > n_j = dim S_j. By (S3), H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) = H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j^c; Q), and S_j^c is an affine variety of dimension n_j, so this vanishes by (S4). Lemma 2 then gives A_j / A_{j+1} = 0. The only dimensions that can occur inside X are n_j in {17, 18, 19, 20, 21}, giving degrees 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, each strictly larger than n_j.\n\n(b) For n_j <= 7 one has 2 n_j - 16 <= -2 < 0, and cohomology in negative degree is zero.\n\n(c) For n_j = 8 one has 2 n_j - 16 = 0. The group H^0(S_j; Q) of a nonempty finite-type DM stack is Q to the power of the finite set of connected components, pure of weight 0, so W_0 H^0 = H^0. Twisting by (8) yields a finite direct sum of Q(8). By Lemma 2 the graded piece is a subquotient of that group, hence itself a finite direct sum of Q(8) by (S6). If S_j is empty this index does not occur.\n\nThese are the two vanishings and the n_j = 8 Tate statement required by (iii). They are not inferences from smallness of unnamed strata: the n_j >= 17 vanishing uses the degree inequality 2 n_j - 16 > n_j together with affineness of the coarse space, and the n_j <= 7 vanishing uses negativity of the degree. The archive constraints that unnamed lower-dimensional strata contribute only zero or Tate classes, and that positive-codimension strata cannot contribute solely because they have smaller dimension, are therefore not walked. Dimensions 9 through 16 are not declared zero or Tate.\n\n## 4. Splitting of T_Z, not necessarily canonical\n\nLemma 4. For every admissible chain, T_Z is isomorphic, not necessarily canonically, to the direct sum of the graded pieces A_j / A_{j+1} indexed by those j with n_j in {8, ..., 16}. At most one such piece occurs per dimension, so at most eight pieces lie in the range 9 <= n_j <= 16.\n\nProof. Each A_j is a subobject of the pure polarizable weight -16 structure T, so the finite filtration T_Z = A_0 superset A_1 superset ... superset A_N = 0 is a filtration by objects of that semisimple abelian category (S6). Semisimplicity supplies some (not unique, not canonical) splitting T_Z isomorphic to the direct sum over j of A_j / A_{j+1}. Lemma 3 kills every summand with n_j <= 7 or n_j >= 17, and identifies the n_j = 8 summand as a finite direct sum of Q(8). The surviving indices therefore lie in {8, ..., 16}. Strict decrease of the n_j in Lemma 1 gives at most one stratum per dimension, hence at most nine surviving dimensions of which at most eight lie in {9, ..., 16}. This is (iv).\n\nT_Z depends only on the pair (X, Y) by CLM-0120-6, so the isomorphism type of the left-hand side is independent of the chain. The individual residual strata S_j with 9 <= n_j <= 16 may depend on the chain; that dependence is outside the scope of this theorem and is not recorded as a defect. No preferred chain is singled out. Clauses (ii) through (iv) have been proved for every admissible chain.\n\nNo realization of any adjudicated non-Tate model as a single admissible stratum is claimed. A proper support is not affine, hence is not an admissible stratum in the sense of Lemma 1; an admissible chain would peel an affine open and leave a lower-dimensional complement. In particular this argument does not present a proper abelian variety (or any other proper non-Tate variety) as a single S_j.\n\n## 5. The sufficiency implication\n\nLemma 5. If for some admissible chain every graded piece A_j / A_{j+1} with 9 <= n_j <= 16 is a finite direct sum of Q(8), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). In particular, this holds if each W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8 - n_j).\n\nProof. By Lemma 4, T_Z is isomorphic to the direct sum of the n_j = 8 piece (already a finite direct sum of Q(8) by Lemma 3(c)) and the pieces with 9 <= n_j <= 16. Under the hypothesis each of the latter is a finite direct sum of Q(8), so the whole sum is. For the instance: if W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8 - n_j), the twist identity Q(8 - n_j)(n_j) = Q(8) and Lemma 2 make A_j / A_{j+1} a subquotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8), hence itself such a sum by (S6). This is (v), proved as an implication. Its antecedent is deliberately left open: nothing here determines W_{2 n - 16} H^{2 n - 16}(S_{(n)}; Q) or the corresponding graded piece for any n with 9 <= n <= 16. That range is the assigned obligation of C66-TATE-SUPPORT and is not a gap in this theorem.\n\nNo Tate type of T_Z is asserted. No lower bound on T_Z is asserted: if T_Z = 0, then every graded piece is zero and (i) through (v) hold as the empty-sum case of a finite direct sum of Q(8). Complementary target terms are not assembled. RED-0001 is never assumed.\n\n## 6. Scope, blocked routes, and recorded constraints\n\nClauses (i) through (v) are proved unconditionally. Conventions for (CE), (N), (BAL), W_f, L, and the packet orientation of F are those of ATT-0112 Section 0.1, citing SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 and FND-0156; they are not reproved.\n\n### 0.1 Dual-confirmed dependency ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP)\n\nATT-0112, independently confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158, is used only through the following clauses, within their recorded scheme-level reduced-base scope:\n\n- CLM-0112-1, CLM-0112-2: H is smooth of pure dimension 18; H^bal is open, hence smooth of pure dimension 18.\n- CLM-0112-4: the discriminant morphism br: H -> |O_{P^1}(18)| = P^{18} is quasi-finite; H^{comp} sits in br^{-1}(Delta_{18}).\n- CLM-0112-5, CLM-0112-6, CLM-0112-7: the type-(ii) / non-primitive locus has dimension at most 14 in H^bal and at most 11 in Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2]; every connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal) meets type (i).\n- CLM-0112-8 / Theorem (E): on every connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian scheme carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family with target P^1 whose classifying image is not contained in H^ii (in particular whenever that image has dimension at least 15), U is connected, H_beta = S_6, Z = Ord(U) is connected finite etale of degree 720, and F(Z)^{S_6} isomorphic to F(U) for additive S_6-equivariant F to Q-vector spaces or mixed Q-Hodge structures.\n\nFND-0152(ii), FND-0053, and ATT-0112 Section 6 are respected: the identity induction functor upgrades nothing to Tate type. Grauert is used only over reduced bases (FND-0131). Numerically (established working-context facts, not reproved as Hodge theorems): dim of the PGL_2-quotient model of Z is 17; Poincare duality on a smooth 17-fold identifies Gr^W_{16} H_c^{16} with Hom(Gr^W_{18} H^{18}, Q(-17)); Borel-Moore duality identifies W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16} with the dual of Gr^W_{16} H_c^{16}; Q(-9)(17) isomorphic to Q(8); a not-asserted Gysin twist Q(-4) would send Q(-9) to Q(-13).
