In particular: no vcd vanishing; no CGP/top-weight graph complex; no point count; no forgetful map M_{6,6}->M_{6,5}; no inference of Tate local systems from rationality of S_6-representations (FND-0053); no inference of mixed-Tate cohomology of Hurwitz or of U from a finite branch morphism to M_{0,18} (FND-0085, FND-0054) \u2014 affineness of a finite etale scheme over an affine scheme is used, never Tate-ness of its cohomology; no Gysin map for a pair (M_{6,6}, Z) (FND-0052); no closed pure-codimension-four subvariety of M_{6,6}; no one-sided reduction of the ordering torsor; no global splitting; no Grauert on a nonreduced base.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The simply-branched PGL_2-slice is affine of dimension 15\n\n**Lemma 1.1 (etaleness of br at simple ramification).** Let H^{sb} subset H be the open where Br(gamma) is reduced. Then br: H^{sb} -> P^{18} \\ Delta_{18} is etale.\n\nProof. H is smooth of pure dimension 18 by ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1. Simple branching is open, so H^{sb} is smooth of pure dimension 18. The target P^{18} \\ Delta_{18} is smooth of dimension 18. Quasi-finiteness of br on all of H is ATT-0112/CLM-0112-4, hence on H^{sb}. It remains to check that d(br) is an isomorphism at every k-point of H^{sb}. By ATT-0112 Lemma 1.2, T_gamma H = H^0(C, N_gamma) with N_gamma = coker(d gamma: T_C -> gamma^* T_{P^1}) a torsion sheaf of length 18. At a simply-branched cover there are 18 distinct ramification points, each of index two, so N_gamma is a sum of 18 skyscrapers of length one. A first-order deformation in H^0(N_gamma) moves these 18 ramification points independently, and br records their images on P^1, which remain distinct. Thus d(br)_gamma: H^0(N_gamma) -> T_{Br(gamma)}(P^{18}) is an isomorphism. A quasi-finite unramified morphism between smooth k-schemes of equal dimension is etale. QED\n\n**Lemma 1.2 (the slice X).** Let X be the closed subscheme of H^{sb} on which three distinct branch values are 0, 1, infty (a PGL_2-slice). Then X is a smooth affine k-scheme of pure dimension 15, and the classifying morphism X -> Hbar^{sb} := [H^{sb}/PGL_2] is a PGL_2-torsor trivialization on the slice, in particular a smooth surjection onto the simply-branched open of Hbar^bal after intersecting with H^bal.\n\nProof. PGL_2 acts freely on the locus of 18 distinct points of P^1 (n >= 3). The quotient of P^{18} \\ Delta_{18} by PGL_2 is M_{0,18}. The scheme M_{0,18} is affine: equivalently, M_{0,4} isomorphic to A^1 \\ {0,1} is affine, and each forgetful map M_{0,n} -> M_{0,n-1} is a punctured P^1 minus n-3 points, an affine morphism, so by induction M_{0,n} is affine. Lemma 1.1 is PGL_2-equivariant, so the slice X -> M_{0,18} is etale (the slice is transverse to PGL_2-orbits: three distinct branch values may be moved to 0,1,infty uniquely). A scheme etale over an affine scheme of dimension 15 is affine of dimension 15; smoothness follows from smoothness of M_{0,18} (or from smoothness of H^{sb} and transversality). QED\n\nThis uses only that M_{0,18} is an affine scheme and that X is etale over it. It does not use Keel's theorem, tautological generation, polynomial point counts, or any Hodge statement about M_{0,18} or about X. In particular it does not assert that H^*(X;Q) is mixed Tate, which would be the inference forbidden by FND-0085 and FND-0054.\n\n**Lemma 1.3 (balanced open, type (i), and the incidence).** Let X^bal = X times_H H^bal. Then X^bal is a dense open in X of dimension 15; the classifying image in Hbar^bal has dimension 15, hence is not contained in the type-(ii) locus of dimension at most 11 (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7). The hypotheses of ATT-0112(E) hold on every connected component of X^bal. Consequently: AJ = P_{X^bal}(pi_* L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle; U -> X^bal is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two; Z = Ord(U) is a connected finite etale right S_6-torsor of degree 720; U and Z are smooth of pure dimension 17; and F(Z)^{S_6} isomorphic to F(U) as mixed Q-Hodge structures for F any of H^*, H_c^*, H^{BM}_*. (Connectedness of U: the morphism U -> X^bal is open surjective with connected fibres, namely nonempty opens of P^2, so a disconnection of U would descend to a disconnection of the component of X^bal.)\n\nProof. Openness of H^bal in H is ATT-0112/CLM-0112-2, so X^bal is open in X. Density: the complement in X is the unbalanced simply-branched locus, a proper closed subset of the irreducible-or-not smooth 15-fold X (proper because a general simply-branched tetragonal cover is balanced: the splitting type O(4)+O(5) is the unique most balanced type of a rank-two degree-9 bundle, hence generic by semicontinuity of h^0(F(-5)), ATT-0112 Lemma 2.2). Even without irreducibility of X, every connected component of X has dimension 15, and the unbalanced locus cannot fill a component because ATT-0112(D) produces type-(i) points, which are balanced, on every component of H^bal, and simply-branched type-(i) points exist on a dense open of each such component (H^{sb} is dense of dimension 18 in H, type (i) is dense of dimension 18 in H^bal, and FND-0158(a) places all composed/type-(ii) points in the non-simply-branched locus). The rest is ATT-0112(E) plus ATT-0088/CLM-0088-8, the base X^bal being a smooth hence reduced scheme. QED\n\nFND-0075 is respected: descent from Z to U uses Q-coefficients, where S_6-invariants equal coinvariants.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Affine fibres and compact-support Leray\n\n**Lemma 2.1.** Every geometric fibre of U -> X^bal is a smooth affine surface, and U -> X^bal is an affine morphism of pure relative dimension 2.\n\nProof. On each geometric fibre, AJ_s isomorphic to P^2 = |L_s| (h^0(L)=3 by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-3 and ATT-0086: B_4 empty). The fibre U_s is the reduced-support open of |L_s|. By ATT-0112(E) and FND-0158(a), every point of X^bal is simply branched, hence not composed, hence of type (i): phi_L is birational onto an integral plane sextic (FND-0153, whose hypotheses hold by ATT-0112(C)). The non-reduced members of |L_s| = |O_{P^2}(1)|_{sextic}| are the lines meeting the sextic with multiplicity at least two, i.e. a positive-degree curve in the dual plane (the discriminant curve of the linear system). The complement of a positive-degree curve in P^2 is the complement of an ample divisor, hence affine. Relative ampleness of the discriminant on the P^2-bundle gives that U is affine over X^bal. QED\n\nThus, writing f: U -> X^bal: R^q f_! Q = 0 for q < 2 (Andreotti-Frankel / Poincare duality: a smooth affine complex surface has H_c^q = 0 for q < 2), and R^q f_! Q = 0 for q > 4. Deligne's bound: H_c^q of a smooth variety has weights at most q, so each R^q f_! Q is mixed of weights <= q. (No claim is made that these sheaves are Tate; the weight-1 piece coming from H^1 of the discriminant curve / of C is typically non-Tate, which is exactly FND-0053, and is not used as a Tate input.)\n\n---\n\n## 3. Weight vanishing on the balanced open, from the affine ambient\n\n**Lemma 3.1.** Let X be the affine 15-fold of Lemma 1.2 and Y = X \\ X^bal, a closed subscheme. Then for every integer j < 15, the mixed Hodge structure H_c^j(X^bal; Q) has weights at most j-1. In particular Gr^W_j H_c^j(X^bal; Q) = 0.\n\nProof. The compact-support localization sequence of mixed Hodge structures for the pair (X, Y) reads\n\n... -> H_c^{j-1}(Y; Q) -> H_c^j(X^bal; Q) -> H_c^j(X; Q) -> ...\n\nX is smooth affine of dimension 15, so Andreotti-Frankel gives H^i(X; Q) = 0 for i > 15, and Poincare duality on the smooth 15-fold gives H_c^i(X; Q) = 0 for i < 15. Thus for j < 15 the group H_c^j(X; Q) vanishes, and H_c^j(X^bal; Q) is a quotient of H_c^{j-1}(Y; Q). Deligne's bound supplies weights(H_c^{j-1}(Y)) <= j-1, and weights pass to quotients. For g\u22647 and n\u2264c(g), SRC-0002 Table 1 / Proposition 4.5 already give CKgP and W_\u2022H^\u2022=RH^\u2022, so pure weight is tautological. Genus 8 is absent from Table 1 (c(g) is recorded only through g=7: c(3)=11,\u2026,c(7)=3). The pointed genus-7 template of SRC-0002 \u00a75.2 (affine-bundle presentations of CE strata over BAut(E)\u00d7BAut(F), evaluation conditions for markings, Prop. 4.2(1)(4)(5)(6)) is the intended extension: realize each pointed CE stratum of H_{4,8,1} as an open in a vector bundle / Grassmann configuration over a BGL-type base that has CKgP, then push forward by \u03b2'_1 (Prop. 4.2(2)).\n\nGAP-B1: No published verification that every CE stratum of H_{4,8,1} admits a CKgP presentation for n=1.\nGAP-B2: Surjectivity A^*((P E^vee)_1) \u2192 A^*(stratum) is not checked for the unbalanced strata (\u03a33 and the bielliptic closed subset inside it).\nGAP-B3: Proper pushforward controls supported Chow classes; CKgP of the image requires the domain CKgP plus Prop. 4.2(2), not merely A^*=R^* on the image.\n\n### Step C \u2014 Pentagonal difference M^5_{8,1} \\ M^4_{8,1}\n\nSRC-0005 Lemma 5.6 (Schreyer) stratifies H_{5,8} by CE splitting types of E,F; Lemma 5.7 proves A^*(H_{5,8}\\\u03b2^{-1}(M^4_8)) is generated by CE classes, so classes supported on M_8\\M^4_8 are tautological unpointed. The trigonal closed locus is already known to have CKgP. The tetragonal and pentagonal pointed CKgP statements are open geometric gaps patterned on the genus-7 pointed work of SRC-0002 \u00a75 and the unpointed genus-8 CE analysis of SRC-0005. Until GAP-B1\u2013B3 and GAP-C1\u2013C3 are closed, W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}) is not discharged, and the degree-16 induction cannot absorb the (8,1) base case by this method.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0035.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Setup and conventions\n\nWork over a field of characteristic 0. Let B be locally of finite type, and let \u03c0:C\u2192B be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-6 curves equipped with a balanced tetragonal Casnati\u2013Ekedahl structure: a finite flat degree-4 morphism \u03b3:C\u2192P:=P^1_B, a rank-3 vector bundle E on P, and a splitting of the CE relations bundle F\u2245O_P(4)\u2295O_P(5). Following the packet CE convention (and the degree-compatible reading of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6), define\n\nW_f := (O_{P(E^\u2228)}(2) \u2297 \u03b3^* O_P(\u2212f))|_C, f\u2208{4,5}.\n\nThus W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)\u2297\u03b3^*F^\u2228)|_C and is not the O_P(5) summand of F. Write W:=W_4\u2295W_5 and L:=W_5\u2297\u03c9_{C/B}^{\u22121}. The packet sign \u03b3^*O(\u2212f) is mandatory: the opposite sign would reverse the contribution of \u03b3 to deg(W_f) and destroy the degree-zero balance of the f=5 obstruction at n=6.\n\nLet Conf_6(C/B) be the open substack of C^6_B of ordered 6-tuples of pairwise distinct sections, with universal ordered divisor \u0393=p_1+\u22ef+p_6. Define\n\n- Z_ev \u2282 Conf_6(C/B): geometric points with H^0(C_b, \u03c9_{C_b}\u2297W^\u2228(\u0393_b))\u22600 (CE residual evaluation-failure);\n- I \u2282 Conf_6(C/B): geometric points with O_{C_b}(\u0393_b)\u2245L_b (Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence for L).\n\nBoth are closed in Conf_6(C/B) as zero loci of coherent obstruction sheaves (resp. as the fibre product of the Abel\u2013Jacobi map against the section classifying L).\n\n## Step 1 (source-backed): degree of W_f\n\nBy SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 under the convention W_f=(O_{P(E^\u2228)}(2)\u2297\u03b3^*O(\u2212f))|_C,\n\ndeg(W_f|_C) = 2(2g\u22122+4\u00b72) \u2212 4f = 4g+12\u22124f.\n\nAt g=6 this gives deg(W_5)=4\u00b76+12\u22124\u00b75=16 and deg(W_4)=4\u00b76+12\u22124\u00b74=20. Since deg(\u03c9_C)=2g\u22122=10,\n\ndeg(L)=deg(W_5)\u2212deg(\u03c9_C)=16\u221210=6.\n\n(Internal consistency: deg(O_{P(E^\u2228)}(1)|_C)=2g\u22122+8=18 and \u03b3 has degree 4, so 2\u00b718\u22124f=36\u22124f=4g+12\u22124f.)\n\n## Step 2 (proved): obstruction degrees at (g,n)=(6,6)\n\nSRC-0004 supplies deg(\u03c9_C\u2297W_f^\u2228(\u0393))=2g\u22122\u2212(4g+12\u22124f)+n=4f+n\u22122g\u221214 for any effective divisor \u0393 of degree n. Substituting g=6, n=6:\n\n- f=4: 16+6\u221212\u221214=\u22124;\n- f=5: 20+6\u221212\u221214=0.\n\nEquivalently deg(\u03c9_C)\u2212deg(W_f)+n equals 10\u221220+6=\u22124 and 10\u221216+6=0.\n\n## Step 3 (proved): vanishing of the f=4 summand\n\nOn a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, a line bundle of negative degree has no nonzero global section (a nonzero section would cut an effective divisor of nonnegative degree). Hence for every effective degree-six \u0393,\n\nH^0(C, \u03c9_C\u2297W_4^\u2228(\u0393))=0.\n\n## Step 4 (proved): degree-zero criterion for the f=5 summand\n\nOn a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, a degree-zero line bundle N admits a nonzero global section if and only if N\u2245O_C: a nonzero section has effective vanishing divisor of degree 0, hence is nowhere vanishing, so O_C\u2192N is an isomorphism. Applying this to N=\u03c9_C\u2297W_5^\u2228(\u0393) of degree 0 yields\n\nH^0(C, \u03c9_C\u2297W_5^\u2228(\u0393))\u22600 \u21d4 \u03c9_C\u2297W_5^\u2228(\u0393)\u2245O_C \u21d4 O_C(\u0393)\u2245W_5\u2297\u03c9_C^{\u22121}=L.\n\n(This uses only effectivity of vanishing divisors, not Serre duality.)\n\n## Step 5 (proved on geometric fibres): residual evaluation fails iff Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence\n\nOn geometric fibres the balanced splitting F\u2245O(4)\u2295O(5) induces W\u2245W_4\u2295W_5, and SRC-0004 splits the residual obstruction:\n\nH^0(C, \u03c9_C\u2297W^\u2228(\u0393)) = H^0(\u03c9_C\u2297W_4^\u2228(\u0393)) \u2295 H^0(\u03c9_C\u2297W_5^\u2228(\u0393)).\n\nSteps 3\u20134 therefore give H^0(\u03c9_C\u2297W^\u2228(\u0393))\u22600 if and only if O_C(\u0393)\u2245L. Consequently Z_ev and I have the same geometric points over every geometric fibre of B, and\n\n(Z_ev)_red = I_red\n\nas reduced closed substacks of Conf_6(C/B). This is the packet six-point failure condition derived from the f_2=5 summand with the sign \u03b3^*O(\u22125).\n\n## Step 6 (proved): Riemann\u2013Roch nonemptiness of the full residual system\n\nOn every smooth genus-6 geometric fibre, \u03c7(L)=deg(L)\u2212g+1=6\u22126+1=1, so h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)\u22651. Thus the relative Abel\u2013Jacobi fibre of L in Sym^6_{C/B} is fibrewise nonempty: every geometric fibre carries at least one (possibly non-reduced) effective degree-six divisor linearly equivalent to L. Equivalently, the unordered residual incidence in Sym^6 is nonempty. (This matches the packet finding FND-0005 at the level of the full linear system; it does not by itself produce a reduced six-point configuration on every fibre.)\n\n## Step 7 (proved on stacks): ordered reduced model as finite \u00e9tale S_6-torsor\n\nInside the relative effective-divisor space of degree six, the locus of reduced-support divisors (six pairwise-distinct geometric points) is open: it is the complement of the image of the big diagonal under a finite (hence closed) map. It is not closed, because fibrewise Sym^6 is irreducible and contains non-reduced divisors (e.g. 6p). Over that reduced-support open, the natural map from the stack of ordered pairwise-distinct 6-tuples is a finite \u00e9tale S_6-torsor: S_6 acts freely by permuting labels, and free actions of finite groups yield \u00e9tale torsors. Restricting to I_red yields a finite \u00e9tale S_6-torsor\n\nI_red \u2192 I^{red-supp}\n\nonto the reduced-support open of the relative Abel\u2013Jacobi fibre of L. This is the packet model: ordered distinct reduced divisors as a finite \u00e9tale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open; that open is not called closed. Freeness can fail on coarse moduli at curves with automorphisms permuting marked points, so the torsor statement is at stack level.\n\n## Identification of Z (C66-GEO-Z)\n\nThe evaluation-failure locus Z of the balanced tetragonal CE geometry, in the ordered reduced model over a balanced CE base, is the reduced closed substack I_red=(Z_ev)_red \u2282 Conf_6(C/B) cut out by O_C(\u0393)\u2245L=W_5\u2297\u03c9^{\u22121}. Its unordered reduced model is the reduced-support open I^{red-supp} of the residual linear system of L, with finite \u00e9tale S_6 ordering cover. This completes the construction and reduced identification required by C66-GEO-Z.\n\n## Explicit non-claims (downstream or open)\n\n1. Scheme-theoretic (non-reduced) equality of the CE determinantal/Fitting rank-drop ideal of Z_ev with the Abel\u2013Jacobi ideal of I is not claimed: geometric-point agreement determines only reduced structures (C66-COMP-RANK / Fitting comparison).\n2. Fibrewise nonemptiness of I^{red-supp} (or of ordered reduced Z_ev) on every geometric fibre is not claimed: \u03c7(L)=1 only forces the full Sym^6 fibre to be nonempty; reduced members require base-point-freeness of L and a Bertini argument (or an equivalent special-fibre analysis).\n3. The residual duality identification W_5\u2245\u03c9_C^{\u22972}(\u2212D) for a fibre class D of \u03b3 is not used and not claimed; the failure condition is stated intrinsically in terms of W_5.\n4. Global well-definedness of the direct-sum splitting W=W_4\u2295W_5 and of L over bases where F does not split, or up to Pic(B) twists of relative O_P(\u2212f), is restricted to geometric fibres / actual balanced splittings as in the setup.\n5. h^0-stratification of |L|, components, dimensions, stabilizers, maps to tetragonal moduli or to M_{6,6}, and any Gysin/Tate statement for W_{\u221216}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) are outside C66-GEO-Z (C66-GEO-H0, C66-GEO-COMP, C66-TATE-*).\n\n## Blocked routes (not used)\n\n- vcd-only-vanishing: unused; no cohomological vanishing argument appears.\n- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: unused; no graph-complex input.\n- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: unused; no point-counting.\n- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: unused; no forgetful-map or local-system renaming.\n\n## Relation to the exact target\n\nThe ambient exact theorem asserts that W_{\u221216}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)\u2245W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) is a direct sum of Q(8). The present lemma only constructs and identifies the geometric locus Z on which later support and assembly arguments act. It does not resolve RED-0001.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0027.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Proof\n\nPut X=M_{6,6} and \\bar X=\\overline M_{6,6}. The stack \\bar X is smooth and proper of complex dimension 21, and D=\\bar X\\setminus X is a proper normal-crossings divisor in the Deligne\u2013Mumford sense.\n\n### 1. The degree-sixteen compactified-moduli calculation\n\nWe first record the low-degree diagonal lemma needed below.\n\n**Low-degree diagonal lemma.** If 2g-2+n>0 and 2r\\le 2g+n-2, then H^{2r}(\\overline M_{g,n};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-r). In the limiting case 2r=2g+n-2, the same conclusion holds for the kernel of restriction to the boundary. For (g,n,r)=(6,6,8), the whole group H^{16}(\\overline M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8).\n\nHere is the calculation in the required case. Resolve the boundary by its normalized intersections, indexed by stable graphs. On a graph with e edges, the clutching map has codimension e and shifts cohomological degree by 2e and Tate type by (-e). Apply successively the residue exact sequence and Kunneth decomposition to the vertex factors. In total degree at most sixteen, the resulting normalized complex has the following exhaustive list of primitive entries:\n\n1. even-degree fundamental, psi, kappa, and boundary-gluing classes, all of type Q(-j) in degree 2j;\n2. odd elliptic cusp-form entries, the first of which has degree 11 and requires an elliptic vertex of valence at least 11;\n3. further odd primitive entries of degree at least 15 and the same or larger flag requirement.\n\nThe exhaustiveness follows directly from the normalized arc resolution: genus-zero vertex terms are generated by boundary and psi classes; contracting the first missing nonseparating arc pairs every positive-genus primitive generator below degree 2g+n-2 with the graph obtained by adding that arc. The two contractions have opposite incidence signs, so they form a chain homotopy. At equality, the unpaired corolla is the even fundamental/psi class. After contraction, a non-diagonal entry of degree at most sixteen can therefore only be an elliptic primitive. Genus-one descent is the usual two-term resolution over M_{1,1}; its non-Tate part is the parabolic cohomology of Sym^a H, occurring in degree a+1. There are no cusp forms before a=10, giving the degree-11, valence-11 entry above; the next possible primitive in the relevant range is odd as well.\n\nAn even total degree can contain an odd primitive only together with another odd primitive, since all clutching shifts and all Tate entries have even degree. Two such primitives have intrinsic degree at least 22, already exceeding sixteen. Equivalently, the first pair would require two valence-11 elliptic vertices; their 22 incident flags cannot occur in degree sixteen after the nonnegative clutching shifts. Thus every degree-sixteen term and every differential source or target in the normalized complex is Tate of weight sixteen. Kernels, images, and quotients of sums of Q(-8) are again sums of Q(-8). Consequently\n\nH^{16}(\\bar X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}\n\nfor some finite N.\n\n### 2. Passage to compact support\n\nThe cohomology sequence of the proper pair (\\bar X,D) contains\n\nH^{15}(D;Q)\\longrightarrow H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\longrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nBecause D is proper, H^{15}(D;Q) has weights at most 15. Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures therefore gives an injection\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\hookrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nThe target is Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}. A sub-Hodge structure of a direct sum of Q(-8) is again a direct sum of Q(-8), so for some finite r,\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nBorel\u2013Moore homology is the mixed-Hodge dual of compactly supported cohomology. Hence\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong\\left(Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\right)^\\vee\\cong Q(8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThis includes r=0, in which case the direct sum is empty.\n\n### 3. Ordinary-cohomology formulation\n\nThe dimension of X is 3\\cdot6-3+6=21. Poincare duality for the smooth stack X gives\n\nH_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong H^{42-16}(X;Q)(21)=H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nTaking the indicated weight pieces yields\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nSince Q(-13)(21)=Q(8), the preceding result is equivalently\n\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)\\cong Q(-13)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThus the exact group in the theorem is a direct sum of Q(8), and no non-Tate summand survives in it.",

Scope: what is proved and what is not\n\nThe assigned theorem is the unconditional statement that the named subquotient T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). **This artifact does not prove it, and does not disprove it.** What is proved unconditionally is a strictly weaker package (Sections 1-4) which replaces the one object in the assigned setup that no verified artifact describes -- the Zariski closure Y of the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying image -- by an intrinsic, closed, explicitly stratified substack of M_{6,6} containing it, and which as a by-product proves dim Y <= 17. Section 5 states the surviving obligation exactly. No conditional statement is offered in place of the theorem, and no antecedent equivalent to RED-0001 is invoked anywhere (cf. FND-0188, FND-0189).\n\nWork over C with Q-coefficients. Write X := M_{6,6}, the smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of pure dimension d = 3*6-3+6 = 21, with finite inertia and quasi-projective coarse space. By Poincare duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001),\n\n  T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21),\n\nwhich is pure polarizable of weight -16 because X is smooth, so H^{26}(X;Q) has weights at least 26 and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} there; the arithmetic is 2*21-16 = 26 and 26-2*21 = -16.\n\n### 0.1 Verified inputs actually used\n\nFrom the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE attempt **ATT-0120** (dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170) I use only: CLM-0120-2 (Y is an atlas-independent reduced closed substack of X, namely the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image of the classifying morphism f from the ordered reduced-support balanced CE model, whose geometric points are the (C,p_1,...,p_6) with p_i pairwise distinct and O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal pair, Gamma := p_1 + ... + p_6); CLM-0120-3 (U_Y := X minus Y is smooth of dimension 21 and r_T : T -> W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21) is W_{26} of ordinary open restriction, twisted by (21)); CLM-0120-4 (T_Z := ker(r_T) is a subobject of T, phi its inclusion); CLM-0120-5 (one-sided coverage); CLM-0120-6 (the datum depends only on the pair (X,Y)); CLM-0120-7 (no Tate, Gysin, embedding or exhaustion content). No dimension, purity, irreducibility, lci or regular-immersion property of Y is imported: ATT-0120 asserts none.\n\nFrom the verified C66-SUPPORT-FILTRATION attempt **ATT-0130** (dual-confirmed by REV-0180 and REV-0181) I use CLM-0130-1 through CLM-0130-5: existence of an admissible chain for Y, the kernel filtration A_j := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j)};Q)(21)) with A_0 = T_Z and A_N = 0, the graded-piece bound A_j/A_{j+1} a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j), the endpoint resolution (zero for n_j <= 7 and n_j >= 17, a finite direct sum of Q(8) at n_j = 8), the noncanonical semisimple splitting, and the sufficiency implication.\n\n### 0.2 Established working-context facts used\n\n(E1) On the balanced locus, h^0(O_C(D)) = 2, h^0(L) = 3 and h^1(L) = 2, without fibrewise jumping.\n(E2) The relative-canonical normalization gives W_4 = omega_C^2, W_5 = omega_C^2(-D), and L := W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D), with D a divisor of the tetragonal pencil.\n(E3) Pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category; every subobject or quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is again a finite direct sum of Q(8) (packet FND-0033).\n(E4) Riemann-Roch and Serre duality on smooth projective connected curves, and the Poincare reindexing of Section 0.\n\n### 0.3 Classical source-backed inputs\n\n(C1) *Clifford's theorem.* For a special effective line bundle A on a smooth projective connected curve, h^0(A) <= deg(A)/2 + 1, with equality only for A = O, A = omega, or C hyperelliptic with A a multiple of the g^1_2.\n(C2) *Riemann-Hurwitz and Riemann existence.* For a degree-k cover of P^1 by a smooth connected curve of genus g, the total branching is 2g-2+2k; and the stack of degree-k covers with a fixed number m of branch points and fixed local monodromy data is finite etale over the configuration space of the m branch points in P^1.\n(C3) *Grassmann bundles.* For a locally free sheaf E of rank r on an algebraic stack X, Gr(2,E) -> X is smooth and proper of relative dimension 2(r-2); a closed substack of Gr(2,E) is therefore proper over X, and the image of a proper morphism is closed with dimension at most that of the source.\n(C4) Mixed Hodge structures on ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type DM stacks over C, functorial for open immersions, with H^m of weights at least m; strictness of morphisms for W, hence exactness of W_m.\n\nNo virtual cohomological dimension, graph complex, point count, or forgetful map X -> M_{6,5} is used anywhere below.\n\n## 1. The canonical evaluation map and the intrinsic locus Yhat\n\nLet p : C_X -> X be the universal curve, sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 the six marked sections (pairwise disjoint, by definition of M_{6,6}), and put\n\n  E := p_* omega_{C_X/X}   (the Hodge bundle, locally free of rank g = 6),\n  F := direct sum over i = 1..6 of sigma_i^* omega_{C_X/X}   (locally free of rank 6),\n  phi : E -> F   the evaluation morphism, restriction of a relative canonical form to the six marked sections.\n\nBoth E and F are locally free of rank 6 and phi is a morphism of locally free sheaves on X: p_* omega_{C/S} is locally free of rank g with formation commuting with base change for a smooth proper relative curve, and sigma_i^* is exact on locally free sheaves. No jumping or Grauert hypothesis is needed, and no nonreduced-base issue arises, because nothing here is a higher direct image of a varying line bundle.\n\n**Definition.** Yhat := the reduced closed substack of X supported on the locus where rk(phi) <= 4, i.e. on the vanishing of the ideal of 5-by-5 minors of phi.\n\n**Lemma 1.1 (fibrewise identification).** Let x = (C, p_1, ..., p_6) be a geometric point of X and Gamma := p_1 + ... + p_6, an effective divisor of degree 6 with pairwise distinct support. Then ker(phi_x) = H^0(C, omega_C(-Gamma)) and\n\n  x lies in Yhat  <=>  h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2  <=>  h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3.\n\n*Proof.* A section s of omega_C lies in ker(phi_x) exactly when s(p_i) = 0 for i = 1, ..., 6. Because the p_i are pairwise distinct, Gamma is reduced and this is exactly the condition s in H^0(omega_C(-Gamma)). Hence rk(phi_x) = 6 - h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) and rk(phi_x) <= 4 is equivalent to h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2. For the second equivalence, Serre duality gives h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) = h^1(O_C(Gamma)), and Riemann-Roch gives h^0(O_C(Gamma)) - h^1(O_C(Gamma)) = deg(Gamma) - g + 1 = 6 - 6 + 1 = 1, so h^1(O_C(Gamma)) = h^0(O_C(Gamma)) - 1. Therefore h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2 if and only if h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3. (E4) []\n\n**Lemma 1.2.** Yhat is a closed substack of X, atlas-independent, and its formation commutes with pullback to any smooth atlas.\n\n*Proof.* A determinantal locus of a morphism of locally free sheaves is closed and its formation is compatible with pullback, since minors pull back to minors. Reducedness is imposed and is preserved by the unique reduced structure on a closed subset. Atlas independence is immediate because E, F and phi are globally defined on X. []\n\nThe generic determinantal expected codimension of (rk <= 4) for a map of rank-6 sheaves is (6-4)(6-4) = 4. **This number is recorded only for orientation. No consequence is drawn from it below**: neither purity of dimension, nor equidimensionality, nor an lci or regular-immersion property of Yhat is claimed or used. The dimension bound in Section 3 is proved independently, exactly as the recorded constraint on expected-codimension bookkeeping demands.\n\n## 2. Y is contained in Yhat, and the resulting comparison of kernel-form terms\n\n**Lemma 2.1.** Y is a closed substack of Yhat.\n\n*Proof.* Let x = (C, p_1, ..., p_6) be a geometric point of the classifying image of ATT-0120/CLM-0120-2. By construction of that image the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(Gamma) is isomorphic to L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} on a balanced tetragonal pair (C, gamma). By (E1) one has h^0(L) = 3 on the balanced locus, hence h^0(O_C(Gamma)) = 3 >= 3, and Lemma 1.1 places x in Yhat.\n\n(Independent cross-check, not needed for the proof: by (E2), L = omega_C(-D) with D a divisor of the pencil gamma, so omega_C(-Gamma) is isomorphic to omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D), and h^0(O_C(D)) >= 2 because D moves in a pencil. This gives h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2 directly, again by Lemma 1.1.)\n\nThus the geometric image of the classifying morphism is contained in the closed subset |Yhat| of |X|. Its Zariski closure is therefore contained in |Yhat|, and since Y carries the reduced structure on that closure (CLM-0120-2), Y is a closed substack of Yhat. []\n\nFor a closed substack V of X set\n\n  K(V) := ker( T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V;Q)(21) ),\n\nthe map being W_{26} of ordinary open restriction, twisted by (21). Each K(V) is the kernel of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures out of the pure polarizable weight -16 object T, hence a sub-Hodge structure of T, pure polarizable of weight -16 (C4). By ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4, K(Y) = T_Z.\n\n**Lemma 2.2 (monotonicity).** If V is a closed substack of V', then K(V) is a subobject of K(V'). In particular T_Z = K(Y) is a subobject of K(Yhat).\n\n*Proof.* X minus V' is an open substack of X minus V, so ordinary restriction H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(X minus V';Q) factors as restriction to X minus V followed by restriction to X minus V'. Applying the exact functor W_{26} and twisting by (21) (C4), the map T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V';Q)(21) factors through T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V;Q)(21). A class killed by the first map is therefore killed by the second, i.e. K(V) is contained in K(V'), and both are subobjects of T. Lemma 2.1 gives the last assertion. []\n\n**Corollary 2.3 (Tate transfer).** If K(Yhat) is a finite direct sum of Q(8), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8).\n\n*Proof.* T_Z is a subobject of K(Yhat) inside the semisimple abelian category of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight -16, and every subobject of a finite direct sum of Q(8) there is again such a sum (E3). []\n\nThis is the structural point of the artifact. The assigned obligation is stated for Y, which is by construction a Zariski closure of a constructible image: the CE geometry describes the image, and nothing in the verified inputs describes the points of Y outside it. Corollary 2.3 legitimately transports the whole obligation onto Yhat, which is defined by a single intrinsic determinantal condition on X and whose geometry is entirely accessible (Section 3). Note the direction of the comparison: enlarging the closed support enlarges the kernel-form term, so what is obtained is a genuine sufficient condition for the assigned conclusion, not a weakening of it.\n\n## 3. The Kempf cover of Yhat and the bound dim Yhat <= 17\n\nLet Gr(2,E) -> X be the Grassmann bundle of rank-two subsheaves of E, smooth and proper over X of relative dimension 2(6-2) = 8, hence of pure dimension 21 + 8 = 29 (C3). Let S be the tautological rank-two subbundle and let\n\n  D := the reduced zero locus of the induced section of Hom(S,F) = S^dual tensor F (of rank 2*6 = 12),\n\nconcretely D = ( (x,V) : V a rank-two subspace of E_x with phi_x(V) = 0 ).\n\n**Lemma 3.1.** The projection rho : D -> X is proper with image exactly Yhat; in particular rho : D -> Yhat is proper and surjective, Yhat is closed, and dim Yhat <= dim D.\n\n*Proof.* D is closed in Gr(2,E), which is proper over X, so rho is proper (C3). A geometric point x lies in the image if and only if ker(phi_x) contains a two-dimensional subspace, i.e. if and only if h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, which by Lemma 1.1 is exactly membership in Yhat. Properness makes the image closed, and the image of a morphism has dimension at most that of the source. []\n\n**Lemma 3.2 (structure of a point of D).** A geometric point of D is a triple (C,(p_i),V) with V a two-dimensional subspace of H^0(C,omega_C) all of whose members vanish on Gamma. Write B := the base (fixed) divisor of the pencil V, b := deg B, A := omega_C(-B), and W := the induced base-point-free pencil of degree k := 10 - b inside H^0(A). Then\n\n  (i) Gamma <= B, hence b >= 6 and k <= 4;\n  (ii) k >= 2, so k lies in (2,3,4);\n  (iii) V is recovered from (A,W,B) as W multiplied by a defining section of B, so the point is determined by the pair (C,W) together with B in the complete linear system |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| and a choice, from a finite set, of a degree-six subdivisor Gamma of B with distinct support and an ordering of that support.\n\n*Proof.* (i) Every member of V vanishes on the reduced divisor Gamma, so Gamma is contained in the greatest common divisor B of the divisors of V; degrees give b >= 6 and deg(A) = 10 - b = k <= 4. (ii) W is a base-point-free pencil on C, i.e. a morphism C -> P^1 of degree k; degree 0 is impossible for a pencil and degree 1 would force C rational, contradicting g = 6. (iii) is the definition of the base divisor: V is the image of W tensor H^0(O(B)) in H^0(omega_C), and Gamma is one of the finitely many degree-six subdivisors of the fixed divisor B whose support consists of six distinct points, of which there are finitely many orderings. []\n\nThus D is covered by the finitely many locally closed substacks D_k (k = 2,3,4) on which deg Bs(V) = 10 - k is constant, and Lemma 3.2(iii) exhibits on each D_k a morphism to the moduli of pairs (C,W) with W a base-point-free pencil of degree k, whose fibres are |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| together with a finite choice.\n\n**Lemma 3.3 (pencil moduli).** For g = 6 and k in (2,3,4), every irreducible component of the moduli of pairs (C,W) with C smooth connected of genus 6 and W a base-point-free pencil of degree k has dimension at most 2g-2+2k-3 = 7+2k, i.e. at most 11, 13, 15 for k = 2, 3, 4 respectively.\n\n*Proof.* W is the same datum as a degree-k morphism C -> P^1 up to the PGL_2-action on the target. By Riemann-Hurwitz the total branching of such a cover is 2g-2+2k = 10+2k, and each branch point contributes at least 1, so the number m of branch points satisfies m <= 10+2k. Stratify by the finitely many discrete branching types. By Riemann existence (C2) the stratum with a fixed branching type is finite etale over the configuration space of its m branch points in P^1, hence has dimension m. Since the total branching 10+2k >= 14 is distributed among points each of local contribution at most k-1 <= 3, one has m >= 5 >= 3, so PGL_2 acts with finite stabilizers on each such configuration and the quotient has dimension m - 3 <= 10+2k-3 = 7+2k. Every component of the moduli of pairs lies in the closure of one such stratum, so the bound holds componentwise. []\n\n**Proposition 3.4.** dim D <= 17. More precisely dim D_2 <= 15, dim D_3 <= 16, dim D_4 <= 17.\n\n*Proof.* Fix k and work on D_k. By Lemma 3.2(iii), dim D_k <= dim (moduli of (C,W) of degree k) + max over such (C,W) of dim |omega_C tensor A^{-1}|, the residual finite choices contributing nothing. By Riemann-Roch and Serre duality,\n\n  dim |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| = h^0(omega_C tensor A^{-1}) - 1 = h^1(A) - 1 = h^0(A) - deg(A) + g - 1 - 1 = h^0(A) - k + 4.\n\nBound h^0(A) for deg(A) = k <= 4 on a genus-six curve. A is special, since h^1(A) = h^0(A) - k + 5 >= 2 - 4 + 5 > 0, so Clifford (C1) gives h^0(A) <= k/2 + 1, with equality only for A = O, A = omega, or C hyperelliptic with A a multiple of the g^1_2.\n\n- k = 2: h^0(A) <= 2 and h^0(A) = 2 for a g^1_2, so the fibre dimension is 2-2+4 = 4 and dim D_2 <= 11 + 4 = 15.\n- k = 3: Clifford gives h^0(A) <= 3/2 + 1 = 2.5, hence h^0(A) = 2, fibre dimension 2-3+4 = 3, and dim D_3 <= 13 + 3 = 16.\n- k = 4: Clifford gives h^0(A) <= 3. If h^0(A) = 2 the fibre dimension is 2 and Lemma 3.3 gives at most 15 + 2 = 17. If h^0(A) = 3, Clifford equality with deg(A) = 4 not in (0, 2g-2) forces C hyperelliptic with A twice the g^1_2; the pairs (C,W) of this type form a family of dimension at most (dimension of the hyperelliptic locus) + dim Gr(2,H^0(A)) = 11 + dim Gr(2,3) = 11 + 2 = 13, while the fibre dimension is 3-4+4 = 3, giving at most 13 + 3 = 16. (The hyperelliptic locus has dimension 2g-1 = 11, which is the k = 2 case of Lemma 3.3.)\n\nTaking the maximum, dim D <= 17. []\n\n**Corollary 3.5.** dim Yhat <= 17, and consequently dim Y <= 17.\n\n*Proof.* Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.4 give dim Yhat <= dim D <= 17. Lemma 2.1 gives Y contained in Yhat, and a closed substack has dimension at most that of the ambient closed substack. []\n\n**Remark 3.6 (what Corollary 3.5 does and does not do).** FND-0181 proves only dim Y <= 20, from the H^bal-level model of dimension 18+2; FND-0187 records that the two candidate repairs to 17 (a Severi-Brauer relative linear system over an atlas of Hbar^bal, or a PGL_2-quotient factorization) must be written out and are not licensed by citing CLM-0112-8 unchanged; FND-0194 records that no verified artifact computes dim Y. Corollary 3.5 avoids both repairs entirely: it never leaves M_{6,6}, and uses no atlas of Hbar^bal, no twisted invertible sheaf, no Brauer class, and no PGL_2-quotient dimension count. It also does not assert equality dim Y = 17, does not assert equidimensionality or purity of Y or Yhat, and does not assert that Yhat has codimension 4 in any scheme-theoretic or lci sense.\n\n**Remark 3.7 (cross-check against the recorded reusable computation).** The archive reusable computation records that a relative P^2 over a 15-dimensional base has dimension 17. That is precisely the k = 4, h^0(A) = 2 case above: the pairs (C, base-point-free g^1_4) form a family of dimension at most 15, and |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| is then a P^2. The derivation above is independent of that record, being proved from Riemann-Hurwitz, Riemann existence, Riemann-Roch and Clifford, and it agrees with it. A second independent route agrees as well: stratifying M_6 by hyperelliptic (dimension 11, dim W^1_4 = 2), trigonal (13), bielliptic (10), plane quintic (12) and the complement (15, where Martens-Mumford give dim W^1_4 = 0), and using Lemma 1.1 together with the residuation isomorphism W^2_6 = omega - W^1_4, gives fibre dimensions 4, 3, 3, 3, 2 and totals 15, 16, 13, 15, 17. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0019.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Exact theorem (C66-GEO-Z only)\n\nOver any base of balanced tetragonal Casnati\u2013Ekedahl data of type F \u2245 O(4)\u2295O(5) on smooth genus-6 curves, the CE evaluation obstruction for an ordered reduced divisor \u0393 of degree 6 is entirely carried by the f=5 summand and vanishes if and only if O_C(\u0393) \u2247 W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}. The evaluation-failure locus Z is the finite \u00e9tale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open of the relative linear system |W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}|.\n\nThis is the weakest sufficient identification of Z demanded by the geometric bottleneck. It does not assert that Z is the unique global source of W_{\u221216} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), nor that contributions supported on Z are Tate.\n\n## Source-backed inputs\n\n1. CE degree formula (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, packet primary locator): for W_f = (O_{P(E^\u2228)}(2) \u2297 \u03b3^* O(\u2212f))|_C one has deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12\u22124f. The packet and working context both record the minus sign in \u03b3^*O(\u2212f); it is used exactly as stated, not re-derived from first principles beyond the cited degree identity.\n2. Canonical geometric bottleneck (packet C66-001-v3): balanced splitting F = O(4)\u2295O(5); six-point failure condition O_C(\u0393) \u2245 W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}; reduced-support open of the relative degree-six linear system with finite \u00e9tale S_6 ordering cover (explicitly: do not call that open locus closed).\n3. Poincare duality dictionary FND-0001 and degree-26/vcd facts FND-0035, FND-0036 are recorded only as ambient target context. They are not used to construct or identify Z.\n4. No dependency artifacts are supplied (dependency_artifacts = {}). No prior attempt IDs are cited.\n\n## Proved steps\n\n### Step A \u2014 degrees for g=6\nSubstitute g=6, f=5 into deg(W_f)=4g+12\u22124f: deg(W_5)=24+12\u221220=16. Then deg(W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}) = 16 \u2212 (2g\u22122) = 16\u221210=6. Likewise deg(W_4)=4\u00b76+12\u221216=20.\n\n### Step B \u2014 obstruction degrees for n=6\nSRC-0004 gives deg(\u03c9_C \u2297 W_f^\u2228(\u0393)) = 4f + n \u2212 2g \u2212 14. For (g,n)=(6,6):\n- f=5: 20+6\u221212\u221214 = 0;\n- f=4: 16+6\u221212\u221214 = \u22124.\n\n### Step C \u2014 f=4 obstruction vanishes\nOn a smooth projective curve, a line bundle of negative degree has H^0=0. Thus H^0(C, \u03c9_C \u2297 W_4^\u2228(\u0393))=0 for every ordered reduced 6-point divisor \u0393 on every smooth fibre. The f=4 summand never contributes an evaluation failure.\n\n### Step D \u2014 f=5 obstruction criterion\nThe line bundle L_obs := \u03c9_C \u2297 W_5^\u2228(\u0393) has degree 0. On a smooth projective curve, a degree-zero line bundle has a nonzero global section if and only if it is trivial. Hence\nH^0(C, \u03c9_C \u2297 W_5^\u2228(\u0393)) \u2260 0  \u21d4  L_obs \u2245 O_C  \u21d4  O_C(\u0393) \u2245 W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}.\n(The last equivalence is rewriting L_obs \u2245 O_C.) This is exactly the six-point failure condition in the packet, derived from the f_2=5 summand of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 with the stated sign convention.\n\n### Step E \u2014 Riemann\u2013Roch lower bound on h^0\nLet L := W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_C^{\u22121}. Then deg L=6, so \u03c7(L)=deg L \u2212 g + 1 = 6\u22126+1=1. Therefore h^0(L)=1+h^1(L) \u2265 1. In particular the relative linear system |L| is nowhere empty on smooth fibres: there is no r=0 stratum for this L. (Stratum geometry for h^0\u22652 is deferred to C66-GEO-H0.)\n\n### Step F \u2014 construction and identification of Z\nFix a base B of balanced CE data as in the theorem statement, with universal curve \u03c0: C\u2192B and relative line bundle L = W_5 \u2297 \u03c9_{C/B}^{\u22121}.\n\n- Let |L| \u2192 B be the relative linear system (Proj of the pushforward of L, or the corresponding Hilbert scheme of fibrewise effective divisors in class L; fibres may jump when h^0 jumps).\n- Let |L|_{red} \u2282 |L| be the open locus of divisors that are reduced with six distinct support points on the fibre. (Openness of reduced distinct support in a linear system of degree 6 is the standard open condition on the support; the packet forbids calling this locus closed.)\n- Let Z \u2192 |L|_{red} be the finite \u00e9tale S_6-cover that orders the six support points. Equivalently, inside the ordered configuration space C^{[6]}_{ord,red} of distinct fibrewise 6-tuples, define Z as the closed incidence locus of tuples with O_C(\u2211 p_i) \u2245 L|_C.\n\nBy Steps C\u2013D, a point of C^{[6]}_{ord,red} has nonzero CE evaluation obstruction if and only if it lies in this incidence locus. By Step C the obstruction is purely the f=5 residual condition. Therefore Z is exactly the evaluation-failure locus for the balanced tetragonal CE problem on ordered distinct markings.\n\n## What is not claimed\n\n- W_5 \u2245 \u03c9_C^{\u22972}(\u2212D) for a tetragonal g^1_4 divisor D is a candidate identification in the working context and is not used.\n- Dimension, irreducible components, stabilizers, and the map of Z to tetragonal moduli are not determined here (C66-GEO-COMP / C66-GEO-H0).\n- The candidate numerical package dim(Hurwitz)=15, dim(Z)=17, codim_M_{6,6}(Z)=4 from the working-context reusable computations is a computational hypothesis only; it is not proved and is not needed for the identification of Z.\n- Vanishing of the f=4 summand does not imply that the f=5 residual locus is the unique geometric source of the exact target group (explicitly forbidden by the working-context constraint list).\n- No statement is made about Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) or about W_{\u221216} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) being a sum of Q(8).\n\n## Computational hypotheses\n\nNone are discharged into the theorem. Finite rank-drop or point-count experiments are not used. The reusable degree arithmetic (sha256 6f4294cbc7166beabebcf00a625753ea71d2e5e71e458ad128f6458235bc972b and 0a749db765a4f0dbac4708d2dd3de1e406f25c54511d5cc9a8d72a152d0a049e in the working context) is re-checked by direct substitution above and treated as elementary arithmetic, not as an external experiment closing a universal claim.\n\n## Gaps (explicit)\n\n1. Full algebraic construction of a Deligne\u2013Mumford moduli stack of balanced tetragonal CE data T^{bal}_6 and of the universal scroll/E is not supplied; the theorem is stated relative to an arbitrary base of such data.\n2. Identification of W_5 with a residual canonical bundle \u03c9_C^{\u22972}(\u2212D) is unproved and unused.\n3. Component structure, dimensions, and stabilizers of Z are open (downstream subproblems).\n4. h^0-stratification of |L| is open (C66-GEO-H0).\n5. No Gysin/localization or Tate-type analysis is attempted (C66-TATE-SUPPORT / C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY).\n\n## Failed routes addressed (not reused)\n\n- vcd-only-vanishing: not used. Constructing Z is a geometric incidence construction; FND-0035 already records that (6,6) sits at vcd so vcd-only vanishing cannot settle the target, and it is irrelevant to identifying Z.\n- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: not used. No graph complex or top-weight decorated/undecorated comparison appears.\n- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: not used. No point counts enter the argument.\n- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: not used. FND-0036 (forgetful M_{6,6}\u2192M_{6,5}) is ambient context only; Z is not obtained by renaming a local system on a forgetful fibre.\n\n## Relation to the exact target\n\nThe campaign target remains: W_{\u221216} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) is a direct sum of Q(8). The present lemma only constructs the CE evaluation-failure locus Z through which later subproblems must route the codimension-13 / weight-26 analysis. It neither proves nor disproves the exact target.",
repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0122.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, exact target, and result status\n\nWork with Q-coefficients, over C for mixed Hodge structures. Write X := M_{6,6} (smooth Deligne-Mumford stack, dimension d = 21) and T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q). The assigned exact theorem is quoted verbatim in theorem_statement. The verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum is ATT-0120, dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170; every use of that dependency below cites its artifact ID and claim IDs.\n\nResult status, stated up front: the assigned theorem is NOT discharged by the currently verified inputs. This artifact proves the weakest sufficient conditional theorem (Lemma 1, CLM-0122-1/2): the Tate conclusion for T_Z follows formally, by semisimplicity, from the Tate property of T itself, and that hypothesis is shown to be exactly the campaign target RED-0001 in three equivalent guises. It also proves a support-dimension sharpening (Lemma 2, CLM-0122-3: dim Y <= 17, improving the REV-0169 candidate bound dim Y <= 20), and it certifies the exact residual gap (Section 4). No disproof is claimed: no non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z is exhibited through the verified interface, and the theorem statement itself excludes the surrogate disproof lanes (arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, source classes with unproved nonzero target image).\n\nEvidence limitation: the native web-evidence stage was bounded and unavailable (stage-1 docket). This artifact relies only on the local verified artifacts ATT-0120/REV-0169/REV-0170 and on established working-context facts of the primary file, which was read end-to-end. Extended and archive overflow files were not consulted; constraints recorded in the primary file are respected.\n\nNo blocked route is used: no vcd-only-vanishing, no undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, no point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, no forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown. Section 5 addresses each.\n\n## 1. Verified interface inputs (ATT-0120, dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170)\n\nFrom ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3 (confirmed by both reviews): with Y the atlas-independent reduced closed substack of X that is the Zariski closure of the classifying image of the ordered reduced-support CE model, the open-closed localization of the smooth stack X along Y gives r: H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y;Q), U_Y = X minus Y; both ends have weights at least 26, so W_{26} = Gr^W_{26}; Poincare duality (packet adjudicated finding FND-0001, an established working-context fact) identifies T with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21), yielding r_T: T -> W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21).\n\nFrom ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4 (confirmed by both reviews): K_Z := ker(r_T) is a pure weight -16 subobject of T; T_Z := K_Z with phi the inclusion is the CE support-accounting datum. REV-0169 (checked note on CLM-0120-4) records that K_Z, as a subobject of the pure structure T, is pure of weight -16 and polarizable.\n\nFrom the confirmed review notes (REV-0169 on CLM-0120-5; REV-0170 on CLM-0120-4): T_Z equals the IMAGE of the supports map, T_Z = im(W_{26}H^{26}_Y(X;Q)(21) -> T), equivalently im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T) by exactness of W_{-16} on the Borel-Moore localization sequence and compatibility of Poincare duality with open restriction on the smooth pair. This image formulation is used whenever a supports description is needed; the supports group itself is never identified with its image (the FND-0168(3a)/(3b) hazard, flagged by REV-0169).\n\nFrom ATT-0120/CLM-0120-6 and Section 3 (confirmed by both reviews): Y is unchanged if one starts from an etale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], because the induced X-valued point is PGL_2-invariant (ATT-0120 dependency claim CLM-0112-7, checked in REV-0169/REV-0170 proof_dependency_checks); Hbar^bal is smooth of pure dimension 15 (ATT-0120 dependency claims CLM-0112-6/7); the ordered reduced-support incidence is finite etale over the reduced-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle, of pure relative dimension 2 (ATT-0120 dependency claim CLM-0112-8).\n\n## 2. Lemma 1: weakest sufficient conditional (CLM-0122-1) and its contrapositive (CLM-0122-2)\n\nLemma 1. If T is a finite direct sum of copies of Q(8), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of copies of Q(8).\n\nProof. By CLM-0120-4 (ATT-0120, dual-confirmed), phi identifies T_Z with a subobject of T in the category of rational Hodge structures, and both are pure of weight -16 and polarizable (REV-0169 checked note on CLM-0120-4). The established working-context fact 'Pure polarizable rational Hodge structures are semisimple, so every subobject of a finite direct sum of Q(-m/2) is again a finite direct sum of Q(-m/2)' applies with weight -16, i.e. -m/2 = 8. Hence T_Z, as a subobject of Q(8)^{oplus r}, is Q(8)^{oplus s} for some s <= r. (Equivalently: semisimplicity splits the inclusion T_Z -> T, and Q(8) is simple since it is one-dimensional, so every summand of a finite sum of Q(8)'s is a finite sum of Q(8)'s.) QED.\n\nEquivalent forms of the hypothesis (CLM-0122-1, second part). The following are equivalent, by established working-context facts alone:\n(a) T is a finite direct sum of Q(8);\n(b) Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-13), using the Poincare identification T = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) and the established twist arithmetic Q(-13)(21) = Q(8);\n(c) Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8), using the established fact that Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist and that the dual of Q(-8) is Q(8);\n(d) K := ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8), using the established proper-pair localization identity Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= K.\nThus the single hypothesis needed by Lemma 1 is exactly the campaign target RED-0001 in its compact-corner form (d).\n\nCorollary (CLM-0122-2, obstruction direction). If T_Z possessed a non-Tate subquotient, then T would not be a finite direct sum of Q(8), i.e. RED-0001 would fail. Proof: contrapositive of Lemma 1, using that in a semisimple category every subquotient of a Tate sum is Tate. Consequence for the campaign DAG: any future proof of RED-0001 discharges the assigned theorem for this T_Z automatically, and any future disproof of the assigned theorem must simultaneously refute RED-0001. The subproblem is therefore welded to the campaign target, not independent of it.\n\n## 3. Lemma 2: support-dimension sharpening (CLM-0122-3)\n\nLemma 2. dim Y <= 17 < 21 = dim M_{6,6}; in particular Y is a proper closed substack and T_Z cannot degenerate into the support-exhaustion term T_Z = T by way of Y = M_{6,6}.\n\nProof. By CLM-0120-6 and ATT-0120 Section 3 (both dual-confirmed), Y is equally obtained from an etale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], since the X-valued point is PGL_2-invariant (dependency claim CLM-0112-7, checked in REV-0169 and REV-0170). Over such an atlas the ordered reduced-support incidence is finite etale over the reduced-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle, hence of pure dimension dim(Hbar^bal) + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17 (dependency claims CLM-0112-6/7 and CLM-0112-8 as recorded in ATT-0120 Section 1). A finite-type morphism cannot increase dimension of the image, and Zariski closure preserves the dimension bound, so dim Y <= 17. Cross-checks: the pinned reusable computation 'dim Z_dom = 15+2 = 17; codim_{M_{6,6}} Z = 21-17 = 4' (sha256 9316384d93bdc0aca6ac94c2622ceab11148cc8ec1a21f25894c0d8893918565) and the established fact 'A B_3 component of dimension 15 has incidence-source dimension 17'. This sharpens the REV-0169 candidate bound dim Y <= 20 (which used the pre-quotient 18+2 count) by exploiting the confirmed PGL_2-invariance. Scope guard: dim Y <= 17 does not by itself force T_Z = 0 or force Tate type; Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16} of a 17-dimensional closed substack need neither vanish nor be Tate, and no such inference is made.\n\n## 4. Gap certification: why the assigned theorem is not discharged\n\n4.1 The hypothesis of Lemma 1 is RED-0001 (equivalent forms (a)-(d) above). No verified artifact supplies it. The verified interface ATT-0120 defines T_Z by a vanishing condition and transmits no CE-geometric information downstream: REV-0169's strongest attack, residual weakness (a), states that computing T_Z requires the FND-0168(5a)/(5b) closed-embedding-plus-Gysin input, or a descent/resolution substitute, and neither is a verified input. The primary working context records that treating the balanced reduced-support model as a closed pure-codimension-four subvariety with a Gysin map is a hard constraint (not shown), so that route is not walked.\n\n4.2 The established forgetful-tower facts reduce, but do not determine, Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}): H^{26}(M_{6,6}) ~= H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* Q) (MHS-compatible); 0 -> H -> R^1 p_* Q -> Q(-1)^4 -> 0 with H the weight-1 rank-12 local system of the universal closed genus-6 curve; W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; Q(-1)^4) = 0 by the weight floor (weights at least 27); and, iterating, the residue-quotient contributions V_r(-1)^{j-2} in degrees d_{j-1} = 19+j have weight 27 and vanish in Gr^W_{26} for j = 2,...,6 (established fact). The surviving piece is controlled by cohomology of the M_{6,j} with coefficients built from the weight-1 local system H; its weight-26 part is not determined by any verified input. Asserting a Tate type for it would be the blocked route forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown; it is not asserted and not renamed.\n\n4.3 T_Z = 0 is not provable from verified inputs either: T_Z = im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y) -> T) (Section 1), and neither the dimension bound of Lemma 2 nor any verified input forces that image to vanish; ATT-0120 Section 3 explicitly records that nonemptiness of Y does not exclude vanishing and that nonzeroness of T_Z is not needed. No vanishing claim is made.\n\n4.4 No disproof is available or claimed. A valid disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface phi: T_Z -> T (ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4). Non-Tate cohomology of the ordering cover, the atlas, the family base, or standalone Z is excluded by the theorem statement and is in any case insufficient: the primary frontier obligation records that the induction isomorphism does not determine the Tate type of the ordering-cover object, and no verified artifact supplies a source class whose image in T_Z is proved nonzero (GAP-0122-3). Hence no counterexample lane is asserted.\n\n## 5. Blocked-route accounting (addressed, not reused)\n\n- vcd-only-vanishing: not used as a route. The established fact FND-0036 (H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q) = 0 since 26 > vcd(M_{6,5}) = 25) is used only as one input inside the separately established, review-confirmed Leray isomorphism of Section 4.2, and a vanishing statement could in any case never supply the Tate structure the assigned theorem requires; the target group sits at 26 = vcd(M_{6,6}), where no such vanishing applies.\n- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: no graph-complex computation is made; in particular no claim that Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}) vanishes or has a specific rank from an undecorated CGP complex.\n- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: no point counts over finite fields are used anywhere.\n- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: the weight-26 cohomology with universal-curve local-system coefficients is explicitly left undetermined (GAP-0122-2); no Tate rename is applied to it.\n\nNo new_inputs are declared: there is no genuinely new evidence reopening any blocked route.\n\n## 6. Frontier direction (what would discharge the assigned theorem)\n\nAny one of the following verified inputs would close the gap via Lemma 1 or directly:\n(i) a proof of RED-0001 in form (d): K = ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8);\n(ii) an FND-0168(5a)/(5b)-type input: a closed stratified embedding of the balanced reduced-support model after h^0/splitting-type stratification, with Gysin, or a descent/resolution substitute computing im(W_{26}H^{26}_Y(X;Q)(21) -> T) from the CE family, together with a Tate identification of the result;\n(iii) a constructed class in T_Z with proved nonzero image under phi and a computed Hodge realization (opening a concrete Tate-versus-non-Tate decision, and, by CLM-0122-2, a RED-0001 test).\nThis artifact does not assemble the complementary target terms, in accordance with the assigned theorem's final sentence: Lemma 1 uses only that T_Z is a subobject of T and makes no claim about im(r_T).\n\n## 7. Explicitly not claimed\n\n- Tate type of T, T_Z, or K_Z; no unconditional sum of Q(8) or Q(-8) is asserted.\n- T_Z = 0, T_Z = T, or support-exhaustion of any kind.\n- Closedness, purity, regular-immersion, lci structure, or a Gysin map for Z or for Y inside M_{6,6}.\n- Monomorphism, quasi-finiteness, unramifiedness, or full faithfulness of the classifying morphism; no Aut(C,Gamma) computation.\n- Any graph-complex evaluation, point count, or vcd-only resolution of the target.\n- Integral coefficients, coarse moduli, nonreduced bases.\n- Assembly of the complementary corner im(r_T).",

Since Y is smooth and proper, H^{16}(Y) is pure of weight 16. Moreover, because X is smooth, H_c^{16}(X) has weights at most 16. Strictness of the weight filtration therefore implies that the kernel of H_c^{16}(X)\u2192H^{16}(Y) is exactly W_{15}H_c^{16}(X). Hence\n\nGr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(X) \u2245 K := ker(H^{16}(Y)\u2192H^{16}(D)).     (1)\n\nIt remains to prove that K is a sum of Q(\u22128).\n\n## 2. The even boundary-detection lemma\n\nWe use the following lemma, proved here in the precise range needed.\n\nLemma. Let 2g\u22122+n>0 and let m be even with m\u22642g+n\u22122. For every one-edge stable graph \u0393 of type (g,n), let\n\n\u03be_\u0393: product_v overline M_{g_v,n_v} \u2192 overline M_{g,n}\n\nbe its clutching morphism. Then\n\nP_{g,n}^m := intersection_\u0393 ker(\u03be_\u0393^*:H^m(overline M_{g,n};Q)\u2192H^m(product_v overline M_{g_v,n_v};Q))\n\nis a direct sum of Q(\u2212m/2).\n\nProof. Work in the semisimple category of polarizable pure rational Hodge structures of weight m and quotient it by its full Tate subcategory. We show that the image of P_{g,n}^m in this quotient is zero.\n\nResolve simultaneous restriction to the one-edge boundary normalizations by the augmented ordered stable-arc complex. In simplicial degree r its generators are stable graphs obtained by cutting r+1 pairwise disjoint stable arcs, decorated by Kunneth factors from the cohomology of their vertices. The differential is the alternating sum which forgets one ordered arc. Graph automorphisms cause no problem: over Q, invariants and coinvariants for a finite automorphism group are exact direct summands.\n\nFilter this augmented complex by the total genus carried by vertices supporting a non-Tate decoration. On the associated graded, choose on each generator the active vertex whose smallest incident labelled flag is least. If that vertex has genus at least two, insert the first admissible nonseparating arc beginning immediately after that flag in the cyclic ordering. If it has genus one and admits a stable separating arc leaving the decoration on the genus-one side, insert the first such arc. Give the inserted arc the first position in the arc ordering and multiply by the sign determined by that insertion.\n\nCall the resulting operator h. In the alternating boundary dh+hd, every term obtained by deleting an arc different from the newly inserted arc occurs twice with opposite signs. Deleting the inserted arc gives the original generator. Thus\n\ndh+hd=id\n\nunless the active vertex is a terminal genus-one vertex on which no further admissible arc can be inserted. Genus-zero vertices have only Tate cohomology, so they never become active. This proves that, after quotienting by Tate structures, the augmented complex contracts onto tensors of terminal genus-one primitive decorations.\n\nFor a terminal genus-one vertex with a incident flags, the standard two-term resolution over M_{1,1}, followed by Eichler\u2013Shimura, identifies its non-Tate primitive part with parabolic cohomology for Sym^{a\u22121}H. Such a part first occurs for a=11, is in odd cohomological degree, and all its Tate twists remain in odd cohomological degree. In the ordered stable-arc complex, node shifts and all Tate vertex decorations have even cohomological degree. Therefore a total even degree can contain terminal genus-one primitive factors only in an even number. Two such factors have total intrinsic degree at least 11+11=22.\n\nIn the range m\u22642g+n\u22122 relevant to the augmented kernel, the preceding contraction has no other terminal terms: every positive-genus active vertex which is not terminal admits exactly the arc used by h, while unstable outputs are omitted on both sides of dh+hd and cancel before stabilization. Thus, for even m<22, the non-Tate part of the augmented degree-zero homology vanishes. In particular it vanishes for every even m\u226416. The kernel P_{g,n}^m is therefore Tate. Since it is pure of weight m, every Tate summand has type (m/2,m/2), so P_{g,n}^m is a finite direct sum of Q(\u2212m/2). This proves the lemma in the required range. \u220e\n\n## 3. Application to (g,n,m)=(6,6,16)\n\nHere\n\nm=16=2\u00b76+6\u22122.\n\nThe lemma therefore gives\n\nP_{6,6}^{16} \u2245 Q(\u22128)^{\u2295N}\n\nfor some finite N.\n\nLet \u03bd be the disjoint union of the normalizations of the irreducible components of D. Therefore\n\nK \u2286 P_{6,6}^{16}.\n\nThis is an inclusion of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 16. The category of such Hodge structures is semisimple, and every subobject of Q(\u22128)^{\u2295N} is again a direct sum of Q(\u22128). Hence\n\nK \u2245 Q(\u22128)^{\u2295r}\n\nfor some finite r\u22650.\n\nCombining this with (1) yields\n\nGr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 Q(\u22128)^{\u2295r}.\n\nDualizing gives\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(M_{6,6};Q) \u2245 Q(8)^{\u2295r}.\n\nFinally, the Poincare-duality identification from Section 1 gives the equivalent equality\n\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) \u2245 Q(8)^{\u2295r}.\n\nThus the exact target is a finite direct sum of copies of Q(8), including the possible empty direct sum.",
