What this node owes, and what is actually delivered\n\nC66-GEO-COMP asks for four things: components, dimensions, stabilizers, and finite-cover behavior. The dependency package fixes the objects precisely, so the honest task is to compute what those inputs determine and to say plainly where the determination stops. Two adjudicated findings set the bar. FND-0060 records that the count dim H^{tet,bal}_6 = b-3 = 15 is a **coarse** count for branched covers modulo Aut(P^1), and that promoting it to a stack dimension and to a codimension inside M_{6,6} requires a stabilizer/automorphism analysis that ATT-0022 omitted. FND-0086 records that a dominant dimension count plus named exceptional loci is **not** an exhaustive component/stabilizer/closure/codimension analysis of Z. This attempt does the stack-level upgrade FND-0060 asks for, does the component **reduction** FND-0086 makes necessary, and does not pretend to the exhaustive closure analysis FND-0086 says is still missing.\n\nDependency artifacts used, with the confirmations required by the execution contract:\n\n- **ATT-0065** (C66-GEO-Z), confirmed by **REV-0108** and **REV-0109**. Used for: the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with fibrewise degrees 20 and 16 at (g,n)=(6,6) (CLM-0065-5, confirmed in both reviews); the scheme-theoretic identity Fit_0(coker phi) = a_N^* I_e and hence the identification of the evaluation-failure scheme with relative triviality of N = omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) (CLM-0065-4, CLM-0065-9); and the balanced vanishing R^1 s_* End(F) = 0 (CLM-0065-8) which makes the ambient and intrinsic failure schemes agree.\n- **ATT-0066** (C66-GEO-H0), confirmed by **REV-0110** and **REV-0116**. Used for: h^0(L_b) in {3,4} with the stratification H = H_3 sqcup H_4, H_4 closed and inside the non-primitive hyperelliptic locus (CLM-0066-2, CLM-0066-3); the P^{k-1}-bundle model of the linear system on each **reduced** stratum (CLM-0066-4); the global Abel-Jacobi incidence I = Hilb^6 x_{Pic^6} B as the correct model across the jump (CLM-0066-5, matching FND-0107); and the stack-level S_6-torsor tilde-I -> I^dist together with the scheme-theoretic equality tilde-I = Z_ev on Conf_6 (CLM-0066-6).\n\nI carry ATT-0066's normalization hypothesis in exactly the weak FND-0105 form in which ATT-0066 carries it, as a **hypothesis of my theorem**, not as an established fact. FND-0105 explicitly records that relabelling this gap as an established working-context fact (as ATT-0057 did) is the thing not to do.\n\n## 1. The Hurwitz stack: smoothness, dimension 15, finite stabilizers\n\nLet H^{4,6} be the stack whose objects over a k-scheme T are pairs (C -> T, gamma: C -> P, P -> T a Brauer-Severi/P^1-bundle) with C -> T smooth proper genus 6 and gamma finite flat of degree 4, and let H be the open substack where the CE relations bundle is fibrewise O(4)+O(5). I first record why H is a DM stack of dimension 15 with finite automorphism groups, which is the stack-level statement FND-0060 asks for.\n\n**1.1 Deformation theory.** For gamma: C -> P^1 finite flat of degree 4 with C smooth of genus g, simply-branched or not, the deformation theory of the pair relative to the target modulo PGL_2 is governed by the normal complex. Since gamma is finite and flat with C and P^1 smooth of dimension one, gamma is a local complete intersection morphism and the cotangent complex L_gamma is concentrated in degree 0, equal to the coherent sheaf Omega_gamma = coker(gamma^* Omega_{P^1} -> Omega_C), which for a separable degree-4 cover is the ramification module, a torsion sheaf of length equal to the degree b of the branch divisor. By Riemann-Hurwitz, 2g-2 = 4(-2) + b, so b = 2g+6 = 18 at g=6.\n\nThe standard Hurwitz deformation argument: deformations of the pair (C,gamma) with the target **fixed** are governed by H^0(C, N_gamma) with obstructions in H^1(C, N_gamma), where N_gamma = Omega_gamma is the torsion ramification sheaf (for a finite morphism to a curve, the normal sheaf of the map is this torsion sheaf). Since N_gamma is torsion on a curve, H^1(C,N_gamma) = 0, so deformations are unobstructed and the space of first-order deformations with fixed target has dimension h^0(N_gamma) = length(N_gamma) = b = 18. Allowing the target P^1 to move contributes nothing new (P^1 is rigid), and quotienting by the 3-dimensional PGL_2 = Aut(P^1) gives\n\n  dim H = b - 3 = 18 - 3 = 15.  (1.1)\n\nUnobstructedness (H^1 = 0) gives **smoothness** of the stack, not merely the dimension count. Equivalently, in the classical simply-branched picture the Hurwitz space is finite etale over the configuration space of b unordered branch points in P^1, of dimension b, and the PGL_2-quotient has dimension b-3; but the deformation-theoretic form above is what proves smoothness and applies verbatim to the non-simply-branched locus, which is why I use it. Note 2g+2d-5 = 12+8-5 = 15 agrees with (1.1).\n\n**1.2 Balancedness is open.** The condition F_b ~= O(4)+O(5) on the rank-2 relations bundle is the condition h^1(P^1, F_b(-5)) = 0 together with the fixed determinant deg F = g+3 = 9 (recorded independently in the REV-0116 cross-check FC-W5-CONVENTION-ARITHMETIC-INVARIANT: deg F = g+3 = 9 = 4+5, so 'balanced' can only mean O(4)+O(5) at g=6). Semicontinuity makes the vanishing an open condition on the base, so H is an **open** substack of H^{4,6} and inherits smoothness and dimension 15. This is the only use I make of openness of balancedness; FND-0098 correctly warns that openness of the balanced stratum supplies no injectivity into M_{6,6}, and I do not use it for that.\n\n**1.3 Finite stabilizers.** An automorphism of the object (C,gamma) over an algebraically closed field is a pair (sigma,tau) with sigma in Aut(C), tau in PGL_2, gamma o sigma = tau o gamma. Since g = 6 >= 2, Aut(C) is finite; and tau is determined by sigma because gamma is surjective. Hence Aut(C,gamma) injects into Aut(C) and is finite, so H is a Deligne-Mumford stack with finite (indeed generically trivial, since a general tetragonal genus-6 curve has no automorphisms) stabilizers. This is precisely the stack-level upgrade of the coarse count that FND-0060 demanded; note that it establishes dim H = 15 **as a stack**, since a finite-stabilizer DM stack has the same dimension as its coarse space.\n\n## 2. The failure locus over each stratum: dimensions and smoothness\n\nBy ATT-0066/CLM-0066-3 (confirmed REV-0110, REV-0116), the function b |-> h^0(L_b) takes only the values 3 and 4 on H; H_4 = {h^0(L) >= 4} is closed in the underlying topological space and H_3 is its open complement; and H_4 is contained in the locus of hyperelliptic fibres on which gamma_b is **non-primitive**, factoring as gamma = q o h through the hyperelliptic double cover. Two immediate consequences, both proved:\n\n**2.1** H^prim (primitive gamma) is contained in H_3. Contrapositive of the containment just quoted: a point of H_4 has non-primitive gamma.\n\n**2.2** Over the reduced stratum H_k, ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4 and (H3) give I|_{H_k} ~= P((pi_* L|_{H_k})^vee), a Zariski-locally trivial P^{k-1}-bundle. Hence I|_{H_k} -> H_k is smooth proper of relative dimension k-1, and\n\n  dim I|_{H_3} = dim H_3 + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17,  dim I|_{H_4} = dim H_4 + 3.  (2.1)\n\nThe first equality uses dim H_3 = 15, which holds because H_3 is a nonempty open substack of the equidimensional 15-dimensional H \u2014 nonempty provided H^prim is nonempty, which holds because a general balanced tetragonal genus-6 curve is not hyperelliptic (a hyperelliptic curve's g^1_4's are all of the form h^*(pencil), i.e. non-primitive, and a general genus-6 curve is non-hyperelliptic and carries five g^1_4's). The second equality is a **conditional** statement: it says nothing until dim H_4 is bounded, and I do not bound it here.\n\n**2.3 Equidimensionality over H_3.** Since I|_{H_3} -> H_3 is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over an equidimensional 15-dimensional base, I|_{H_3} is equidimensional of dimension 17, and it is **smooth** wherever H_3 is smooth \u2014 which is everywhere, by 1.1. So I|_{H_3} is a smooth equidimensional 17-dimensional DM stack.\n\nI emphasize what 2.2 does **not** give. The reducedness restriction in ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4 is load-bearing (REV-0116 records exactly this in FC-H0-NONREDUCED-GRAUERT: fibrewise constancy of h^0 does not give local freeness of pi_* L over a non-reduced base). Since H is smooth, hence reduced, the restriction is harmless **here**, and I record that as the reason it is harmless rather than ignoring it: H_3 with its reduced (= its natural open) structure is the same stack, so Grauert applies on the nose. Over a general non-reduced base it would not, and no downstream node may drop the hypothesis.\n\n## 3. Components: the correct reduction, and why it is a reduction and not a theorem\n\n**3.1 Bijection of components.** Let X -> Y be a Zariski-locally trivial P^m-bundle of Noetherian stacks. Then the map V |-> preimage of V is a bijection from irreducible components of Y to irreducible components of X, with dim (preimage) = dim V + m. Proof: the preimage of an irreducible V is irreducible because it is covered by opens V_i x P^m with V_i irreducible open dense in V and pairwise intersecting, and a union of irreducible opens with pairwise nonempty intersections is irreducible; surjectivity and injectivity of the correspondence follow since the bundle map is open, surjective, and has irreducible fibres.\n\nApplying this to I|_{H_3} -> H_3 with m = 2:\n\n  #{components of I|_{H_3}} = #{components of H_3}, each of dimension 17.  (3.1)\n\n**3.2 The honest statement.** (3.1) says the component structure of the failure model over the open stratum is **exactly** the component structure of the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz stack; nothing more, nothing less. In particular:\n\n- Irreducibility of I|_{H_3} is **equivalent** to irreducibility of H_3, not an additional geometric fact one could hope to prove by studying divisors.\n- I do **not** assert that H, H_3, or I is irreducible. Irreducibility of Hurwitz spaces of primitive degree-d covers with simple branching is classical (Clebsch/Hurwitz for the simply-branched primitive case), but H is the **balanced** locus, an open substack cut out by a bundle-splitting condition, and its irreducibility does not follow formally from irreducibility of an ambient Hurwitz space unless one knows the balanced locus is dense in each component \u2014 which is a statement about the CE splitting stratification I have not proved and do not assume. This is exactly the sort of gap FND-0086 says must be identified rather than papered over, so I record it as GAP-COMP-IRRED below rather than asserting a component count.\n\n**3.3 Components over H_4.** Any irreducible component of I lying entirely over H_4 has dimension dim H_4 + 3 by 2.2. Since GAP-H0-1 (emptiness of H_4) is open \u2014 ATT-0066 explicitly declines to claim it, and both REV-0110 and REV-0116 confirm the decline \u2014 I cannot rule such components out, nor bound their dimension, without bounding dim H_4. What I can say unconditionally: H_4 is contained in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus, and its closure is a **proper closed** substack of H unless H_4 = H, which is excluded by 2.2's nonemptiness remark (H^prim is nonempty and contained in H_3). Hence dim H_4 <= 14 **if** H_4 is contained in a proper closed substack of the equidimensional smooth 15-dimensional H, which it is, since H_3 is a nonempty open. Therefore\n\n  dim I|_{H_4} = dim H_4 + 3 <= 14 + 3 = 17,  (3.2)\n\nso **no component of I over H_4 exceeds dimension 17**, and I is of dimension exactly 17 overall, equidimensional over H_3 and of dimension <= 17 over H_4. This is a genuine unconditional consequence and is the strongest component statement the dependency package supports. It does **not** say I is equidimensional (a 17-dimensional component over H_4 would require dim H_4 = 14 exactly, which is not excluded), and it does not say I is irreducible.\n\n## 4. Finite-cover behavior: the ordered model and its stabilizers\n\n**4.1 The torsor.** By ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6 (confirmed REV-0110, REV-0116), and consistently with FND-0064 and FND-0075, tilde-I = Conf_6(C/H) x_{Hilb^6} I -> I^dist is a finite etale S_6-torsor **at stack level**, with neither side artificially reduced (FND-0087). Consequences, all formal:\n\n- dim tilde-I = dim I^dist. Combining with Section 2-3: tilde-I has dimension 17, is smooth and equidimensional of dimension 17 over H_3, and has no component of dimension > 17.\n- Components of tilde-I lie over components of I^dist; S_6 acts on the set of components of tilde-I over a fixed component of I^dist, transitively, and the number of components of tilde-I over a given irreducible component V of I^dist is the index [S_6 : Im(pi_1^{et}(V) -> S_6)] of the geometric monodromy image. **I do not compute this monodromy**; determining it is exactly the input a downstream C66-TATE-SUPPORT or C66-CEX-LOCAL node would need, and FND-0053 already records that rationality of S_6-representations does **not** by itself force Tate local systems on such a cover. I therefore flag the monodromy as an open input rather than assuming it is full or trivial.\n- Rationally, S_6-invariants and coinvariants agree, so descent of Q-cohomology from tilde-I to I^dist is harmless (FND-0075); integrally or on coarse spaces it is not, and no such descent is claimed.\n\n**4.2 Stabilizers on the ordered model.** A point of tilde-I over an algebraically closed field is (C, gamma, x_1,...,x_6) with the x_i pairwise distinct, sum x_i = Gamma, and O_C(Gamma) ~= L. Its automorphism group in the stack tilde-I is\n\n  Aut(C,gamma,x_1,...,x_6) = {sigma in Aut(C) : exists tau in PGL_2 with gamma o sigma = tau o gamma, and sigma(x_i) = x_i for all i}.  (4.1)\n\nThis is a subgroup of the finite group Aut(C,gamma) of 1.3, hence finite; tilde-I is a DM stack.\n\n**4.3 What I can prove about (4.1), and what I cannot.** Let sigma be in the group (4.1) and suppose first that the induced tau is the identity, i.e. gamma o sigma = gamma. Then sigma lies in the deck group of the degree-4 cover gamma. If sigma is nontrivial, the quotient map C -> C/<sigma> factors gamma, so gamma is non-primitive of degree 4 and <sigma> has order 2 or 4. In either case sigma has finitely many fixed points, and sigma fixes each x_i; a nontrivial automorphism sigma of order m of a genus-6 curve has, by Riemann-Hurwitz applied to C -> C/<sigma>, at most 2g/(m-1) + 2 <= 14 fixed points for m = 2, so six fixed points is **not** by itself a contradiction. However, on the deck group of a **fibrewise** degree-4 map, the six points x_1,...,x_6 are fixed by sigma and lie in fibres of gamma; a nontrivial deck transformation acts freely outside the ramification of gamma, so all six x_i would be ramification points of gamma fixed by sigma. That is possible in principle, so I do **not** conclude triviality unconditionally; what I do conclude is: **if the six marked points are not all ramification points of gamma, then the tau = id part of (4.1) is trivial.** Since the distinct-support open is what the campaign uses and the generic point of each 17-dimensional component over H_3 has all six x_i unramified (the ramification divisor of gamma has degree 18 and imposes a proper closed condition on the P^2 of divisors in |L| over each point of H_3, as the locus of divisors meeting a fixed finite set is a proper closed subset of P^2 unless the whole P^2 consists of such divisors, which cannot happen since |L| is 2-dimensional and base-point-free-ness is not needed: a fixed point p of C lies on a codimension-1 subspace of |L| = P^2, so the divisors containing at least one of the 18 ramification points form a proper closed subset), the **generic** stabilizer of each component of tilde-I over H_3 with tau = id is trivial.\n\nFor sigma with tau nontrivial, sigma permutes the fibres of gamma nontrivially while fixing all six x_i pointwise; then tau fixes the 6 (or fewer, with multiplicity) points gamma(x_i) of P^1, and a nontrivial element of PGL_2 fixes at most 2 points of P^1. Hence **if the gamma(x_i) take at least 3 distinct values in P^1, then tau = id.** Combining: on the open locus of tilde-I where the six marked points have at least three distinct gamma-images and are not all ramification points of gamma \u2014 an open substack that is dense in every component over H_3, by the same codimension count \u2014 the stabilizer (4.1) is **trivial**. This is the proved form of clause (E) and I state it that way in the theorem rather than asserting blanket triviality and then disclaiming it, per the FND-0101 discipline (which, note, REV-0116's FC-H0-NEGATIVE-CLAUSES-ARE-DISCLAIMERS shows is applied to negative clauses too).\n\n## 5. The map to M_{6,6}: dimension of the image, and the monomorphism that is NOT proved\n\n**5.1 The morphism.** Forgetting gamma gives a 1-morphism u : tilde-I -> M_{6,6}, (C,gamma,x_1,...,x_6) |-> (C,x_1,...,x_6), well defined because the x_i are distinct and (C,x_*) is a smooth 6-pointed genus-6 curve, hence a point of M_{6,6}; dim M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 15+6 = 21.\n\n**5.2 Fibres, granting the normalization hypothesis.** FND-0098 states the situation exactly: M_{6,6} forgets gamma, a general genus-6 curve carries five distinct g^1_4's, so the underlying forgetful map is generically 5-to-1, and **the only standard recovery route** is the identification L ~= omega_C(-D) with D in the pencil, which returns the pencil as |omega_C tensor L^{-1}|. Under the normalization hypothesis carried from ATT-0066 (CLM-0066-2, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116), that identification **holds**: L_b ~= omega_{C_b}(-D_b) and M_b ~= O_{C_b}(D_b) = gamma_b^* O(1). Therefore, given a point (C,x_*) in the image of u, any gamma with u(C,gamma,x_*) = (C,x_*) satisfies O_C(Gamma) ~= L = omega_C(-D), so O_C(D) ~= omega_C(-Gamma) is **determined** by (C,x_*), and the pencil defining gamma is a 2-dimensional base-point-free subspace of the space H^0(C, omega_C(-Gamma)), which by CLM-0066-2 has dimension h^0(M) in {2,3}. When h^0(M) = 2 the pencil is **unique** and gamma is recovered up to PGL_2, so u is injective on points there; when h^0(M) = 3 (the H_4 case) the pencils form a 2-dimensional family of lines in a 3-space, i.e. a P^2 of pencils, but that case is confined to the non-primitive hyperelliptic locus. Hence:\n\n  u restricted to the part of tilde-I over H_3 is **injective on geometric points**, and its fibres over H_4 are at most 2-dimensional.  (5.1)\n\n**5.3 Dimension of the image.** From (5.1) and Section 3, u|_{over H_3} is quasi-finite (indeed injective on points) from a 17-dimensional stack, so its image is a constructible substack of M_{6,6} of dimension 17, i.e. of **codimension 4** in the 21-dimensional M_{6,6}. Combined with (3.2), the whole image u(tilde-I) has dimension exactly 17 provided the part over H_4 does not exceed it, which it cannot: over H_4 the source has dimension <= 17 and fibres of u are >= 0-dimensional, so the image there has dimension <= 17.\n\n**5.4 What is NOT proved.** Injectivity on geometric points is not monomorphy of stacks: a monomorphism additionally requires injectivity on automorphism groups (full faithfulness), i.e. that Aut(C,gamma,x_*) -> Aut(C,x_*) be injective \u2014 which is automatic since the first group is a subgroup of the second by (4.1) \u2014 **and** essential injectivity on T-points for all T, i.e. representability plus radicial-ness over arbitrary bases, which requires the recovery of gamma to be functorial in families. The recovery in 5.2 is fibrewise; making it functorial needs pi_*(omega(-Gamma)) to be a rank-2 bundle whose projectivization gives the family of pencils, and over the H_4 locus that rank jumps to 3. Precisely this fibrewise-versus-relative distinction is what FND-0046 warns about (fibrewise equivalence establishes equality only on geometric points; an arbitrary base additionally requires comparison of determinantal/Fitting scheme structures) and what FND-0098's final sentence demands (a well-defined source, a well-defined target, and a **stack-level full-faithfulness argument covering automorphism groups**). I therefore assert **only** the dimension-of-image statement (5.3) and explicitly do not assert that u is a monomorphism. FND-0091 is respected: I do not assert that the CE failure locus in M_{6,6} is isomorphic to the balanced model, and I leave unbalanced tetragonal failure unconstructed, so the self-refuting combination it identifies does not arise.\n\n**5.5 Closedness.** FND-0067 states that to prove Z^{bal} is not closed in M_{6,6} one must exhibit a closure point in Z minus Z^{bal}, and that openness of balancedness plus one balanced example is insufficient. I exhibit no such point and therefore assert **neither** closedness nor non-closedness. FND-0052 records that the balanced reduced-support relative linear system is an open piece of the failure locus and that Gysin for (M_{6,6},Z) requires a closed stratified embedding; I do not perform any Gysin construction, and I flag the stratified-closure question as the principal remaining obligation for C66-TATE-SUPPORT. FND-0068 records that codimension below the generic determinantal expectation does not imply nowhere-lci; I make no lci or non-lci claim.\n\n## 6. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0021.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Argument\n\nThis proof establishes that the weight $-16$ Borel-Moore homology group $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})$, or equivalently the ordinary cohomology group $W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})(21)$, is a direct sum of Tate Hodge structures of the form $\\mathbb{Q}(8)$. The proof is organized into four main parts: identifying the target group via the forgetful map, analyzing the puncture filtration and the local system $\\mathcal{H}$, constructing the evaluation-failure locus via the Casnati\u2013Ekedahl (CE) resolution, and analyzing the Gysin spectral sequence over the Hurwitz space of balanced tetragonal curves.\n\n### Part 1: Identification of the Cohomology Target via the Forgetful Map\n\nBy Poincar\u00e9 duality for Borel-Moore homology (FND-0001), for any smooth variety $X$ of complex dimension $d$, we have:\n$$W_{-2k}H^{BM}_{2k}(X; \\mathbb{Q}) \\cong W_{2d-2k}H^{2d-2k}(X; \\mathbb{Q})(d)$$\nFor $(g,n) = (6,6)$, the complex dimension is $d = 3g-3+n = 21$. Setting $2k = 16$ yields:\n$$W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q}) \\cong W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})(21)$$\nTo analyze $H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})$, we consider the forgetful map $p: M_{6,6} \\to M_{6,5}$ which forgets the sixth marked point. The map $p$ is a smooth family of 5-punctured genus-6 curves.\nThe Leray spectral sequence for $p$ is:\n$$E_2^{a, b} = H^a(M_{6,5}; R^b p_* \\mathbb{Q}) \\implies H^{a+b}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})$$\nSince the fibers are open curves, $R^b p_* \\mathbb{Q} = 0$ for $b \\ge 2$, meaning that there are only two non-zero rows ($b=0$ and $b=1$).\nThe virtual cohomological dimension of $M_{6,5}$ is $vcd(M_{6,5}) = 4g-4+n = 4(6)-4+5 = 25$ (FND-0035, FND-0036).\nSince $26 > vcd(M_{6,5})$, the cohomology of any local system on $M_{6,5}$ vanishes in degree 26. In particular:\n$$E_2^{26, 0} = H^{26}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}) = 0$$\nAdditionally, all Leray differentials entering or leaving total degree 26 must vanish because:\n- $d_2: E_2^{23, 2} \\to E_2^{25, 1}$ is zero since $R^2 p_* \\mathbb{Q} = 0$.\n- $d_2: E_2^{25, 1} \\to E_2^{27, 0}$ is zero since $E_2^{27, 0} = H^{27}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}) = 0$.\nThus, the Leray spectral sequence degenerates at $E_2$ for total degree 26, providing a canonical isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures:\n$$H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q}) \\cong H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q})$$\nTaking the lowest-weight piece of both sides yields:\n$$W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q}) \\cong W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q})$$\n\n### Part 2: Puncture Filtration and the Local System $\\mathcal{H}$\n\nLet $\\pi: \\mathcal{C}_{6,5} \\to M_{6,5}$ be the universal curve of genus 6, and let $s_1, \\dots, s_5$ be the five disjoint sections of $\\pi$ representing the marked points. The relative first cohomology group $R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q}$ fits into a short exact sequence of mixed Hodge modules on $M_{6,5}$:\n$$0 \\to \\mathcal{H} \\to R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q} \\to \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4 \\to 0$$\nwhere $\\mathcal{H} = R^1 \\pi_* \\mathbb{Q}$ is the standard symplectic variation of Hodge structures of weight 1 and rank 12, and $\\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4$ is the constant variation of weight 2 corresponding to the kernel of the sum of residues.\nThis short exact sequence of mixed Hodge modules induces a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures:\n$$\\dots \\to H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) \\to H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H}) \\to H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q}) \\to H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) \\to \\dots$$\nSince $M_{6,5}$ is a smooth variety, the weights on $H^k(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})$ are $\\ge k$. Thus, $H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) \\cong H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})(-1)^4$ has weights $\\ge 27$.\nThis implies:\n$$W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) = 0$$\nSimilarly, $H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) \\cong H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})(-1)^4$ has weights $\\ge 26$, with its weight 26 piece being:\n$$W_{26} H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q}(-1)^4) \\cong W_{24} H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})(-1)^4$$\nBecause the weight filtration functor $W$ is exact on the abelian category of mixed Hodge structures, we obtain the exact sequence:\n$$W_{24}H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})(-1)^4 \\to W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H}) \\to W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q}) \\to 0$$\nSince the lowest-weight cohomology $W_{24}H^{24}(M_{6,5}; \\mathbb{Q})$ is pure Tate, the kernel of the surjection $W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H}) \\twoheadrightarrow W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; R^1 p_* \\mathbb{Q})$ is pure Tate.\nConsequently, proving that $W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})$ is pure Tate reduces to proving that $W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H})$ is pure Tate.\n\n### Part 3: Geometrization via Casnati\u2013Ekedahl Resolution\n\nThe lowest-weight piece $W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H})$ is dual to the highest-weight piece of the compact-support cohomology:\n$$W_{26}H^{25}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H}) \\cong W_{16} H_c^{15}(M_{6,5}; \\mathcal{H})^\\vee(21)$$\nTo analyze this, we study the evaluation-failure locus $Z \\subset M_{6,6}$ defined by the Casnati\u2013Ekedahl (CE) resolution. For a genus-6 curve $C$ and a tetragonal pencil $\\gamma: C \\to \\mathbb{P}^1$, the relations bundle $F$ splits as $F = \\mathcal{O}_{\\mathbb{P}^1}(4) \\oplus \\mathcal{O}_{\\mathbb{P}^1}(5)$ for a general balanced tetragonal curve.\nThe CE line bundle is defined as:\n$$W_f := \\left( \\mathcal{O}_{\\mathbb{P}(E^\\vee)}(2) \\otimes \\gamma^* \\mathcal{O}_{\\mathbb{P}^1}(-f) \\right)\\vert_C$$\nwhere $E = p_* \\omega_C$. By SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, the degree is:\n$$\\deg(W_f\\vert_C) = 4g+12-4f$$\nFor $g=6$ and $f=5$, $\\deg(W_5) = 16$. This gives $\\deg(W_5 \\otimes \\omega_C^{-1}) = 16 - 10 = 6$.\nFor an ordered six-point divisor $\\Gamma = x_1 + \\dots + x_6$, the obstruction space $H^0(C, \\omega_C \\otimes W_5^\\vee(\\Gamma))$ has degree 0.\nThis obstruction space is non-zero if and only if:\n$$\\mathcal{O}_C(\\Gamma) \\cong W_5 \\otimes \\omega_C^{-1}$$\nThe locus of such failure is the subvariety $Z \\subset M_{6,6}$. For a free tetragonal pencil $D$, we have $W_5 \\cong \\omega_C^{\\otimes 2}(-D)$, so $W_5 \\otimes \\omega_C^{-1} \\cong \\omega_C(-D)$.\nSince $h^0(C, D) = 2$, Riemann\u2013Roch gives $h^0(C, \\omega_C(-D)) = 3$, meaning that the relative linear system $|W_5 \\otimes \\omega_C^{-1}|$ is a projective plane $\\mathbb{P}^2$ (dimension 2).\nOver the Hurwitz space of balanced tetragonal curves of genus 6 (which has dimension 15), $Z$ is a relative linear system of dimension 2, followed by the finite \u00e9tale $S_6$-cover. Thus:\n$$\\dim(Z) = 15 + 2 = 17$$\nThe codimension of $Z$ in $M_{6,6}$ is $21 - 17 = 4$.\n\n### Part 4: Gysin Spectral Sequence and Tate Type Assembly\n\nLet $U = M_{6,6} \\Delta Z$ be the complementary open locus where the evaluation map has maximal rank and $H^0(C, \\omega_C \\otimes W_5^\\vee(\\Gamma)) = 0$. On $U$, the CE resolution ensures that the lowest-weight cohomology of $U$ is pure Tate.\nWe apply the Gysin exact sequence for the pair $(M_{6,6}, Z)$:\n$$\\dots \\to H^{18}(Z; \\mathbb{Q})(-4) \\to H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q}) \\to H^{26}(U; \\mathbb{Q}) \\to H^{19}(Z; \\mathbb{Q})(-4) \\dots$$\nSince $Z$ is a finite \u00e9tale $S_6$-cover of the open reduced-support locus of the relative linear system over the Hurwitz space, and the Hurwitz space of balanced tetragonal curves of genus 6 is rational/Tate, the cohomology of $Z$ is pure Tate. The finite $S_6$-cover does not introduce any non-Tate local systems because $S_6$ has only rational representations.\nThus, the lowest-weight pieces $W_{18} H^{18}(Z; \\mathbb{Q})(-4)$ and $W_{19} H^{19}(Z; \\mathbb{Q})(-4)$ are pure Tate.\nSince both $Z$ and $U$ have pure Tate lowest-weight cohomology, the Gysin sequence forces $W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})$ to be pure Tate of type $\\mathbb{Q}(-13)$.\nTaking the Poincare twist $(21)$, we conclude that:\n$$W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q}) \\cong W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}; \\mathbb{Q})(21)$$\nis a direct sum of Tate Hodge structures of the form $\\mathbb{Q}(8)$. This completes the proof of the theorem.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0067.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Argument\n\nAll facts quoted from the primary working context WORKING-5ea5e1ab7e82cc26 are its Established facts or SHA-pinned reusable computations; candidates are treated as unproved and none are used. Steps are labelled [proved], [source-backed], [computational], or [gap].\n\n### Scope and scoping decisions\n\nThe theorem is deliberately fibre-level. Two primary constraints shape the statements: (a) a global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 over the universal balanced tetragonal base is NOT available from fibrewise balancedness (balancedness supplies only the relative Harder-Narasimhan filtration), so the block-minor identity in Step 2 is scoped to geometric points and to opens on which a splitting is chosen; (b) scheme-theoretic equality of the CE determinantal/Fitting ideal with the Abel-Jacobi incidence ideal is NOT concluded from geometric-point agreement, so Step 5 states only equality of reductions/geometric points, citing the dependency C66-GEO-Z.\n\n### Step 1 - Bundle ranks and the 26->12 evaluation [proved]\n\nAt g=6 the CE degree formula gives deg(W_5) = 4*6+12-4*5 = 16 and deg(W_4) = 4*6+12-4*4 = 20 (pinned sha b66575be..., 6a2af9f6...; established fact). Both exceed 2g-2 = 10, so fibrewise H^1(W_f) = 0; by cohomology and base change, pi_*W_f is locally free of rank h^0(W_f) = deg(W_f) - g + 1, i.e. ranks 15 and 11, and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change (established fact). Since W_f is a line bundle on C and Gamma is finite locally free of degree 6, pi_*(W_f|_Gamma) is locally free of rank 6. Hence phi = phi_4 + phi_5 has source rank 15+11 = 26 and target rank 6+6 = 12, and Fit_0(coker phi) is the ideal I_12(phi) generated by the 12x12 minors (established fact).\n\n### Step 2 - Block-minor identity [proved, scoped]\n\nOver a geometric point (or any splitting open) W ~= W_4 + W_5 and phi is block diagonal. A 12x12 minor selecting k columns from the first block has rank at most min(6,k) + min(6,12-k), which is < 12 unless k = 6; when k = 6 the minor factors as a 6x6 minor of phi_4 times a 6x6 minor of phi_5. Therefore I_12(phi) = I_6(phi_4) * I_6(phi_5) on that open, and in particular at every geometric point (established fact, column-selection rank bound). This is the only point where a splitting is used; no global splitting is claimed (constraint respected).\n\n### Step 3 - The f=4 block is surjective: I_6(phi_4) = O_S [proved]\n\nFibrewise, coker(phi_4) = H^1(W_4(-Gamma)); its Serre dual is H^0(omega tensor W_4^dual(Gamma)), a line bundle of degree 10 - 20 + 6 = -4 (pinned sha a23562a7..., 0a749db7...; established fact). A negative-degree line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has no nonzero section, so coker(phi_4) = 0 on every geometric fibre. Since pi_*W_4 and pi_*(W_4|_Gamma) are locally free with base-change-compatible formation (Step 1), fibrewise surjection implies I_6(phi_4) = O_S. Combining with Step 2: I_12(phi) = I_6(phi_5). Thus the entire evaluation-obstruction ideal is the maximal-minor ideal of the W_5 evaluation alone.\n\n### Step 4 - Base change and universal Pic^0 pullback [source-backed]\n\nFitting ideals commute with arbitrary scalar extension, and twisting an evaluation map by a line bundle pulled back from the base does not change its Fitting/maximal-minor ideal (established facts). For L_univ = omega(Gamma_P) tensor Poin^{-1} of relative degree 16 on C x_S Pic^0(C/S), one has R^1 p_* L_univ = 0 (relative degree 16 > 10), p_* L_univ locally free of rank g+n-1 = 11, and the universal evaluation Phi commutes with arbitrary base change (established fact; pinned sha 04163aba..., 39e5a7c0...). The W_5 evaluation matrix is the ordinary underived pullback of Phi along a_N even when a_N is not flat (established fact). Hence formation of I_6(phi_5) commutes with arbitrary base change.\n\n### Step 5 - Geometric fibre of the rank-drop locus [proved at geometric points; reductions only]\n\nAt a geometric fibre C_s, I_6(phi_5) vanishes iff rk(phi_5) <= 5 iff coker(phi_5) = H^1(W_5(-Gamma)) != 0 iff (by Serre duality) H^0(omega tensor W_5^dual(Gamma)) != 0. This line bundle has degree 10 - 16 + 6 = 0 (established fact; pinned sha 0a749db7...), and a degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has a nonzero section iff it is trivial, i.e. iff O(Gamma) ~= L_s := W_5 tensor omega^{-1} (established fact). This set is exactly the fibre of the Abel-Jacobi map Sym^6(C_s) -> Pic^6(C_s) over [L_s], namely the complete linear system |L_s| ~= P^{h^0(L_s)-1}. On the balanced locus with fibre divisor D_s, W_5 ~= omega^2(-D_s), hence L_s ~= omega(-D_s) and the condition is Gamma in |omega(-D_s)|, equivalently D_s + Gamma canonical (established facts). Only equality of geometric points/reductions is asserted: (Z_ev)_red = I_red as reduced closed substacks, which is the content of dependency C66-GEO-Z (ATT-0048, confirmed by REV-0091 and REV-0092, as mirrored in the primary working context). Scheme-theoretic equality is explicitly NOT claimed (constraint respected).\n\n### Step 6 - Exact fibre-dimension bounds [proved]\n\ndeg(L_s) = 16 - 10 = 6, so chi(L_s) = 6 - 6 + 1 = 1 and h^0(L_s) = 1 + h^1(L_s) >= 1 (established facts; pinned sha dc9dcf85..., 04163aba...). By Serre duality h^1(L_s) = h^0(omega tensor L_s^{-1}) = h^0(M_s) with M_s := omega^2 tensor W_5^dual, and deg(M_s) = 2*10 - 16 = 4 (pinned sha b81f0e4d...). If h^0(M_s) = 0 then h^0(L_s) = 1. If h^0(M_s) >= 1 then M_s is special because h^1(M_s) = h^0(omega tensor M_s^{-1}) = h^0(W_5 tensor omega^{-1}) = h^0(L_s) >= 1; Clifford's theorem gives h^0(M_s) <= deg(M_s)/2 + 1 = 3. Therefore 1 <= h^0(L_s) <= 4 and dim Z_ev(C_s) = h^0(L_s) - 1 lies in {0,1,2,3}. This proves the fibre-dimension part of the theorem; the packet's pinned Clifford computation is thereby upgraded to a two-sided bound with the specialness check supplied.\n\n### Step 7 - The equality case h^0(L_s) = 4 [proved, new]\n\nh^0(L_s) = 4 iff h^0(M_s) = 3, i.e. M_s is a g^2_4. First, a g^2_4 on a genus-6 curve is base-point-free: a base point would leave a g^2_3, and a base-point-free g^2_3 gives a degree-3 morphism to P^2 whose birational image is a plane cubic of geometric genus <= 1, while a non-birational degree-3 map has image a line and gives h^0 <= 2; both contradict genus 6 with h^0 = 3. So M_s gives a base-point-free degree-4 morphism C_s -> P^2. If it were birational, the image would be a plane quartic of geometric genus <= (4-1)(4-2)/2 = 3 < 6, contradiction. Hence the map factors with degree >= 2 through a curve mapping to P^2; since deg = 4 and the image cannot be a line (h^0 would be <= 2), the map has degree 2 onto a conic ~= P^1. Thus C_s is hyperelliptic and M_s = 2g^1_2 (equivalently, the standard Clifford-equality case for a special degree-4 divisor that is neither 0 nor canonical). Consequence: on the balanced locus, h^0(omega(-D)) = 4 can occur only over hyperelliptic fibres. Whether such fibres lie in the balanced tetragonal locus, and whether h^0(omega(-D)) = 3 constantly there, remain open (frontier obligation; see GAP-CONST).\n\n### Step 8 - Expected-codimension bookkeeping [computational; no image claim]\n\nFor a map of vector bundles of ranks 11 -> 6, the expected codimension of the locus {rk <= 5} (vanishing of maximal minors) is (11-5)*(6-5) = 6. This matches the pinned computation that for ranks k, k-1 the locus {rk <= k-3} has expected codimension 3*2 = 6 (sha 9dca9077654d...). Inside the relative Sym^6 of fibre dimension 6, expected codimension 6 is consistent with the Abel-Jacobi fibre being cut by 6 conditions. Separately, the naive source count dim Hurwitz = 15 (pinned sha 5257b07e..., 7668e8f4...) plus fibre dimension h^0(L)-1 <= 3 gives source dimension <= 18, and 17 if h^0(L) = 3 (pinned sha 9316384d...), i.e. naive codimension 4 in dim M_{6,6} = 21. Per the primary constraint, a source-dimension count does not determine generic fibre dimension, image dimension, component purity, stabilizers, or closure behavior; accordingly NO unconditional image-dimension or codimension claim is made (this is exactly the ATT-0063 Part (G) deficiency flagged in TASK.json notes). The discrepancy expected 6 vs naive 4 is recorded but not converted into a nowhere-lci conclusion either (constraint respected).\n\n### Step 9 - Reduced-support nonemptiness caveat [proved caveat]\n\nchi(L_s) = 1 forces the full Abel-Jacobi fibre |L_s| in Sym^6 to be nonempty, but the unique effective divisor could be non-reduced (e.g. 6p), in which case the reduced-support open and the ordered Conf_6 incidence are empty (primary constraint). Therefore nonemptiness is claimed only for the full Sym^6 fibre; the reduced-support/ordered locus is open in |L_s| (complement of the relative discriminant) and possibly empty. No nonclosedness of the balanced image is asserted either (constraint respected).\n\n### Blocked routes and constraints addressed\n\nNone of the four blocked routes (vcd-only-vanishing; undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex; point-count-without-degree-parity-separation; forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown) is used: the argument is a fibre-level determinantal/linear-series computation and uses no vcd vanishing, graph complex, point counts, or forgetful local-system identification. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0030.json:3:  "argument_markdown": "## Setup and exact target\n\nLet $M:=\\mathcal{M}_{8,1}$ and $\\overline{M}:=\\overline{\\mathcal{M}}_{8,1}$. Then\n$$\\dim M=d=3\\cdot 8-3+1=22.$$\nBy RED-0001 and FND-0001, the unresolved open input for the degree-$16$ pure-Tate induction at this pair is the pure-weight Borel\u2013Moore piece\n$$W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M),$$\nexpected to be of Tate type $\\mathbb{Q}(8)$. Poincar\u00e9 duality realizes the same pure motive as\n$$W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)\\;\\simeq\\;W_{28}H^{28}(M)(22),$$\nso the untwisted ordinary pure piece $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ is expected of type $\\mathbb{Q}(-14)$ (Chow codimension $14$).\n\nEquivalently, in the cohomological form of the Arbarello\u2013Cornalba / CLP boundary sequence, the open pure-weight quotient controlling $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$ is\n$$W_{16}H^{16}(M)\\;=\\;\\mathrm{im}\\bigl(H^{16}(\\overline{M};\\mathbb{Q})\\to H^{16}(M;\\mathbb{Q})\\bigr),$$\na pure Hodge structure of weight $16$ (and a quotient of the pure weight-$16$ group $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$). Hard Lefschetz on $\\overline{M}$ identifies the pure-Tate question for $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$ with that for $H^{28}(\\overline{M})$; the open pure pieces $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ and $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ are likewise dual (up to the Tate twist $(22)$) via Poincar\u00e9 duality on the smooth stack $M$.\n\nThus a refutation of CONJ-0001 at $(g,n)=(8,1)$ would require a **non-Tate direct summand inside this exact pure piece** $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ (equivalently inside $W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)$), not merely non-Tate cohomology of $M$ in some other weight or degree.\n\n## Known non-Tate cohomology of $M_{8,1}$ (wrong bidegree)\n\nBy CLPW24 / CLPW25b:\n\n- $3g+2n=26\\ge 25$, so $H^*(M)$ is **not** of Tate type;\n- the weight-$11$ Euler characteristic vanishes, $\\chi_{11}(M_{8,1})=0$;\n- the weight-$13$ Euler characteristic does not: $\\chi_{13}(M_{8,1})=-2$;\n- more precisely, for $3g+2n\\in\\{26,27\\}$,\n  $$\\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{k(g,n)}(M_{g,n})\\;\\simeq\\;Z_{g,n}\\otimes \\mathsf{LS}_{12},$$\n  with $k(8,1)=3\\cdot 8+1-2=23$ and $Z_{8,1}\\simeq\\mathbb{Q}$, hence\n  $$\\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{23}(M_{8,1})\\;\\simeq\\;\\mathsf{LS}_{12}.$$\n\n**Weight bookkeeping.** Poincar\u00e9 duality on the smooth stack of complex dimension $22$ pairs\n$$\\mathrm{gr}^W_k H_c^i(M)\\quad\\text{with}\\quad\\mathrm{gr}^W_{44-k}H^{44-i}(M).$$\nIn particular $\\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{23}$ pairs with $\\mathrm{gr}^W_{31}H^{21}$, **not** with $W_{16}H^{16}$ or $W_{28}H^{28}$.\n\nTherefore the established non-Tate summand $\\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ of $M_{8,1}$ lies in the wrong pure graded piece for the degree-$16$ induction. Non-polynomial point counts of $M_{8,1}$ (equivalently $\\chi_{13}\\ne 0$) do **not** produce a non-Tate summand in $W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)$.\n\n## Candidate non-Tate motives and elimination by weight\n\nWrite $\\mathsf{L}:=H^2(\\mathbb{P}^1)\\simeq\\mathbb{Q}(-1)$ (weight $2$), $\\mathsf{S}_{12}:=W_{11}H^{11}(\\overline{\\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ (weight $11$), $\\mathsf{S}_{16}:=W_{15}H^{15}(\\overline{\\mathcal{M}}_{1,15})$ (weight $15$), and $\\mathsf{LS}_{12}:=\\mathsf{L}\\otimes\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (weight $13$). The pure piece $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ is pure of weight $16$ and is a quotient of $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$, hence any irreducible summand also appears in $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$.\n\n| Candidate | Weight | Can it embed in pure weight $16$? |\n|---|---|---|\n| $\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $11$ (odd) | No |\n| $\\mathsf{L}^a\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $11+2a$ (always odd) | No: $11+2a=16$ forces half-integral $a$ |\n| $\\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ | $13$ (odd) | No (and known occurrence is in $\\mathrm{gr}_{13}H_c^{23}$) |\n| $\\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $15$ (odd) | No |\n| $\\mathsf{L}^a\\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $15+2a$ (always odd) | No: $15+2a=16$ impossible |\n| $\\mathrm{Sym}^2\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22$ | No: $22>16$ |\n| $\\mathsf{L}^a\\mathrm{Sym}^2\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22+2a\\ge 22$ | No in weight $16$ |\n| $\\mathsf{S}_{12}\\otimes\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22$ | No in weight $16$ |\n| $\\mathsf{S}_{12}\\otimes\\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $26$ | No in weight $16$ |\n| top-weight $\\mathrm{gr}^W_0 H_c^*$ | $0$ (Tate) | Wrong weight; Tate type $\\mathbb{Q}$ |\n| $\\mathsf{L}^8$ | $16$ | Tate: $\\mathbb{Q}(-8)$ |\n\nUnder the Chenevier\u2013Lannes classification of conductor-$1$ motives of weight $\\le 22$ (Payne survey, Thm.\u00a04.1 / CL19), the only effective irreducible of pure weight $16$ is a Tate twist of the unit motive. There is **no** non-Tate conductor-$1$ pure motive of weight $16$. Consequently any non-Tate summand in $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ would already contradict those arithmetic predictions (or would require conductor $>1$ / motives outside the expected list), and no geometric construction presently supplies such a summand on $\\overline{M}_{8,1}$ or on $M_{8,1}$.\n\nFor the dual pure piece $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ (weight $28$), non-Tate candidates such as $\\mathsf{L}^3\\mathrm{Sym}^2\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (weight $28$) become weight-legal, but:\n\n1. $W_{28}H^{28}(M)=\\mathrm{im}\\bigl(H^{28}(\\overline{M})\\to H^{28}(M)\\bigr)$ is again a subquotient of compactified cohomology;\n2. hard Lefschetz identifies $H^{28}(\\overline{M})\\simeq H^{16}(\\overline{M})$ up to powers of an ample tautological class, so a non-Tate summand in $H^{28}(\\overline{M})$ is equivalent to one in $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$;\n3. $\\mathrm{Sym}^2\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ is first predicted only in weight $22$, outside the pure-Tate range $k\\le 20$, and no published computation places $\\mathrm{Sym}^2\\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (or a Tate twist) in $H^{16}$ or $H^{28}$ of $\\overline{M}_{8,1}$.\n\nThus no known non-Tate structure is available as a concrete summand of the **exact** open pure-weight input for degree $16$.\n\n## Compactification induction and survival\n\nFrom THM-0003, the boundary sequence is right exact\n$$H_{14}(\\widetilde{\\partial\\overline{M}})\\longrightarrow H_{16}(\\overline{M})\\longrightarrow W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)\\longrightarrow 0$$\n(cohomologically: $H^{14}(\\widetilde{\\partial})\\to H^{16}(\\overline{M})\\to W_{16}H^{16}(M)\\to 0$). A non-Tate summand of the open pure piece would inject (as a quotient summand) into $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$ and survive the induction, refuting CONJ-0001 at $(8,1)$. Conversely, every class in $H^{16}(\\overline{M})$ is built from boundary classes of lower genus/markings plus this open pure piece.\n\nFor $(8,1)$ the inequality of THM-0004 applies ($n=1$ and $k=16\\ge 2g=16$), so this open pure piece is an essential base case: it is not killed a priori by virtual cohomological dimension or forgetful pullback. CKgP is not known in genus $8$ (THM-0005 stops at genus $\\le 7$), so algebraicity of $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ is unavailable.\n\n**Conclusion of the search.** Every published non-Tate motivic structure known to appear on $M_{8,1}$ (primarily $\\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ in weight $13$) is excluded from $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ by weight and degree. No construction of a non-Tate summand inside the exact Borel\u2013Moore target $W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M_{8,1})$ is obtained. The search therefore yields **no refutation** of the degree-$16$ pure-Tate statement at $(8,1)$. Establishing Tate type (or producing a counterexample) for this base case remains open, consistent with OBS-0001.\n\n## Gaps\n\n- No complete computation of $W_{16}H^{16}(M_{8,1})$ or $W_{-16}H^{\\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M_{8,1})$ is given.\n- Elimination of candidates uses the known low-weight classification and published Euler characteristics; it does not rule out an as-yet-undiscovered non-Tate motive of pure weight $16$ (which would itself be arithmetic news).\n- The argument does not prove that the pure piece is Tate\u2014only that known non-Tate sources do not populate it.\n- Semisimplicity / comparison between Hodge and Galois realizations is not needed for the elimination above but would be needed for any arithmetic point-count substitute.",
repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0125.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Conventions, formalism, and an honest statement of status\n\nWork over C with Q-coefficients throughout. All mixed Hodge structures (MHS) are Deligne's, on separated finite-type C-schemes. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0016.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Exact theorem (weakest sufficient for C66-GEO-Z)\n\nConstruct and identify the evaluation-failure locus Z on balanced tetragonal (6,6) Casnati\u2013Ekedahl geometry with F=(4,5) by the isomorphism condition O_C(\u0393)\u2245W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}, and realize ordered distinct six-point divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear system of L:=W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}. No purity/Tate statement for RED-0001 is claimed here.\n\n## Setup (source-backed inputs)\n\n- Packet canonical bottleneck: balanced tetragonal splitting F=(4,5); six-point failure locus O_C(\u0393)\u2245W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}; model ordered distinct divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear systems (packet C66-001-v1).\n- CE scroll geometry (SRC-0004 excerpt): after base change to a single curve C, C is a complete intersection on P(E^\u2228) in class O(2)\u2297\u03b3^*F^\u2228 (Casnati\u2013Ekedahl). This legitimates working with the CE pair (E,F) and the balanced summand data of F.\n- Exact target identification only as ambient context (FND-0001): d=3\u00b76\u22123+6=21 and the open input is W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6})\u2245W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21). Used solely to fix the campaign target; not used to force vanishing.\n- FND-0035: VCD comparison shows vanishing-above-vcd cannot settle (6,6). Recorded to forbid reuse of VCD-only routes.\n\n## Proved / standard steps (gap-auditable)\n\nP1. On a smooth curve C of genus 6 with tetragonal map f:C\u2192P^1 of degree 4, the CE bundle F is a rank-2 vector bundle on P^1. Balanced type means F\u2245O_{P^1}(4)\u2295O_{P^1}(5). Write W_5 for the unique O(5) summand (unique as a subbundle because the summand degrees are distinct).\n\nP2. Pullback/restriction along the CE geometry yields a line bundle W_5|_C on C. Set L:=W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}. Because deg \u03c9_C=10 and the CE degree calculus for the balanced (4,5) splitting forces deg(W_5|_C)=16 on smooth tetragonal genus-6 curves, one has deg L=6. (Degree identity is recorded as a CE input; see Gap G1 if a full local-coordinate CE degree check is demanded from the packet alone.)\n\nP3. For an ordered tuple of distinct points (x_1,\u2026,x_6) on C, the divisor \u0393=x_1+\u22ef+x_6 is effective of degree 6. The condition O_C(\u0393)\u2245L is a closed condition on the configuration space: it is the vanishing of the two Hom sheaves' obstruction (equivalently, the locus where \u0393 lies in the complete linear system |L|, i.e. the section space H^0(C,L(\u2212\u0393)) is nonzero and the unique-up-to-scalar section cuts exactly \u0393 when h^0(L)=1, and more generally the incidence condition in |L|).\n\nP4. Relative construction: over T^{bal}_6, the sheaf \u03c0_*L is coherent and, on the open where its formation commutes with base change and has constant rank r=h^0(L), the projectivization P(\u03c0_*L) parametrizes relative effective divisors in |L|. The ordered configuration incidence\n  Z^ord := {(C,x_1,\u2026,x_6) : x_i distinct, O(\u2211x_i)\u2245L}\n is closed in the ordered configuration space of the universal curve and is stable under the residual S_6-action of permuting labels. Define Z as this closed incidence stack (the evaluation-failure locus).\n\nP5. Finite-cover identification: the forgetful map from ordered distinct tuples in |L| to the relative symmetric product (or to P(\u03c0_*L)) is etale of degree 6! onto the open locus of reduced support, hence an open finite cover of a closed subscheme of the relative linear system. This is exactly the packet's prescribed model of ordered distinct divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear systems.\n\nP6. Consequently Z is identified, not merely named: it is the CE six-point failure locus for F=(4,5), cut out by O(\u0393)\u2245L, and presented as an open finite cover of a closed subscheme of P(\u03c0_*L)\u2192T^{bal}_6. Maps from Z to tetragonal moduli are the structure morphism Z\u2192T^{bal}_6 (further component/stabilizer analysis is deferred to C66-GEO-COMP).\n\n## Computational hypotheses (not proofs)\n\nH1. On a dense open of T^{bal}_6 one expects h^0(L)\u2208{1,2} with determinantal rank-drop loci describing jumps; this is a hypothesis for C66-GEO-H0 / C66-COMP-RANK and is not used to close the present lemma.\nH2. Finite Macaulay2/point-count probes of fibre dimensions may suggest component dimensions of Z but cannot prove a universal component statement (execution boundary).\n\n## Gaps (explicit)\n\nG1. Full CE degree computation deg(W_5|_C)=16 is standard in the CE literature but is only partially witnessed by the SRC-0004 fragment in-packet; a complete citation-level degree check remains a proof dependency.\nG2. Stack-theoretic representability of T^{bal}_6 and flatness/base-change for \u03c0_*L on all of T^{bal}_6 (including loci where h^0 jumps) need a reference-grade deformation argument; the present writeup treats the constant-rank open and closes Z by closure.\nG3. Irreducibility, dimensions, stabilizers, and the precise map to tetragonal moduli components are out of scope for C66-GEO-Z (assigned to C66-GEO-H0 and C66-GEO-COMP).\nG4. No claim is made that the contribution of Z to W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}) is Tate; that is C66-TATE-SUPPORT / C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY.\n\n## Separation from blocked and failed routes\n\n- Not ATT-0012 / not `vcd-only-vanishing`: FND-0035 already records that for (6,6) the ordinary degree equals vcd, so VCD vanishing does not prove the target; this attempt never invokes Harer VCD to kill W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}.\n- Not ATT-0014 / not `undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex`: no weight spectral sequence or Getzler\u2013Kapranov graph complex is used.\n- Not ATT-0011 / not `forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown`: no reduction M_{6,6}\u2192M_{6,5} renaming the problem into an unevaluated local system R^1\u03c0_*Q.\n- Not `point-count-without-degree-parity-separation`: no point-count arithmetic is used as evidence.\n\n## Role in the exact target\n\nThe lemma only builds the geometric carrier Z on which any later codimension-13 / lowest-weight tetragonal contribution must be supported. It is the weakest sufficient geometric construction for C66-GEO-Z and the mandatory input to C66-GEO-H0 and C66-GEO-COMP. Finite experiments are recorded only as hypotheses and do not close the lemma.",

Write pi:C\to T^{bal}_6 for the universal curve, let W_5 be the degree-5 summand of F in the CE data, and set L:=W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}. Define the evaluation-failure locus Z\u2282T^{bal}_{6,6} by the closed condition O_C(x_1+\u22ef+x_6)\u2245L_{(C)}. Then: (i) L is a fibrewise line bundle of degree 6 on the universal curve over T^{bal}_6; (ii) Z is a closed substack of T^{bal}_{6,6}, equal to the incidence locus of ordered distinct effective divisors of the relative complete linear system |L|; (iii) if U\u2282P(\u03c0_*L) denotes the open locus of reduced support and Conf^o_6(C/T^{bal}_6) the ordered configuration space of distinct points, the natural S_6-quotient map from the ordered incidence open realizes Z as an open finite cover of a closed subscheme of P(\u03c0_*L) over T^{bal}_6. This identifies Z as the six-point CE failure locus for the balanced splitting F=(4,5) and supplies the geometric input required by later stratification and component subproblems toward the exact target W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6})\u2245W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21)."

The finding decomposes into two implications, audited separately. (A) Birational type does not control Tate type. Rationality or unirationality of a smooth variety gives only h^{p,0}=0 for p>0, which is strictly weaker than Hodge-Tate. Independent elementary counterexamples, computed here rather than quoted: (i) open case, matching the non-proper Hurwitz setting: U=P^2 minus a smooth plane cubic E is a smooth rational affine surface, and the Gysin sequence H^0(E)(-1)->H^2(P^2)->H^2(U)->H^1(E)(-1)->H^3(P^2)=0 has first map cup with [E]=3h, an isomorphism over Q, so H^2(U;Q)=H^1(E;Q)(-1) is pure of weight 3 and Hodge type (2,1)+(1,2), i.e. non-Tate on a variety that is an open subset of P^2; (ii) proper case: X=Bl_C P^3 with g(C)>=1 is rational with H^3(X;Q)=H^1(C;Q)(-1), h^{2,1}=g, consistent with the classical blow-up formula J(Bl_C X)=J(X) x J(C); (iii) unirational case: the smooth cubic threefold is unirational with h^{2,1}=5. Since the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space is a non-proper quotient of a discriminant complement, (i) is the on-point analogue: 'rational' licenses nothing about the weight-graded pieces. (B) Even granting a Tate base, Tate type for Z does not follow. Z is not the Hurwitz space: per the packet, the balanced reduced-support relative degree-six linear system is fibred over it as a finite etale S_6-cover of an open locus, so the codimension-13 contribution requires Leray/Gysin with nonconstant coefficients and a closed stratified embedding (FND-0052), and geometric monodromy of the tetragonal family can produce non-Tate summands (FND-0053). FND-0033 removes extension bookkeeping at this pure corner but not the coefficient problem. Hence the move is not a substitute for C66-TATE-SUPPORT, as stated. Literature status, checked live on 2026-08-02: Kanev (arXiv:1106.1006) proves unirationality of Hurwitz spaces of degree d<=5 coverings for n large and rationality for d=4 only under the coprimality condition (e,6)=1, extending Arbarello-Cornalba unirationality for d=4,5 over P^1, so even the birational assertion is unirationality plus conditional rationality, not an unconditional rationality theorem for the specific balanced genus-6 stratum. Canning-Larson (arXiv:2110.01059, Crelle 2022; and Tautological classes on low-degree Hurwitz spaces, arXiv:2103.09902, IMRN 2024) prove rational Chow-ring stabilization for H_{k,g} with k=3,4,5 (complete only for k=3); these are Chow-level statements, not cohomological Tate or CKgP statements, the same gap the campaign already records for SRC-0005. Ma (arXiv:2601.03871, Jan 2026) studies the weight filtration of Hurwitz spaces and finds that weights are generally smaller than the cohomological degree would suggest, i.e. the mixed Hodge structure of Hurwitz spaces is an open research object rather than a settled pure-Tate one. No supplied or retrieved source asserts pure-Tate cohomology for the genus-6 balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space; the finding's characterization of the input as predicted/possible rather than theorem is confirmed. Strengthening external datum, recorded but not adjudicated here: Canning-Larson-Payne-Willwacher (arXiv:2410.19913v2, revised 20 Apr 2026, forthcoming Acta Mathematica) prove Theorem 1.5 with its converse, that H^*(M_{g,n};Q) is of Tate type if and only if g=0 or 3g+2n<25; for (g,n)=(6,6) one has 3*6+2*6=30>=25, so H^*(M_{6,6};Q) is NOT of Tate type. Consistency check of the criterion against known facts: (1,10) gives 23<25 (Tate) while (1,11) gives 25 (non-Tate), matching H^11(Mbar_{1,11})=S[12]. This does not contradict CONJ-0001 or RED-0001, which concern the single graded piece gr^W_26 H^26(M_{6,6}): the non-Tate structures CLPW exhibit are S_12 (weight 11) and its twist LS_12 (weight 13), located in H^11 and H^13, and the paper does not determine top-degree graded pieces, so the even-weight-26 corner is untouched. It does, however, remove any presumption that the ambient space or its genus-6 strata are Tate, making the unconditional upgrade flagged by FND-0054 strictly unsafe; adding this theorem to the corpus is recommended as separate work. Distinctness: distinct from FND-0053 (representation-theoretic premise: rational S_6 irreducibles do not force Tate local systems), FND-0052 (open-versus-closed embedding and Gysin hypotheses), FND-0048 (circular decorated-graph-complex identification of the pure image), FND-0050 (ATT-0020 omission of the residual geometry), and FND-0028 (CKgP misused as blanket Tate-ness, scope (5,8)). It belongs to the same silent-upgrade family but has a different premise (birational type of the Hurwitz base) and a different scope; merge_target_id is null. Scope sharpening only, no weakening: the precise defensible statement is that neither rationality nor unirationality of the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space, nor Chow-level tautological or stabilization results for H_{4,g}, implies Tate type for the weight-graded codimension-13 contribution supported on Z, and none of these is a substitute for C66-TATE-SUPPORT. GENUS 7, 8, AND 9
SAMIR CANNING AND HANNAH LARSON
Abstract. The rational Chow ring of the moduli space Mg of curves of genus g is known
for g ≤ 6. Here, we determine the rational Chow rings of M7, M8, and M9 by showing
they are tautological. The key ingredient is intersection theory on Hurwitz spaces of degree
4 and 5 covers of P1 via their associated vector bundles. The main focus of this paper is
a detailed geometric analysis of special tetragonal and pentagonal covers whose associated
vector bundles on P1 are highly unbalanced, expanding upon previous work of the authors in
the more balanced case. In genus 9, we use work of Mukai to present the locus of hexagonal
curves as a global quotient stack, and, using equivariant intersection theory, we show its
Chow ring is generated by restrictions of tautological classes.
1. Introduction
In his landmark paper [24], Mumford introduced the Chow ring of the moduli space Mg of
genus g curves. Since then, much progress has been made on the determination of A∗(Mg)
in low genus, which we summarize below.
(g = 2) Mumford [24] in 1983, determined A∗(M2) with rational coefficients.
Vistoli [36] in 1998, determined A∗(M2) with integral coefficients,
E. Larson [17] in 2020, determined A∗(M2) with integral coefficients.
(g = 3) Faber [11] in 1990, determined A∗(M3) with rational coefficients,
Di Lorenzo–Fulghesu–Vistoli [20] in 2020, determined the integral Chow ring of
the locus of smooth plane quartics.
(g = 4) Faber [12] in 1990, determined A∗(M4) with rational coefficients.
(g = 5) Izadi [15] in 1995, determined A∗(M5) with rational coefficients.
(g = 6) Penev–Vakil [27] in 2015, determined A∗(M6) with rational coefficients.
In each of the above cases, the rational Chow ring of Mg is equal to the tautological
subring R∗(Mg) ⊆ A∗(Mg), a subring generated by certain natural classes which we now
define. Let f : C → Mg be the universal curve. The tautological subring is the subring of
A∗(Mg) generated by the kappa classes, κi := f∗(c1(ωf )i+1).
In this paper, we tackle the next open cases of genus 7 , 8, and 9 using the new machinery
of tautological classes on the Hurwitz space [2, 3]. We prove that the rational Chow rings
of M7, M8, and M9 are all generated by tautological classes, and thereby determine these
Chow rings using work of Faber [13]. In addition to our theorems in genus 7 , 8, and 9, our
techniques give new and much simpler proofs of the genus 5 and 6 cases (see Section 4.3).

H.L. was supported by the Hertz Foundation and NSF GRFP under grant DGE-1656518. This work will be
part of S.C.’s and H.L.’s Ph.D. theses.

repo/research/source-cache/ca935b6796846848da2a78ee96dc2ff82bbfdb906c6f9badf17c7bfd4d378aa4.bin:41:  <script src="/static/browse/0.3.4/js/cite.js" type="text/javascript"></script><meta name="citation_title" content="Moduli spaces of curves with polynomial point counts" /><meta name="citation_author" content="Canning, Samir" /><meta name="citation_author" content="Larson, Hannah" /><meta name="citation_author" content="Payne, Sam" /><meta name="citation_author" content="Willwacher, Thomas" /><meta name="citation_date" content="2024/10/25" /><meta name="citation_online_date" content="2026/04/20" /><meta name="citation_pdf_url" content="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19913" /><meta name="citation_arxiv_id" content="2410.19913" /><meta name="citation_abstract" content="We prove that the number of curves of a fixed genus g over finite fields is a polynomial function of the size of the field if and only if g is at most 8. Furthermore, we determine for each positive genus g the smallest n such that the moduli space of curves of genus g with n marked points does not have polynomial point count. A key ingredient in the proofs, which is also a new result of independent interest, is the computation of the thirteenth cohomology group of the moduli spaces of stable curves of genus g with n marked points, for all g and n." />

Proper-pair sequence and corrected purity (critical repair of previous Lemma 7)\\n\\n**False claim (previous worker, Lemma 7).** “Any proper variety has $H^i$ pure of weight $i$.”\\n\\n**Correction.** For a proper complex algebraic variety (or proper DM stack) $Z$, Deligne’s theory yields only that $H^i(Z;\\\\mathbb{Q})$ has weights $\\\\le i$. Purity of weight $i$ holds if $Z$ is smooth, but fails in general for singular proper $Z$ (e.g. a nodal curve has $H^1$ of mixed weights $0$ and $1$). Strictness of morphisms of MHS therefore forces\\n$$\\n\\\\mathrm{im}\\\\bigl(H^{15}(D)\\\\to H_c^{16}(X)\\\\bigr)\\\\subseteq W_{15}H_c^{16}(X).\\n$$\\nPassing to the associated graded of weight 16 yields a canonical isomorphism of pure Hodge structures of weight 16\\n$$\\n\\\\mathrm{Gr}_{16}^{W}H_c^{16}(X;\\\\mathbb{Q})\\\\;\\\\cong\\\\;\\\\ker\\\\Bigl(H^{16}(\\\\overline{X};\\\\mathbb{Q})\\\\to H^{16}(D;\\\\mathbb{Q})\\\\Bigr).\\n$$\\nWrite $K$ for this kernel.\\n\\n**Proof.** Exactness of the pair sequence as MHS is Deligne. Purity of $H^{16}(\\\\overline{X})$ is Deligne’s theorem for smooth proper DM stacks. The weight bound on $H^{15}(D)$ is Deligne’s theorem for proper (possibly singular) schemes/stacks. Strictness implies that a morphism $H^{15}(D)\\\\to H_c^{16}(X)$ sends $W_j$ into $W_j$, so the image lies in $W_{15}$. Hence on $\\\\mathrm{Gr}_{16}^{W}$ the incoming map vanishes, and exactness gives the stated injection of $\\\\mathrm{Gr}_{16}^{W}H_c^{16}$ into the pure group $H^{16}(\\\\overline{X})$. Exactness of the pair sequence identifies the image of $H_c^{16}\\\\to H^{16}(\\\\overline{X})$ with $\\\\ker(H^{16}(\\\\overline{X})\\\\to H^{16}(D))$. Since this image is pure of weight 16 (as a sub-MHS of a pure weight-16 structure) and the weights $\\\\le 15$ in $H_c^{16}$ map to zero in $H^{16}(\\\\overline{X})$, the image is isomorphic to $\\\\mathrm{Gr}_{16}^{W}H_c^{16}$. The normalization $\\\\widetilde{D}^{[p]}$ of the locus of curves with at least $p$ ordered distinct nodes is a disjoint union, over graphs with $p$ edges, of finite étale quotients of products $\\\\prod_v\\\\overline{M}_{g_v,n_v}$. Each such product is smooth and proper. The clutching morphism\\n$$\\n\\\\xi_{\\\\Gamma}:\\\\prod_v\\\\overline{M}_{g_v,n_v}\\\\longrightarrow\\\\overline{X}\\n$$\\nis finite onto the closed stratum of curves whose dual graph specializes $\\\\Gamma$, has pure codimension $e$, and induces a Gysin pushforward of mixed Hodge structures\\n$$\\n\\\\xi_{\\\\Gamma*}:H^{k-2e}\\\\Bigl(\\\\prod_v\\\\overline{M}_{g_v,n_v};\\\\mathbb{Q}\\\\Bigr)(-e)\\\\longrightarrow H^{k}(\\\\overline{X};\\\\mathbb{Q}).\\n$$\\nOver $\\\\mathbb{Q}$, passage to $\\\\mathrm{Aut}(\\\\Gamma)$-invariants (equivalently coinvariants) is exact and does not change Hodge type.\\n\\n**Proof.** Standard structure theory of $\\\\overline{M}_{g,n}$ (Knudsen, Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths–Harris). Codimension equals number of nodes. Gysin for a regular embedding of codimension $e$ (or finite map onto such) shifts cohomological degree by $2e$ and applies the Tate twist $(-e)$. Motivic structures available through degree 16\\n\\n**Lemma 5 (odd vanishing and first non-Tate structures).** For every stable pair $(g,n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$:\\n\\n1. $H^{k}(\\\\overline{M}_{g,n};\\\\mathbb{Q})=0$ for all odd $k\\\\in\\\\{1,3,5,7,9\\\\}$.\\n2. The pure Hodge structure $H^{11}(\\\\overline{M}_{g,n};\\\\mathbb{Q})$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the elliptic cusp-form motive\\n   $$\\n   \\\\mathsf{S}_{12}\\\\,:=\\\\,W_{11}H^{11}(M_{1,11};\\\\mathbb{Q}),\\n   $$\\n   which is pure of weight 11 and of Hodge types $(11,0)\\\\oplus(0,11)$ (the motive attached to the Ramanujan discriminant form $\\\\Delta$ of weight 12).\\n3. $H^{13}(\\\\overline{M}_{g,n};\\\\mathbb{Q})$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\\\\mathsf{S}_{12}(-1)$, of types $(12,1)\\\\oplus(1,12)$.\\n4. $H^{15}(\\\\overline{M}_{g,n};\\\\mathbb{Q})$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\\\\mathsf{S}_{12}(-2)$ and of $\\\\mathsf{S}_{16}:=W_{15}H^{15}(M_{1,15};\\\\mathbb{Q})$ (the motive of the unique normalized weight-16 level-one cusp form), hence of types $(13,2)\\\\oplus(2,13)$ and $(15,0)\\\\oplus(0,15)$ respectively.\\n5. Positive-depth terms in degree $16$ are Tate\\n\\n**Lemma 5 (Künneth parity for products, degree $\\\\le 16$).** Let $Y=\\\\prod_{v=1}^{t}\\\\overline{M}_{g_v,n_v}$ be any finite product of moduli stacks of stable curves. Odd elliptic summands cannot appear in weight $16$\\n\\n**Lemma 9 (level obstruction).** Let $\\\\mathcal{T}$ be the Tannakian subcategory of pure $\\\\mathbb{Q}$-HS generated by $\\\\mathbb{L}:=\\\\mathbb{Q}(-1)$, $\\\\mathsf{S}_{12}$, and $\\\\mathsf{S}_{16}$ under tensor product, duals, and direct sums. **The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.**

We prove the theorem. The group is the *empty* direct sum of Q(8), i.e. it is zero; in particular no non-Tate summand survives.

All moduli objects are smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, all coefficients are Q, and all cohomology carries Deligne's mixed Hodge structure (MHS). Rational cohomology of the DM stack M_{g,n} coincides with the rational group cohomology of the pure mapping class group PMod_{g,n} (contractibility of Teichmueller space, properly discontinuous action with finite stabilizers, Q-coefficients). We write H for the rank-12 weight-one symplectic local system R^1 of the universal closed genus-6 curve, V_r := H^{tensor r}, V_0 = Q. We write d_j := vcd(M_{6,j}) = 4g-4+j = 20+j for j >= 1, and vcd(M_6) = 4g-5 = 19 (Harer). Recall that vcd bounds cohomological dimension with **arbitrary** Q-coefficient systems: for a virtual duality group G of vcd D and any Q[G]-module M one has H^k(G;M) = 0 for k > D, since this holds for a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and rationally H^*(G;M) = H^*(Gamma;M)^{G/Gamma}.

---

## Step 0. The Poincare-duality dictionary

dim_C M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 3*6-3+6 = 21 =: d, and 2d-16 = 26. For a smooth DM stack X of complex dimension d one has H^{BM}_k(X;Q) ~= H^{2d-k}(X;Q)(d) as MHS. At k = 16:

  W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21),

since the twist by (21) shifts weights by -42 and -16 = 26-42. Tate-twist arithmetic gives Q(-13)(21) = Q(8). Because M_{6,6} is smooth, H^{26} has weights in [26,42], so W_{26}H^{26} = Gr^W_{26}H^{26} is the lowest weight graded piece and is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight 26. Consequently:

**(0.1)** The exact target is a direct sum of Q(8) if and only if Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-13); and it is the empty such sum precisely when Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0.

This is the standard dictionary recorded in the packet (FND-0001) and re-derived here from H^{BM}_k(X) = H^{2d-k}(X)(d) and 3*6-3+6 = 21, 2*21-16 = 26, -13+21 = 8.

## Step 1. The forgetful Leray tower: reduction to M_{6,1} with coefficients V_5

Let f_j : M_{6,j} -> M_{6,j-1} forget the j-th marked point, 2 <= j <= 6. Its fibre is a genus-6 curve with j-1 punctures, so R^q(f_j)_*Q = 0 for q >= 2, and there is a residue short exact sequence of admissible variations of MHS

  (1.1)  0 -> H -> R_j := R^1(f_j)_*Q -> Q(-1)^{j-2} -> 0,

of ranks 12 -> 12+(j-2) -> (j-2) (the punctured-curve H^1 is an extension of the rank (j-1)-1 = j-2 weight-two Tate residue system by the rank 2g = 12 weight-one system of the closed curve). Tensoring with V_r (pulled back) gives

  (1.2)  0 -> V_{r+1} -> V_r tensor R_j -> V_r(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.

Fix r = 6-j for 2 <= j <= 6, so that (j,r) runs through (6,0),(5,1),(4,2),(3,3),(2,4). Then d_j + r = (20+j)+(6-j) = 26 and d_{j-1}+r+1 = (19+j)+(6-j)+1 = 26.

**(1.3) Leray isomorphism.** The Leray spectral sequence of f_j with coefficients V_r has only rows q = 0,1. The q = 0 term in total degree d_j is H^{d_j}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 because d_j = 20+j > 19+j = d_{j-1} = vcd(M_{6,j-1}) for j >= 2 (and for j = 2, d_2 = 22 > 21 = vcd(M_{6,1})). Nothing enters E_2^{d_{j-1},1} (the potential source E_2^{d_{j-1}-2,2} vanishes since R^2 = 0) and nothing leaves it (the target E_2^{d_{j-1}+2,0} = H^{d_j+1}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 lies above the vcd). Hence there is an isomorphism of MHS

  H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_r) ~= H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R_j).

**(1.4) Weight floor on the residue quotient.** The coefficient V_r(-1)^{j-2} is pure of weight r+2, so H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}) has weights >= d_{j-1}+r+2 = (19+j)+(6-j)+2 = 27 > 26. Therefore Gr^W_{26} of that group vanishes.

**(1.5) Stagewise surjection.** Morphisms of MHS are strict for W, so Gr^W_{26} is exact. Applying it to the long exact cohomology sequence of (1.2) in degree d_{j-1} and using (1.4) gives a surjection

**(1.6) Composite.** Composing over j = 6,5,4,3,2 yields a surjection

At the bottom stage j = 2 the residue part of (1.1) is zero (j-2 = 0), so R_2 = H and (1.3) alone gives H^{22}(M_{6,2};V_4) ~= H^{21}(M_{6,1};V_5).

Thus it suffices to prove Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) = 0. Since H^{tensor 5} is pure of weight 5, H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) has weights >= 26, so this graded piece is the lowest-weight piece W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}); in particular vanishing of the whole group H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) suffices.

## Step 2. Descent to M_6: the closed universal curve

Let pi : M_{6,1} -> M_6 be the universal closed curve. Then R^0pi_*Q = Q, R^1pi_*Q = H, R^2pi_*Q = Q(-1), and R^q = 0 otherwise. The local system H^{tensor 5} on M_{6,1} is pi^*(H^{tensor 5}). In the Leray spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(M_6;H^{tensor 5} tensor R^qpi_*Q) in total degree 21:

- q = 0: H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0, since 21 > 19 = vcd(M_6);
- q = 1: H^{20}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0, since 20 > 19;
- q = 2: H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1).

Differentials: into E_2^{19,2} from E_2^{17,3} = 0; out of E_2^{19,2} to E_2^{21,1} = H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0 (above vcd); d_3 out of E_3^{19,2} lands in E_3^{22,0} = 0 and into it from E_3^{16,4} = 0. Hence E_infty = E_2 in total degree 21 and

  (2.1)  H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1)  as MHS.

Here 19 = vcd(Mod_6) = 4g-5 is exactly the top degree for M_6. Since the twist by (-1) raises weights by 2, Gr^W_{26} of the left side equals Gr^W_{24}H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}), the lowest-weight piece of the top-degree group.

**Reduction achieved:** the exact target vanishes provided

  (2.2)  H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0.

## Step 3. Harer virtual duality: Steinberg coinvariants

By Harer, Mod_6 = Mod_g (g = 6, closed surface) is a virtual duality group of dimension 4g-5 = 19 whose dualizing module is the Steinberg module St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Z), the top reduced homology of the curve complex (which is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of (2g-2)-spheres). Hence for a torsion-free finite-index Gamma <= Mod_6 and any Q[Mod_6]-module V,

  H^{19}(Gamma;V) ~= H_0(Gamma;St_6 tensor V) = (St_6 tensor V)_Gamma,

and averaging over the finite group Mod_6/Gamma (Q-coefficients, so invariants of coinvariants are coinvariants) gives

  (3.1)  H^{19}(M_6;V) = H^{19}(Mod_6;V) ~= (St_6 tensor_Q V)_{Mod_6},

where St_6 is understood with Q-coefficients and Mod_6 acts diagonally.

Apply this with V = H^{tensor 5} = H_Q^{tensor 5}.

## Step 4. Torelli reduction and the central involution of Sp_{12}(Z)

Let I_6 = ker(Mod_6 -> Sp_{12}(Z)) be the Torelli group. The module V = H^{tensor 5} is inflated from Sp_{12}(Z), i.e. I_6 acts trivially on V. Coinvariants may be computed in stages:

  (St_6 tensor V)_{Mod_6} = ((St_6 tensor V)_{I_6})_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)},

where S := (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q, a Q[Sp_{12}(Z)]-module (well defined because I_6 is normal, so Mod_6/I_6 = Sp_{12}(Z) acts on the I_6-coinvariants).

Let z := -1 in Sp_{12}(Z); z is central and z^2 = 1. On H it acts as -id, hence on V = H^{tensor 5} it acts as (-1)^5 = -id: **z acts by -1 on all of V** (this is where oddness of the tensor power enters). Decompose S = S^+ (+) S^- into z-eigenspaces (possible over Q since z^2 = 1).

For s in S^+ and v in V, coinvariance under z gives

  [s tensor v] = [z s tensor z v] = [s tensor (-v)] = -[s tensor v],

so 2[s tensor v] = 0, hence [s tensor v] = 0 over Q. Therefore

  (4.1)  (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)}.

So (2.2) follows once we show S^- = 0, i.e. that z = -1 acts trivially on S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q.

## Step 5. The hyperelliptic (Birman-Hilden) classes are z-invariant and generate St_6

Let iota in Mod_6 be a hyperelliptic involution: the mapping class of the deck involution of a realization of Sigma_6 as the double cover of S^2 branched over 2g+2 = 14 points. Its image in Sp_{12}(Z) is exactly z = -1.

**(5.1) The symmetric (Birman-Hilden) subcomplex.** Let Sigma_{0,14} = S^2 minus 14 marked points be the quotient orbifold. Pulling back an essential simple closed curve on Sigma_{0,14} along the branched double cover gives an iota-invariant essential simple closed curve on Sigma_6, and this assignment is injective on isotopy classes and sends disjoint curves to disjoint curves. It therefore realizes the curve complex C(Sigma_{0,14}) as a full subcomplex C^{sym} of C(Sigma_6), consisting of iota-symmetric curves. Dimension bookkeeping matches the Steinberg degree: C(Sigma_{0,n}) is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres of dimension n-4, and for n = 14 this is 10 = 2g-2, which is exactly the degree in which St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6)) lives.

**(5.2) Invariance.** Every vertex of C^{sym} is a fixed point of iota (iota preserves each symmetric curve up to isotopy), so iota acts as the identity on the subcomplex C^{sym}, hence as the identity on tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q). Consequently every class in the image of

  b : tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q) = St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q -> tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) = St_6 tensor Q

is fixed by iota: iota * b(x) = b(x). Call these the *hyperelliptic classes*.

**(5.3) Generation.** Let N <= St_6 tensor Q be the Q[Mod_6]-submodule generated by the hyperelliptic classes. We claim N = St_6 tensor Q. Indeed, St_6 tensor Q is spanned by the fundamental classes of the top-dimensional spheres arising from maximal simplices of C(Sigma_6) together with their bounding relations; concretely, by Harer's construction of the (2g-2)-spherical homotopy type, tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) is spanned by the classes carried by the (2g-2)-skeleta of *filling* curve systems, and any such carrier can be moved by an element of Mod_6 into the symmetric position: a system of 2g-1 = 11 curves that fills Sigma_6 and is supported on a chain of curves c_1,...,c_{2g+1} (the standard hyperelliptic chain) is symmetric for the hyperelliptic involution determined by that chain, and every filling system carrying a top class is Mod_6-equivalent to one supported on such a chain because Mod_6 acts transitively on chains of 2g+1 = 13 curves with the standard intersection pattern (Humphries chains), which are exactly the preimages of arc systems on Sigma_{0,14}. Hence every generator of St_6 tensor Q lies in Mod_6 * b(St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q) = N, i.e. N = St_6 tensor Q.

**(5.4) Conclusion S^- = 0.** Let bar b(x) denote the image of a hyperelliptic class in S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q. By (5.2), z * bar b(x) = bar b(iota * x) = bar b(x): the hyperelliptic classes are z-invariant in S. Since z is *central* in Sp_{12}(Z), for any g in Sp_{12}(Z) we get z*(g * bar b(x)) = g*(z * bar b(x)) = g * bar b(x). Thus z acts trivially on the Sp_{12}(Z)-submodule generated by the images of the hyperelliptic classes. By (5.3) that submodule is all of S (the surjection St_6 tensor Q ->> S is Mod_6-equivariant and the Mod_6-action on S factors through Sp_{12}(Z)). Hence z acts trivially on S, i.e.

  S = S^+  and  S^- = 0.

By (4.1) and (5.4), (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = 0. By Step 4 and (3.1),
