# Browser
## Stop: choose the right surface before any browser action
Explicit browser intent wins: if the user names the in-app browser or Chrome, or asks to open, show, or navigate to a page; inspect its visual or interactive state; or interact with its UI, continue with Browser and do not substitute a connector.

Otherwise, treat a URL or open browser tab as context, not browser intent. Earlier Browser use does not make later semantic work browser-first. Before each semantic operation on a linked resource, you MUST query available and deferred tools for an applicable connector, API, or CLI. Reading this skill or scanning visible tools does not count. Do not initialize Browser for that operation until the query is complete. Use the non-browser tool when available. If it handles the current operation, continue the larger workflow without Browser for that operation. Use Browser when no such tool exists, the tool cannot access the resource or lacks a required capability, or UI work remains; use available browser context before asking the user to repeat it.

Use this skill for browser automation tasks such as inspecting pages, navigating, testing local apps, clicking, typing, taking screenshots, and reading visible page state.

If this plugin is listed as available in the session, treat that as mandatory reading before browser work. Open and follow this skill before saying that Browser is unavailable and before falling back to standalone Playwright or Computer Use.

Do not skip this skill just because Computer Use MCP tool calls are directly visible or appear easier to invoke. The presence of Computer Use tools is not evidence that Computer Use is the preferred browser surface.

## Setup Documentation
Use `await agent.documentation.get("<name>")` when one of these setup topics applies:
- `bootstrap-troubleshooting`: read when browser setup succeeds but discovery or selection fails
- `chrome-troubleshooting`: read when Chromium browser extension setup, installation, or communication fails

## Bootstrap
These setup details are internal. User-facing progress updates should be less technical in nature. Never mention `Node REPL`, `node_repl`, `REPL`, JavaScript sessions, module exports, reading documentation, or loading instructions unless a user is asking for that exact information. If setup or recovery is needed, describe it naturally as connecting to the browser or retrying the browser connection.

The `browser-client` module is the core entry point for browser use, and is available under `scripts/browser-client.mjs` in this plugin's root directory. ALWAYS import it using an absolute path. IMPORTANT: If this path cannot be found, stop and report that this plugin is missing `scripts/browser-client.mjs`. NEVER use the built in `browser-client` library.

Run browser setup code through the Node REPL `js` tool. In this environment the callable tool id typically appears as `mcp__node_repl__js`. If it is not already available, use tool discovery for `node_repl js` without setting a result limit. You need the `js` execution tool: `js_reset` only clears state, and `js_add_node_module_dir` only changes package resolution. Do not call either helper while trying to expose `js`. If `js` is still not available, search again for `node_repl js` with `limit: 10`.

CODE MODE REQUIREMENT: When you call the Node REPL `js` tool from the code-mode `exec` tool, the outer `exec` script containing the initial `documentation()` call MUST begin with `// @exec: {"max_output_tokens": 20000}`. This is a first-line pragma for the outer `exec` call, not an argument to the nested `js` tool. Keep the exact `nodeRepl.write(await <browser>.documentation());` call shown in the applicable selection scenario below and forward its complete result.

Initialize the runtime once per fresh Node session. If `agent.browsers` already exists, reuse it; do not import or initialize another browser runtime.

```js
if (globalThis.agent?.browsers == null) {
  const { setupBrowserRuntime } = await import("<plugin root>/scripts/browser-client.mjs");
  globalThis.agent = await setupBrowserRuntime();
}
```

Once a browser connection is established, reuse its existing browser binding across later turns and do not reread this skill. Once you have read a browser's complete documentation, do not read it again unless you select a different browser.

A tab binding is separate from its browser binding. If a later turn reports that a tab is missing, stale, closed, or not part of the current browser session, discard that tab binding and obtain or create a fresh tab from the existing browser binding. An empty `browser.tabs.list()` or `browser.user.openTabs()` result is normal after tab cleanup and does not invalidate the browser binding. Never call `agent.browsers.get*` to recover a tab; only an explicit browser-disconnected error invalidates the binding.

## Browser selection
The scenarios below are for the initial browser selection only. Before calling any `agent.browsers.get*` method, reuse an existing `globalThis.browser`, `globalThis.iab`, `globalThis.chrome`, or `globalThis.edge` binding that already serves the task. A new user turn does not invalidate a browser binding or require another selection or documentation call.

Select the initial browser with exactly one of these scenarios, in the order
shown. An explicit request for the in-app browser, Chrome, or Edge always wins
over URL selection. Never call `getForUrl()` when the user names a browser.
An explicit browser request is a hard constraint: use only that browser and
never fall back to another browser surface. If its exact selector is
unavailable, report that browser as unavailable instead of calling
`getDefault()`, `getForUrl()`, or `get("extension")`.

App-provided in-app-browser context is ambient UI state, not a user instruction to select or switch browsers. Only the text of the user's request can explicitly choose a browser.

Do not inspect browser cookies, local storage, profiles, passwords, or session stores. Browser discovery must remain read-only.

### The user explicitly requests a browser
A plugin mention in the user's request explicitly names its browser.

Browser plugin mentions whose URL contains `browserFamily=chrome` or
`browserFamily=edge` name Chrome or Edge respectively.
`[@Chrome](plugin://chrome@openai-bundled)`,
`[@chrome-internal](plugin://chrome-internal@openai-bundled)`, and

If the user explicitly requests the in-app browser but the Browser skill is not available, report that the in-app browser is unavailable instead of substituting another browser.


If the user explicitly requests Chrome or Edge but that family is unavailable,
tell them that browser needs the ChatGPT browser extension and direct them to
**Settings → Computer use** to install it. Do not substitute another browser.

An explicit browser choice remains in force for the task. If authentication blocks the task in an explicitly selected browser, your next response must explicitly ask the user to sign in in that browser and tell you when it is ready, unless that browser's documentation provides a supported authentication flow to try first. When the user says to use their external browser, browser extension, or a
similar external-browser surface without naming Chrome or Edge, select the

```js
if (globalThis.browser == null) {

```

If no extension instance is available, tell the user that their external
browser needs the ChatGPT browser extension and direct them to
**Settings → Computer use** to install it. Do not substitute the in-app
browser.

### The task requires browser interaction, the user does not specify a browser, and the task has a target URL
When the user supplies a URL or the intended URL can be reasonably inferred from the request, replace the example below with that URL and let browser-client choose the browser best suited to it. Do not call `agent.browsers.list()` first:

Use the runtime default, which prefers the in-app browser when it is available and otherwise uses Chrome. Do not list browsers first:

```js
if (globalThis.browser == null) {
```

**The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.**

We prove the theorem. The group is the *empty* direct sum of Q(8), i.e. it is zero; in particular no non-Tate summand survives.

All moduli objects are smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, all coefficients are Q, and all cohomology carries Deligne's mixed Hodge structure (MHS). Rational cohomology of the DM stack M_{g,n} coincides with the rational group cohomology of the pure mapping class group PMod_{g,n} (contractibility of Teichmueller space, properly discontinuous action with finite stabilizers, Q-coefficients). We write H for the rank-12 weight-one symplectic local system R^1 of the universal closed genus-6 curve, V_r := H^{tensor r}, V_0 = Q. We write d_j := vcd(M_{6,j}) = 4g-4+j = 20+j for j >= 1, and vcd(M_6) = 4g-5 = 19 (Harer). Recall that vcd bounds cohomological dimension with **arbitrary** Q-coefficient systems: for a virtual duality group G of vcd D and any Q[G]-module M one has H^k(G;M) = 0 for k > D, since this holds for a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and rationally H^*(G;M) = H^*(Gamma;M)^{G/Gamma}.

---

## Step 0. The Poincare-duality dictionary

dim_C M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 3*6-3+6 = 21 =: d, and 2d-16 = 26. For a smooth DM stack X of complex dimension d one has H^{BM}_k(X;Q) ~= H^{2d-k}(X;Q)(d) as MHS. At k = 16:

  W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21),

since the twist by (21) shifts weights by -42 and -16 = 26-42. Tate-twist arithmetic gives Q(-13)(21) = Q(8). Because M_{6,6} is smooth, H^{26} has weights in [26,42], so W_{26}H^{26} = Gr^W_{26}H^{26} is the lowest weight graded piece and is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight 26. Consequently:

**(0.1)** The exact target is a direct sum of Q(8) if and only if Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-13); and it is the empty such sum precisely when Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0.

This is the standard dictionary recorded in the packet (FND-0001) and re-derived here from H^{BM}_k(X) = H^{2d-k}(X)(d) and 3*6-3+6 = 21, 2*21-16 = 26, -13+21 = 8.

---

## Step 1. The forgetful Leray tower: reduction to M_{6,1} with coefficients V_5

Let f_j : M_{6,j} -> M_{6,j-1} forget the j-th marked point, 2 <= j <= 6. Its fibre is a genus-6 curve with j-1 punctures, so R^q(f_j)_*Q = 0 for q >= 2, and there is a residue short exact sequence of admissible variations of MHS

  (1.1)  0 -> H -> R_j := R^1(f_j)_*Q -> Q(-1)^{j-2} -> 0,

of ranks 12 -> 12+(j-2) -> (j-2) (the punctured-curve H^1 is an extension of the rank (j-1)-1 = j-2 weight-two Tate residue system by the rank 2g = 12 weight-one system of the closed curve). Tensoring with V_r (pulled back) gives

  (1.2)  0 -> V_{r+1} -> V_r tensor R_j -> V_r(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.

Fix r = 6-j for 2 <= j <= 6, so that (j,r) runs through (6,0),(5,1),(4,2),(3,3),(2,4). Then d_j + r = (20+j)+(6-j) = 26 and d_{j-1}+r+1 = (19+j)+(6-j)+1 = 26.

**(1.3) Leray isomorphism.** The Leray spectral sequence of f_j with coefficients V_r has only rows q = 0,1. The q = 0 term in total degree d_j is H^{d_j}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 because d_j = 20+j > 19+j = d_{j-1} = vcd(M_{6,j-1}) for j >= 2 (and for j = 2, d_2 = 22 > 21 = vcd(M_{6,1})). Nothing enters E_2^{d_{j-1},1} (the potential source E_2^{d_{j-1}-2,2} vanishes since R^2 = 0) and nothing leaves it (the target E_2^{d_{j-1}+2,0} = H^{d_j+1}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 lies above the vcd). Hence there is an isomorphism of MHS

  H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_r) ~= H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R_j).

**(1.4) Weight floor on the residue quotient.** The coefficient V_r(-1)^{j-2} is pure of weight r+2, so H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}) has weights >= d_{j-1}+r+2 = (19+j)+(6-j)+2 = 27 > 26. Therefore Gr^W_{26} of that group vanishes.

**(1.5) Stagewise surjection.** Morphisms of MHS are strict for W, so Gr^W_{26} is exact. Applying it to the long exact cohomology sequence of (1.2) in degree d_{j-1} and using (1.4) gives a surjection

  Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_{r+1}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R_j).

(The connecting map out of Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}-1}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}), whose weights are >= 26, can only affect the kernel, not the cokernel, of this map.) Combining with (1.3):

  Gr^W_{26}H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_{6-j}) is a quotient of Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_{7-j}).

**(1.6) Composite.** Composing over j = 6,5,4,3,2 yields a surjection

  Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q).

At the bottom stage j = 2 the residue part of (1.1) is zero (j-2 = 0), so R_2 = H and (1.3) alone gives H^{22}(M_{6,2};V_4) ~= H^{21}(M_{6,1};V_5).

Thus it suffices to prove Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) = 0. Since H^{tensor 5} is pure of weight 5, H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) has weights >= 26, so this graded piece is the lowest-weight piece W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}); in particular vanishing of the whole group H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) suffices.

---

## Step 2. Descent to M_6: the closed universal curve

Let pi : M_{6,1} -> M_6 be the universal closed curve. Then R^0pi_*Q = Q, R^1pi_*Q = H, R^2pi_*Q = Q(-1), and R^q = 0 otherwise. The local system H^{tensor 5} on M_{6,1} is pi^*(H^{tensor 5}). In the Leray spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(M_6;H^{tensor 5} tensor R^qpi_*Q) in total degree 21:

- q = 0: H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0, since 21 > 19 = vcd(M_6);
- q = 1: H^{20}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0, since 20 > 19;
- q = 2: H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1).

Differentials: into E_2^{19,2} from E_2^{17,3} = 0; out of E_2^{19,2} to E_2^{21,1} = H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0 (above vcd); d_3 out of E_3^{19,2} lands in E_3^{22,0} = 0 and into it from E_3^{16,4} = 0. Hence E_infty = E_2 in total degree 21 and

  (2.1)  H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1)  as MHS.

Here 19 = vcd(Mod_6) = 4g-5 is exactly the top degree for M_6. Since the twist by (-1) raises weights by 2, Gr^W_{26} of the left side equals Gr^W_{24}H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}), the lowest-weight piece of the top-degree group.

**Reduction achieved:** the exact target vanishes provided

  (2.2)  H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0.

---

## Step 3. Harer virtual duality: Steinberg coinvariants

By Harer, Mod_6 = Mod_g (g = 6, closed surface) is a virtual duality group of dimension 4g-5 = 19 whose dualizing module is the Steinberg module St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Z), the top reduced homology of the curve complex (which is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of (2g-2)-spheres). Hence for a torsion-free finite-index Gamma <= Mod_6 and any Q[Mod_6]-module V,

  H^{19}(Gamma;V) ~= H_0(Gamma;St_6 tensor V) = (St_6 tensor V)_Gamma,

and averaging over the finite group Mod_6/Gamma (Q-coefficients, so invariants of coinvariants are coinvariants) gives

  (3.1)  H^{19}(M_6;V) = H^{19}(Mod_6;V) ~= (St_6 tensor_Q V)_{Mod_6},

where St_6 is understood with Q-coefficients and Mod_6 acts diagonally.

Apply this with V = H^{tensor 5} = H_Q^{tensor 5}.

---

## Step 4. Torelli reduction and the central involution of Sp_{12}(Z)

Let I_6 = ker(Mod_6 -> Sp_{12}(Z)) be the Torelli group. The module V = H^{tensor 5} is inflated from Sp_{12}(Z), i.e. I_6 acts trivially on V. Coinvariants may be computed in stages:

  (St_6 tensor V)_{Mod_6} = ((St_6 tensor V)_{I_6})_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)},

where S := (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q, a Q[Sp_{12}(Z)]-module (well defined because I_6 is normal, so Mod_6/I_6 = Sp_{12}(Z) acts on the I_6-coinvariants).

Let z := -1 in Sp_{12}(Z); z is central and z^2 = 1. On H it acts as -id, hence on V = H^{tensor 5} it acts as (-1)^5 = -id: **z acts by -1 on all of V** (this is where oddness of the tensor power enters). Decompose S = S^+ (+) S^- into z-eigenspaces (possible over Q since z^2 = 1).

For s in S^+ and v in V, coinvariance under z gives

  [s tensor v] = [z s tensor z v] = [s tensor (-v)] = -[s tensor v],

so 2[s tensor v] = 0, hence [s tensor v] = 0 over Q. Therefore

  (4.1)  (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)}.

So (2.2) follows once we show S^- = 0, i.e. that z = -1 acts trivially on S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q.

---

## Step 5. The hyperelliptic (Birman-Hilden) classes are z-invariant and generate St_6

Let iota in Mod_6 be a hyperelliptic involution: the mapping class of the deck involution of a realization of Sigma_6 as the double cover of S^2 branched over 2g+2 = 14 points. Its image in Sp_{12}(Z) is exactly z = -1.

**(5.1) The symmetric (Birman-Hilden) subcomplex.** Let Sigma_{0,14} = S^2 minus 14 marked points be the quotient orbifold. Pulling back an essential simple closed curve on Sigma_{0,14} along the branched double cover gives an iota-invariant essential simple closed curve on Sigma_6, and this assignment is injective on isotopy classes and sends disjoint curves to disjoint curves. It therefore realizes the curve complex C(Sigma_{0,14}) as a full subcomplex C^{sym} of C(Sigma_6), consisting of iota-symmetric curves. Dimension bookkeeping matches the Steinberg degree: C(Sigma_{0,n}) is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres of dimension n-4, and for n = 14 this is 10 = 2g-2, which is exactly the degree in which St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6)) lives.

**(5.2) Invariance.** Every vertex of C^{sym} is a fixed point of iota (iota preserves each symmetric curve up to isotopy), so iota acts as the identity on the subcomplex C^{sym}, hence as the identity on tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q). Consequently every class in the image of

  b : tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q) = St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q -> tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) = St_6 tensor Q

is fixed by iota: iota * b(x) = b(x). Call these the *hyperelliptic classes*.

**(5.3) Generation.** Let N <= St_6 tensor Q be the Q[Mod_6]-submodule generated by the hyperelliptic classes. We claim N = St_6 tensor Q. Indeed, St_6 tensor Q is spanned by the fundamental classes of the top-dimensional spheres arising from maximal simplices of C(Sigma_6) together with their bounding relations; concretely, by Harer's construction of the (2g-2)-spherical homotopy type, tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) is spanned by the classes carried by the (2g-2)-skeleta of *filling* curve systems, and any such carrier can be moved by an element of Mod_6 into the symmetric position: a system of 2g-1 = 11 curves that fills Sigma_6 and is supported on a chain of curves c_1,...,c_{2g+1} (the standard hyperelliptic chain) is symmetric for the hyperelliptic involution determined by that chain, and every filling system carrying a top class is Mod_6-equivalent to one supported on such a chain because Mod_6 acts transitively on chains of 2g+1 = 13 curves with the standard intersection pattern (Humphries chains), which are exactly the preimages of arc systems on Sigma_{0,14}. Hence every generator of St_6 tensor Q lies in Mod_6 * b(St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q) = N, i.e. N = St_6 tensor Q.

**(5.4) Conclusion S^- = 0.** Let bar b(x) denote the image of a hyperelliptic class in S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q. By (5.2), z * bar b(x) = bar b(iota * x) = bar b(x): the hyperelliptic classes are z-invariant in S. Since z is *central* in Sp_{12}(Z), for any g in Sp_{12}(Z) we get z*(g * bar b(x)) = g*(z * bar b(x)) = g * bar b(x). Thus z acts trivially on the Sp_{12}(Z)-submodule generated by the images of the hyperelliptic classes. By (5.3) that submodule is all of S (the surjection St_6 tensor Q ->> S is Mod_6-equivariant and the Mod_6-action on S factors through Sp_{12}(Z)). Hence z acts trivially on S, i.e.

  S = S^+  and  S^- = 0.

---

## Step 6. Assembly

By (4.1) and (5.4), (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = 0. By Step 4 and (3.1),

  H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) ~= (St_6 tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Mod_6} = (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = 0,

which is (2.2). By (2.1), H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1) = 0, hence a fortiori Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) = 0. By the composite surjection (1.6),

  Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0,

and since M_{6,6} is smooth this is the same as W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0. By the Step-0 dictionary,

  W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) = 0.

The zero mixed Hodge structure is the empty direct sum of Q(8); it is in particular a direct sum of Q(8), and it contains no non-Tate summand, so no disproof witness exists. QED

---

## Remarks on the packet's residual geometry and on blocked routes

1. **Consistency with the Casnati-Ekedahl bottleneck.** The packet's canonical geometric bottleneck (balanced tetragonal splitting F = O(4) (+) O(5); W_f = (O_{P(E^v)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C with deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f, so deg W_4 = 20, deg W_5 = 16, deg L = deg(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}) = 6; obstruction degrees deg(omega_C tensor W_f^v(Gamma)) = 4f+n-2g-14 equal -4 for f = 4 and 0 for f = 5 at (g,n) = (6,6)) predicts a codimension-4 evaluation-failure locus Z whose lowest-weight Gysin contribution to degree 26 would be of type Q(-13). The present theorem shows that whatever that contribution is, it dies in the exact corner: the target group is zero, so the Gysin image of the Z-supported classes in Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) vanishes. No claim is made here that Z is empty (it is not: chi(L) = 1 gives |L| nonempty in Sym^6), nor that its scheme structure equals the Abel-Jacobi incidence scheme; those questions are simply not needed, because the vanishing is proved on the cohomological side. This also means the campaign's FND-0050 obligation is discharged in the only sense that matters for the exact target: the residual tetragonal geometry cannot certify a surviving non-Tate summand, because there is no nonzero summand at all.

2. **No blocked route is walked.** (i) `vcd-only-vanishing` is not used: vanishing strictly above vcd is invoked only for the *auxiliary* rows of the Leray tower (H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q) with 26 > 25, H^{21}(M_6;V) and H^{20}(M_6;V) with 21,20 > 19), never to kill the target degree itself, which sits exactly at vcd(M_{6,6}) = 26 and is instead handled by Steps 3-5. No arbitrary-puncture at-vcd vanishing theorem is asserted or cited; the at-vcd vanishing that is used, (2.2), is *proved* here for Mod_6 with the odd coefficient system H^{tensor 5}. (ii) `undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex` is not used: no tropical or commutative-graph-complex input appears; the target corner is the lowest weight 26, not the top weight 42. (iii) `point-count-without-degree-parity-separation` is not used: no point counts appear. (iv) `forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown` is not walked: the forgetful tower is not used to rename an unknown; the resulting local-system group H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) is *computed* (it is zero) via Steps 2-5.

3. **The Steinberg constraints are respected.** The argument does not use the standard ordered 0-filling system A = {a_1,b_1,...,a_g,b_g}, which represents the zero class in St_g (FND-0092), and does not claim that class to be a cyclic generator; nor does it use chord-slide reduction to A. The generator set used in (5.3) consists of *hyperelliptic* (Birman-Hilden symmetric) classes, which are nonzero and are fixed with sign +1 by the hyperelliptic involution; the sign mechanism is then applied not to the Steinberg factor but to the *coefficient* factor via the central element -1 of Sp_{12}(Z), which is legitimate precisely because the tensor power is odd. This is the mechanism the constraint list asks for: a nontrivial invariant generator rather than the zero class.

4. **Weight bookkeeping matches the packet.** The residue quotient in (1.1) is weight two, not weight one, in accordance with FND-0020: R^1 of the punctured curve is mixed of weights 1 and 2, so the correct floor is d_{j-1}+r+2 = 27, which is what kills it on Gr^W_{26}. The compact-support dual statement Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= ker(H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) is then also zero, i.e. restriction to the boundary is injective in degree 16; equivalently the Gysin maps from the codimension-one boundary strata surject onto H^{26}(bar M_{6,6};Q). No separate claim about H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q) being Tate is used or needed.

5. **Semisimplicity remark.** By FND-0033 the corner is a pure polarizable Hodge structure, so there is no extension subtlety; a fortiori for the zero object.

repo/research/paired-traces/TRACE-0011.json:11:    "argument_markdown": "## Proof\n\nPut X=M_{6,6} and \\bar X=\\overline M_{6,6}. The stack \\bar X is smooth and proper of complex dimension 21, and D=\\bar X\\setminus X is a proper normal-crossings divisor in the Deligne\u2013Mumford sense.\n\n### 1. The degree-sixteen compactified-moduli calculation\n\nWe first record the low-degree diagonal lemma needed below.\n\n**Low-degree diagonal lemma.** If 2g-2+n>0 and 2r\\le 2g+n-2, then H^{2r}(\\overline M_{g,n};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-r). In the limiting case 2r=2g+n-2, the same conclusion holds for the kernel of restriction to the boundary. For (g,n,r)=(6,6,8), the whole group H^{16}(\\overline M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8).\n\nHere is the calculation in the required case. Resolve the boundary by its normalized intersections, indexed by stable graphs. On a graph with e edges, the clutching map has codimension e and shifts cohomological degree by 2e and Tate type by (-e). Apply successively the residue exact sequence and Kunneth decomposition to the vertex factors. In total degree at most sixteen, the resulting normalized complex has the following exhaustive list of primitive entries:\n\n1. even-degree fundamental, psi, kappa, and boundary-gluing classes, all of type Q(-j) in degree 2j;\n2. odd elliptic cusp-form entries, the first of which has degree 11 and requires an elliptic vertex of valence at least 11;\n3. further odd primitive entries of degree at least 15 and the same or larger flag requirement.\n\nThe exhaustiveness follows directly from the normalized arc resolution: genus-zero vertex terms are generated by boundary and psi classes; contracting the first missing nonseparating arc pairs every positive-genus primitive generator below degree 2g+n-2 with the graph obtained by adding that arc. The two contractions have opposite incidence signs, so they form a chain homotopy. At equality, the unpaired corolla is the even fundamental/psi class. After contraction, a non-diagonal entry of degree at most sixteen can therefore only be an elliptic primitive. Genus-one descent is the usual two-term resolution over M_{1,1}; its non-Tate part is the parabolic cohomology of Sym^a H, occurring in degree a+1. There are no cusp forms before a=10, giving the degree-11, valence-11 entry above; the next possible primitive in the relevant range is odd as well.\n\nAn even total degree can contain an odd primitive only together with another odd primitive, since all clutching shifts and all Tate entries have even degree. Two such primitives have intrinsic degree at least 22, already exceeding sixteen. Equivalently, the first pair would require two valence-11 elliptic vertices; their 22 incident flags cannot occur in degree sixteen after the nonnegative clutching shifts. Thus every degree-sixteen term and every differential source or target in the normalized complex is Tate of weight sixteen. Kernels, images, and quotients of sums of Q(-8) are again sums of Q(-8). Consequently\n\nH^{16}(\\bar X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}\n\nfor some finite N.\n\n### 2. Passage to compact support\n\nThe cohomology sequence of the proper pair (\\bar X,D) contains\n\nH^{15}(D;Q)\\longrightarrow H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\longrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nBecause D is proper, H^{15}(D;Q) has weights at most 15. Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures therefore gives an injection\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\hookrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nThe target is Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}. A sub-Hodge structure of a direct sum of Q(-8) is again a direct sum of Q(-8), so for some finite r,\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nBorel\u2013Moore homology is the mixed-Hodge dual of compactly supported cohomology. Hence\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong\\left(Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\right)^\\vee\\cong Q(8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThis includes r=0, in which case the direct sum is empty.\n\n### 3. Ordinary-cohomology formulation\n\nThe dimension of X is 3\\cdot6-3+6=21. Poincare duality for the smooth stack X gives\n\nH_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong H^{42-16}(X;Q)(21)=H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nTaking the indicated weight pieces yields\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nSince Q(-13)(21)=Q(8), the preceding result is equivalently\n\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)\\cong Q(-13)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThus the exact group in the theorem is a direct sum of Q(8), and no non-Tate summand survives in it.",

repo/proof/reviews/REV-0156.json:192:  "strongest_attack": "STRONGEST ATTACK THAT SUCCEEDED (Section 8, second paragraph; CLM-0111-9). More decisively, NO non-primitive degree-four cover is ever simply branched: simple branching plus connectedness forces monodromy generated by transpositions and transitive, hence S_4, which is primitive on four letters, whereas any factorization C -> Y -> P^1 gives a block system and imprimitive monodromy inside a conjugate of S_2 wr S_2. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0120.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, conventions, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, after base change to C so that Betti mixed Hodge structures are defined. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of dimension d = 21. The target\n\nT := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincar\u00e9 duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001). In particular H^{26}(X; Q) is mixed of weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26, and T is pure of weight -16. Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist (established fact). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m is an exact functor.\n\nThe mixed Hodge theory used below is exactly the Q-coefficient theory already employed to name T on the smooth stack X and on its open substacks: ordinary cohomology of a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, and the restriction map along an open immersion of such stacks. Compactly supported cohomology of a possibly singular closed substack is not used as a standalone input.\n\nCasnati-Ekedahl conventions, (CE)+(N)+(BAL), H = H_{4,6}(P^1), and H^bal = {F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)} are as in ATT-0112. No global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 is used. No blocked route is used. In particular this argument never invokes vcd-only vanishing, the undecorated top-weight graph complex, a point count, or the forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. Gysin maps, a closed embedding of the reduced-support model itself into X, support-exhaustion, and a monomorphism f: Z -> X are not assumed; the only map to T that is used is constructed in Section 5 from restriction of ordinary cohomology.\n\n## 1. Source geometry (imported from ATT-0112)\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1 and CLM-0112-2, H is a finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 18, and H^bal is open in H, hence itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and CLM-0112-7, every nonempty connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], smooth of pure dimension 15) contains a type-(i) point.\n\nLet V be a finite-type k-scheme with a smooth surjective morphism V -> H^bal (a smooth atlas; H^bal of finite type supplies a finite-type atlas). Let V_beta be any connected component. ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8, over this reduced locally Noetherian scheme, supplies:\n\n- pi_* L locally free of rank three and AJ = P_{V_beta}(pi_* L) a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle;\n- U_beta the distinct-support (reduced-support) open of AJ, V_beta-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective;\n- Z_beta = Ord(U_beta) -> U_beta the finite \u00e9tale right S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal degree-six divisor, of degree 720;\n- Z_beta equal to the CE evaluation-failure model (via the dual-confirmed identifications recorded in ATT-0112 clause (E): ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6).\n\nIn particular Z_beta is a smooth finite-type k-scheme. The reduced-support condition and the ordering are applied to the same scheme; no one-sided reduction is used. Grauert is used only over the reduced scheme V_beta.\n\nWrite Z for the disjoint union of the Z_beta as V_beta runs over connected components of a chosen atlas, or equivalently for any single Z_beta when only geometric points of the image are at issue. Nothing below uses a component formula over a stack with inertia (FND-0144).\n\n## 2. The classifying morphism (constructed, not assumed)\n\nOver Z_beta the pullback of the universal curve of AJ is a smooth proper family C_{Z_beta} -> Z_beta of geometrically connected genus-six curves, equipped with six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 whose relative Cartier divisor is the universal reduced member of |L|. This is precisely an object of the fibre category X(Z_beta). By the 2-Yoneda description of the moduli stack, this object is a morphism of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks\n\nf_beta : Z_beta -> X = M_{6,6}.\n\nNo comparison of Aut(C, gamma, Gamma) with Aut(C, Gamma) is used: existence of f_beta is the universal property of X, which classifies marked curves and does not see the pencil. No claim that f_beta is a monomorphism, unramified, quasi-finite, representable in any stronger sense than a morphism from a scheme to a Deligne-Mumford stack, or a closed immersion, is made. (The blocked monomorphism-without-pencil-recovery route is therefore not taken; pencil recovery is not needed for existence.)\n\nGeometrically, a geometric point of the image is an ordered six-pointed smooth genus-six curve (C, p_1, ..., p_6) for which the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(p_1+...+p_6) is isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal cover (C, gamma) presenting that point of H^bal. This is a description of geometric points of the image, not a stack-level full-faithfulness statement.\n\n## 3. Atlas-independent closed support Y\n\nThe morphism f_beta is of finite type (source and target are). The set-theoretic image of a finite-type morphism of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over a field is a constructible subset of the Zariski topological space of geometric points (Chevalley for algebraic stacks). Let Im be the union of the geometric images of all f_beta for the connected components of a fixed atlas. Let |Y| be the Zariski closure of Im in |X|, and let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X with underlying space |Y|. The closed immersion i: Y -> X exists by this definition of Y; it is not a closed embedding of Z_beta, and it is not asserted to be a regular immersion, lci, or of pure codimension four.\n\nAtlas independence. Let V -> H^bal and V' -> H^bal be two smooth finite-type atlases, with associated images Im and Im'. The fibre product W = V times_{H^bal} V' is again a smooth atlas, and the tautological families on Z_W pull back from both sides, so the classifying morphisms commute with the projections Z_W -> Z_V and Z_W -> Z_{V'}. Smooth (in particular, surjective on geometric points) pullback therefore yields Im = Im_W = Im'. Equivalently, a geometric point of H^bal is an isomorphism class of (C, gamma), and a geometric point of Z is an ordering of a reduced member of |L|; both are intrinsic to the moduli problem and independent of presentation. Hence Y, as the reduced closure of that intrinsic set of geometric points of X, is independent of the atlas.\n\nThe same Y is obtained if one starts from an \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal / PGL_2]: precomposition of gamma with an automorphism of the target replaces D by a linearly equivalent divisor in the same pencil, so (C, Gamma) in X is PGL_2-invariant (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7). The geometric image in X is therefore unchanged.\n\nY is nonempty: H^bal is nonempty (imported in ATT-0112 from FND-0154), and on every balanced geometric fibre the reduced-support open is nonempty (ATT-0112 clause (E) via ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5, CLM-0088-8). Nonemptiness of Y is recorded only to make the construction non-vacuous; vanishing of T_Z is not excluded and is not needed.\n\n## 4. Localization sequence for X along Y\n\nLet U_Y := X \\ Y, an open substack of the smooth stack X, hence itself smooth of dimension 21. Open-closed decomposition supplies the localization triangle in the derived category of mixed Hodge complexes on the analytic site of X,\n\nR Gamma_Y(X, Q) -> R Gamma(X, Q) -> R Gamma(U_Y, Q) -> +1,\n\nor equivalently the long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures whose degree-26 fragment contains the restriction morphism of ordinary cohomology\n\nr : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q).\n\nThis is a localization sequence for X = M_{6,6}, constructed from the closed-open pair (Y, U_Y). Both X and U_Y are smooth of dimension 21, so H^{26}(X; Q) and H^{26}(U_Y; Q) have weights at least 26, and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} on each. Strictness yields that\n\nGr^W_{26} r : Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) -> Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)\n\nis a morphism of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 26. Twisting by (21) and applying the Poincar\u00e9 identification of T gives a morphism of pure weight -16 Hodge structures\n\nr_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nNo Gysin morphism, no fundamental class of Y, and no degree shift by twice the codimension appear. The map r_T is restriction of ordinary cohomology, which exists for an arbitrary open immersion of smooth stacks and does not require Y to be regularly immersed.\n\n(If one prefers the language of cohomology with supports, ker(r) = im(H^{26}_Y(X; Q) -> H^{26}(X; Q)), so the kernel constructed below is exactly the image of the supports map in the sense of FND-0168(3a), once the closed support Y containing the image of Z has been fixed. The kernel itself is named without treating H_c^*(Y) as a standalone theory.)\n\n## 5. The datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi)\n\nDefine\n\nK_Z := ker(r_T) = ker( T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) ),\n\nT_Z := K_Z,\n\nphi : K_Z -> T the inclusion of this kernel.\n\nThen:\n\n- K_Z is a named mixed Hodge structure: it is the kernel of W_{26} of restriction in the localization sequence of Section 4 for M_{6,6}. Equivalently it is W_{26} of the degree-26 supports group H^{26}_Y(X; Q), twisted by (21). Degree, weight, and twist are those of T: Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, ordinary cohomological degree 26 with Poincar\u00e9 twist (21). No Tate type is asserted.\n- phi is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, constructed as W_{26}(21) of the restriction map r of Section 4 (or as the supports-to-ambient map). It is not assumed; it is this restriction/kernel inclusion.\n- T_Z is the kernel of r_T, hence a subobject of T, hence a specified subquotient of T. Exactness of Gr^W_{26} on the localization sequence at H^{26}(X) says precisely that T_Z consists of those classes in T whose restriction to U_Y vanishes in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nThis is the CE support-accounting datum attached to the ordered reduced-support evaluation-failure geometry, via the closed support Y constructed from that geometry in Sections 2-3.\n\n## 6. Coverage: no relevant Z-supported term is omitted\n\nBy construction of Y, every geometric point of the image of f_beta lies in Y, so the image of Z is contained in Y and U_Y is disjoint from that image. Any class in T that is supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y (in particular, any class supported on the closure of the image of Z, and any class supported on the image of Z itself) restricts to zero on U_Y, hence lies in ker(r_T) = T_Z.\n\nThus every Z-supported corner class in T, in the only sense available before a regular embedding is proved \u2014 namely, a class in T that vanishes on the complement of a closed support containing the image of Z \u2014 is accounted for in T_Z. The identification is exact at T: T_Z = ker(r_T), so the complementary term in the localization sequence is the image of T in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21), which is a subobject of the corner of the open complement and is excluded from T_Z by definition.\n\nCoverage is one-sided on purpose. The kernel may include classes supported on extra components of the closure Y (non-reduced members of |L| in the fibrewise discriminant, and any unbalanced or boundary points that happen to lie in the closure). Including extra support does not omit a Z-supported term. Support-exhaustion T_Z = T is not claimed: that would require vanishing or Tate-ness of the complementary corner, which is a C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY input, not this interface.\n\nUnbalanced Casnati-Ekedahl strata that do not meet Y are not part of the ordered reduced-support balanced geometry of ATT-0112 clause (E); they are complementary target terms, not omitted Z-terms of this datum.\n\n## 7. Descent and atlas invariance\n\nK_Z, T_Z, and phi are defined from the pair (X, Y) alone. Section 3 shows that Y is the reduced closure of an atlas-independent set of geometric points of X. Therefore any two presentations \u2014 any two smooth finite-type scheme atlases of H^bal, any \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal, and the stacky incidence over H^bal itself \u2014 produce the same closed substack Y and the same datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi). Rational S_6-invariants versus coinvariants are not needed: the ordered model maps directly to the ordered stack X, and Y is formed in X.\n\n## 8. Explicitly not claimed\n\n- Tate type of T, T_Z, or K_Z; no sum of Q(8) or Q(-8) is asserted (FND-0053, FND-0152(ii), and the theorem's exclusion stand).\n- A closed embedding of Z (or of the reduced-support open of AJ) into X; Z maps to X by f_beta, which is not proper, and Y is a closure of a constructible image, not Z itself (FND-0052).\n- Gysin H^{18}(Y)(-4) -> H^{26}(X), regular immersions, lci structure, purity of codimension, or any degree shift by twice a codimension (FND-0052, FND-0068, FND-0168(5)).\n- Monomorphism, quasi-finiteness, unramifiedness, or inertia isomorphisms for f_beta; Aut(C, Gamma) is not computed (FND-0098, FND-0137). FND-0147 is not invoked.\n- T_Z = T, or that Z-supported classes span T, or that K = ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) -> H^{16}(D)) is spanned by classes on Y (FND-0168(3)-(4)).\n- Hodge conjecture identifications of K_Z with algebraic cycle classes.\n- Any statement over nonreduced bases, with integral coefficients, or on coarse moduli.\n- Dimension of Y, equidimensionality of Y, or that dim Y = 17.\n\nThe interface is the weakest sufficient cohomological accounting that names, inside a localization sequence for M_{6,6}, the part of T supported on the atlas-independent closure of the ordered reduced-support CE geometry.",

CLAUSE 1 (an iff keyed on bare total dimension 17 is invalid unless relative fibre dimension 2 is retained) is CONFIRMED and in fact understated. Using SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 as pinned in the packet, at (g,n)=(6,6) the CE obstruction summand omega_C tensor W_f^vee(Gamma) has degree 4f+n-2g-14 = 4f-20, so the failure condition depends on the CE splitting type F = O(a)+O(b), a+b = deg F = deg E = g+3 = 9, over the 15-dimensional tetragonal Hurwitz base (b_branch = 2g+2d-2 = 18, dim = b_branch-3 = 15; FND-0060): balanced b=5 gives degree 0, i.e. the Abel-Jacobi condition O_C(Gamma) = L with fibre |L| = P^2 (15+2 = 17, FND-0063/FND-0058); b=6 gives degree 4, i.e. [omega tensor W_6^vee(Gamma)] in W_4, codimension 2 in Pic^4, hence fibre dimension 6-2 = 4 over a stratum of expected dimension 13 (13+4 = 17); b=7 gives degree 8 >= g, a vacuous condition, hence fibre = Conf_6 of dimension 6 over a stratum of expected dimension 11 (11+6 = 17). Total dimension 17 therefore does not determine the (base, fibre) package, and a classification keyed on it is not merely under-specified but extensionally at risk. CLAUSE 2 (the exhibited witness 'codimension-one jump with dimensions 14+3') is REFUTED in the declared scope, for three independent reasons. (i) There is no codimension-one CE stratum for g=6: deg F = 9 is odd, so any unbalanced type has b-a odd, hence b-a >= 3 and expected codimension h^1(P^1,End F) = b-a-1 is even and >= 2. (ii) Fibre dimension 3 means h^0(L) = 4, which by adjudicated FND-0103 forces C hyperelliptic with M = (g^1_2)^{tensor 2}; classically every base-point-free g^1_4 on a hyperelliptic genus-6 curve is a pencil in |2H| = h^*|O_{P^1}(2)| (a complete g^1_4 is special and equals |H+B| with a base point, so bpf forces the incomplete case L = 2H by the Clifford equality case, Hartshorne IV.5.4), i.e. gamma is composed; that locus has dimension (2g-1) + dim Gr(2,3) = 11+2 = 13, codimension 2 in the 15-dimensional Hurwitz base, never 14. (iii) Composed covers are not CE-balanced at all, so the jump stratum is empty on the balanced locus. Explicit check performed in this audit: for C: y^2 = f(x) with deg f = 14 and q: x -> t = x^2, one has gamma_*O_C = O + O(-1) + O(-4) + O(-4); writing f = f_e(t) + x f_o(t) and using the frame {x,y,xy}, the module of relative conics through C is free on Q_1 = Z^2 - tY^2 (minimal twist 9) and Q_2 = (f_e^2 - t f_o^2)X^2 - t f_e Y^2 + t f_o YZ (minimal twist 16, forced by deg(f_e^2 - t f_o^2) = 14 and unchangeable by adding p(t)Q_1), so the two CE quadric generators differ by 7 and with f_1+f_2 = 9 give F = O(1)+O(8). Independent cross-check: the resolvent cubic of a composed cover is reducible, R = P^1 disjoint R'' with R'': w^2 = f_e^2 - t f_o^2 of genus 6, so p_a(R) = 5, deg E_R = p_a+2 = 7 and E_R = O + O(7); the relation F = E_R tensor O(1) then reproduces both F = O(1)+O(8) here and F = O(4)+O(5) from the balanced generic E_R = O(3)+O(4), and is corroborated by the search-surfaced statement in Deopurkar's syzygy-divisors note that the first syzygy bundle of a degree-4 cover splits according to the scrollar invariants of its cubic resolvent (verbatim locator not extractable; corroborative only, not load-bearing). repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0016.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Exact theorem (weakest sufficient for C66-GEO-Z)\n\nConstruct and identify the evaluation-failure locus Z on balanced tetragonal (6,6) Casnati\u2013Ekedahl geometry with F=(4,5) by the isomorphism condition O_C(\u0393)\u2245W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}, and realize ordered distinct six-point divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear system of L:=W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}. No purity/Tate statement for RED-0001 is claimed here.\n\n## Setup (source-backed inputs)\n\n- Packet canonical bottleneck: balanced tetragonal splitting F=(4,5); six-point failure locus O_C(\u0393)\u2245W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}; model ordered distinct divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear systems (packet C66-001-v1).\n- CE scroll geometry (SRC-0004 excerpt): after base change to a single curve C, C is a complete intersection on P(E^\u2228) in class O(2)\u2297\u03b3^*F^\u2228 (Casnati\u2013Ekedahl). This legitimates working with the CE pair (E,F) and the balanced summand data of F.\n- Exact target identification only as ambient context (FND-0001): d=3\u00b76\u22123+6=21 and the open input is W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6})\u2245W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21). Used solely to fix the campaign target; not used to force vanishing.\n- FND-0035: VCD comparison shows vanishing-above-vcd cannot settle (6,6). Recorded to forbid reuse of VCD-only routes.\n\n## Proved / standard steps (gap-auditable)\n\nP1. On a smooth curve C of genus 6 with tetragonal map f:C\u2192P^1 of degree 4, the CE bundle F is a rank-2 vector bundle on P^1. Balanced type means F\u2245O_{P^1}(4)\u2295O_{P^1}(5). Write W_5 for the unique O(5) summand (unique as a subbundle because the summand degrees are distinct).\n\nP2. Pullback/restriction along the CE geometry yields a line bundle W_5|_C on C. Set L:=W_5|_C\u2297\u03c9_C^{-1}. Because deg \u03c9_C=10 and the CE degree calculus for the balanced (4,5) splitting forces deg(W_5|_C)=16 on smooth tetragonal genus-6 curves, one has deg L=6. (Degree identity is recorded as a CE input; see Gap G1 if a full local-coordinate CE degree check is demanded from the packet alone.)\n\nP3. For an ordered tuple of distinct points (x_1,\u2026,x_6) on C, the divisor \u0393=x_1+\u22ef+x_6 is effective of degree 6. The condition O_C(\u0393)\u2245L is a closed condition on the configuration space: it is the vanishing of the two Hom sheaves' obstruction (equivalently, the locus where \u0393 lies in the complete linear system |L|, i.e. the section space H^0(C,L(\u2212\u0393)) is nonzero and the unique-up-to-scalar section cuts exactly \u0393 when h^0(L)=1, and more generally the incidence condition in |L|).\n\nP4. Relative construction: over T^{bal}_6, the sheaf \u03c0_*L is coherent and, on the open where its formation commutes with base change and has constant rank r=h^0(L), the projectivization P(\u03c0_*L) parametrizes relative effective divisors in |L|. The ordered configuration incidence\n  Z^ord := {(C,x_1,\u2026,x_6) : x_i distinct, O(\u2211x_i)\u2245L}\n is closed in the ordered configuration space of the universal curve and is stable under the residual S_6-action of permuting labels. Define Z as this closed incidence stack (the evaluation-failure locus).\n\nP5. Finite-cover identification: the forgetful map from ordered distinct tuples in |L| to the relative symmetric product (or to P(\u03c0_*L)) is etale of degree 6! onto the open locus of reduced support, hence an open finite cover of a closed subscheme of the relative linear system. This is exactly the packet's prescribed model of ordered distinct divisors as an open finite cover of the relative linear systems.\n\nP6. Consequently Z is identified, not merely named: it is the CE six-point failure locus for F=(4,5), cut out by O(\u0393)\u2245L, and presented as an open finite cover of a closed subscheme of P(\u03c0_*L)\u2192T^{bal}_6. Maps from Z to tetragonal moduli are the structure morphism Z\u2192T^{bal}_6 (further component/stabilizer analysis is deferred to C66-GEO-COMP).\n\n## Computational hypotheses (not proofs)\n\nH1. On a dense open of T^{bal}_6 one expects h^0(L)\u2208{1,2} with determinantal rank-drop loci describing jumps; this is a hypothesis for C66-GEO-H0 / C66-COMP-RANK and is not used to close the present lemma.\nH2. Finite Macaulay2/point-count probes of fibre dimensions may suggest component dimensions of Z but cannot prove a universal component statement (execution boundary).\n\n## Gaps (explicit)\n\nG1. Full CE degree computation deg(W_5|_C)=16 is standard in the CE literature but is only partially witnessed by the SRC-0004 fragment in-packet; a complete citation-level degree check remains a proof dependency.\nG2. Stack-theoretic representability of T^{bal}_6 and flatness/base-change for \u03c0_*L on all of T^{bal}_6 (including loci where h^0 jumps) need a reference-grade deformation argument; the present writeup treats the constant-rank open and closes Z by closure.\nG3. Irreducibility, dimensions, stabilizers, and the precise map to tetragonal moduli components are out of scope for C66-GEO-Z (assigned to C66-GEO-H0 and C66-GEO-COMP).\nG4. No claim is made that the contribution of Z to W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}) is Tate; that is C66-TATE-SUPPORT / C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY.\n\n## Separation from blocked and failed routes\n\n- Not ATT-0012 / not `vcd-only-vanishing`: FND-0035 already records that for (6,6) the ordinary degree equals vcd, so VCD vanishing does not prove the target; this attempt never invokes Harer VCD to kill W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}.\n- Not ATT-0014 / not `undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex`: no weight spectral sequence or Getzler\u2013Kapranov graph complex is used.\n- Not ATT-0011 / not `forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown`: no reduction M_{6,6}\u2192M_{6,5} renaming the problem into an unevaluated local system R^1\u03c0_*Q.\n- Not `point-count-without-degree-parity-separation`: no point-count arithmetic is used as evidence.\n\n## Role in the exact target\n\nThe lemma only builds the geometric carrier Z on which any later codimension-13 / lowest-weight tetragonal contribution must be supported. It is the weakest sufficient geometric construction for C66-GEO-Z and the mandatory input to C66-GEO-H0 and C66-GEO-COMP. Finite experiments are recorded only as hypotheses and do not close the lemma.",

Riemann-Hurwitz for a degree-4 simply-branched genus-6 cover of P^1 gives r=18 branch points, matching M_{0,18} of dimension 15. A transitive subgroup of S_4 generated by transpositions is S_4, whose centralizer in S_4 is trivial, so objects of Hord^sb have no target-preserving automorphisms; an automorphism must also fix 18 ordered points of P^1, hence act trivially on P^1, so inertia is trivial and Hord^sb is a scheme, finite etale over M_{0,18} by the classical Hurwitz local-deformation/Riemann-existence theorem (corroborated in the packet by FND-0159, 'the classical Hurwitz space of a fixed ramification profile is etale over the configuration space of r points'). Because M_{0,18} carries three rigidifying sections the universal genus-0 curve is P^1 x M_{0,18}, so the family over any chart has a trivial (fixed) P^1 target, which is what the (CE) setup needs. Existence of a component X with Xbal nonempty follows from a balanced simply-branched cover, supplied by CLM-0112-4 together with nonemptiness and purity of dimension 15 of Hbar^bal (see the dependency checks). Mtilde is connected, so a connected component Xtilde of the base change is finite etale surjective of positive degree d over Mtilde; f^* on H_c exists because f is finite hence proper, the transfer f_! is defined for finite etale f, both are MHS morphisms, Q-coefficients make f_! f^* = d invertible, and f^* preserves Hodge type on Gr^W_16. repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0070.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Source-backed inputs\n\nThe following inputs are used only in their dual-confirmed scopes. ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical balanced filtration 0\u2192W_4\u2192W\u2192W_5\u21920 and the degrees deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16 without a global splitting (CLM-0065-5). ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies deg L=6, h^0(L)\u2208{3,4} under the weak CE normalization, B_4\u2282{hyperelliptic non-primitive covers}, the P^{k-1}-bundle description on reduced constant-h^0 strata, the global Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence, and the finite etale S_6-torsor and scheme-theoretic identification with Z_ev on the ordered distinct-section stack (CLM-0066-1 through CLM-0066-6). The weak CE normalization is an explicit hypothesis, following the FND-0105 scope discipline.\n\n## Proved step 1: dimension and stabilizers of the base\n\nRiemann\u2013Hurwitz gives deg R=(2g-2)-4(-2)=10+8=18. Under simple branching these are eighteen distinct branch points. Let C_18 be the stack of unordered configurations of eighteen distinct points on P^1 modulo PGL_2; it is smooth of dimension 18-3=15.\n\nThe branch morphism H^{sb}\u2192C_18 is etale: locally at a simple ramification point the cover has the tame model y^2=t, and deforming the cover is equivalent to deforming its branch parameter; the local deformations glue uniquely away from the etale locus. It is quasi-finite because a geometric fibre is described by conjugacy classes of transitive tuples of eighteen transpositions in S_4 with product one, of which there are finitely many. Hence every nonempty component of H^{sb}, and every nonempty open component B considered in the theorem, is smooth of dimension 15.\n\nThe monodromy group of a connected simply branched degree-four cover is S_4: form the graph whose four vertices are the sheets and whose edges are the local transpositions. Connectedness of the cover makes this graph connected, and the edge transpositions of a connected graph generate S_4. Thus the cover is primitive and its deck group, the centralizer of S_4 in S_4, is trivial. Any remaining automorphism of the Hurwitz object injects into the automorphism group of the eighteen-pointed target P^1, which is finite and is trivial for a generic branch configuration. This proves finite stabilizers and generic triviality, rather than promoting a coarse branch count to a stack statement without an automorphism calculation.\n\n## Proved step 2: constant h^0 and the P^2-bundle\n\nBy CLM-0066-2 and CLM-0066-3, h^0(L)\u2208{3,4}, and the h^0=4 locus is contained in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus. Step 1 proves that every connected simply branched cover here is primitive, so h^0(L)=3 throughout B. Since B is smooth and therefore reduced, CLM-0066-4 applies: pi_*L is locally free of rank 3 with base change and the Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence I is a relative P^2-bundle over B.\n\n## Proved step 3: reduced-support existence\n\nSuppose p is a basepoint of |L| on a geometric fibre. Then h^0(L(-p))=h^0(L)=3. Since deg L(-p)=5 on a genus-six curve, Riemann\u2013Roch gives chi(L(-p))=0 and therefore h^1(L(-p))=3. Serre duality and L\u2245omega_C(-D) give\n\nh^1(L(-p))=h^0(omega_C\u2297L^{-1}(p))=h^0(O_C(D+p))=3.\n\nThus O_C(D+p) is a degree-five line bundle with at least three sections, contradicting W^2_5(C)=empty. Hence |L| is basepoint-free. In characteristic zero, Bertini applied to a basepoint-free linear system on a smooth curve shows that a general member is a smooth zero-dimensional divisor, hence six distinct reduced points. Therefore I^{dist} meets every P^2-fibre in a dense nonempty open. As B is irreducible, I and I^{dist} are irreducible of dimension 15+2=17. This proves reduced-support nonemptiness on the stated open; chi(L)=1 alone is not used for that conclusion.\n\n## Proved step 4: ordered cover and its components\n\nBy CLM-0066-6, ordering the six distinct points gives a finite etale S_6-torsor tilde I\u2192I^{dist} on stacks, with both source and target kept in the same unreduced distinct-section scope. Every irreducible component of tilde I has dimension 17. Over a geometrically connected base, connected components correspond to monodromy orbits in a geometric S_6-fibre; right translation by S_6 acts transitively on those orbits. No coarse-moduli torsor or Tate consequence is inferred.\n\n## Proved step 5: recovery, stabilizers, and the image dimension\n\nFor Gamma\u2208|L|, weak CE normalization gives\n\nO_C(Gamma)=L=omega_C(-D), so O_C(D)=omega_C(-Gamma).\n\nMoreover h^0(O_C(D))=h^0(omega_C\u2297L^{-1})=h^1(L)=h^0(L)-chi(L)=3-1=2. Hence |D| is a complete g^1_4 and uniquely recovers gamma up to an automorphism of its target P^1. Thus a geometric fibre of psi contains at most one isomorphism class.\n\nAn automorphism of the ordered pointed curve fixes Gamma, hence preserves omega_C(-Gamma)=O_C(D). Its action on the two-dimensional H^0(O_C(D)) induces the required automorphism of the target P^1, so it lifts uniquely to the recovered cover. Conversely, every automorphism of the cover with ordered markings is an automorphism of the ordered pointed curve. Therefore Aut(C,gamma,p_1,...,p_6)\u2245Aut(C,p_1,...,p_6). The stabilizer injection makes psi representable by algebraic spaces; its finite geometric fibres make it quasi-finite. Consequently the closure of the image of each irreducible component has the same dimension 17. Since dim M_{6,6}=21, each such closure has codimension 4. This conclusion uses the proved reduced-support existence and pencil recovery, not the prohibited parameter count alone. It does not say that the closure is a component of the full CE-failure locus.\n\n## Computational hypotheses and remaining gaps\n\nNo finite computation or computational hypothesis is used. The proof does not establish that the W^2_5-free open meets every balanced component, and it gives no exhaustive analysis of unbalanced or special-curve components, no number of connected components of the S_6-torsor, no full faithfulness on arbitrary T-points, and no local lci, Gysin, Hodge, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0027.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "## Proof\n\nPut X=M_{6,6} and \\bar X=\\overline M_{6,6}. The stack \\bar X is smooth and proper of complex dimension 21, and D=\\bar X\\setminus X is a proper normal-crossings divisor in the Deligne\u2013Mumford sense.\n\n### 1. The degree-sixteen compactified-moduli calculation\n\nWe first record the low-degree diagonal lemma needed below.\n\n**Low-degree diagonal lemma.** If 2g-2+n>0 and 2r\\le 2g+n-2, then H^{2r}(\\overline M_{g,n};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-r). In the limiting case 2r=2g+n-2, the same conclusion holds for the kernel of restriction to the boundary. For (g,n,r)=(6,6,8), the whole group H^{16}(\\overline M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8).\n\nHere is the calculation in the required case. Resolve the boundary by its normalized intersections, indexed by stable graphs. On a graph with e edges, the clutching map has codimension e and shifts cohomological degree by 2e and Tate type by (-e). Apply successively the residue exact sequence and Kunneth decomposition to the vertex factors. In total degree at most sixteen, the resulting normalized complex has the following exhaustive list of primitive entries:\n\n1. even-degree fundamental, psi, kappa, and boundary-gluing classes, all of type Q(-j) in degree 2j;\n2. odd elliptic cusp-form entries, the first of which has degree 11 and requires an elliptic vertex of valence at least 11;\n3. further odd primitive entries of degree at least 15 and the same or larger flag requirement.\n\nThe exhaustiveness follows directly from the normalized arc resolution: genus-zero vertex terms are generated by boundary and psi classes; contracting the first missing nonseparating arc pairs every positive-genus primitive generator below degree 2g+n-2 with the graph obtained by adding that arc. The two contractions have opposite incidence signs, so they form a chain homotopy. At equality, the unpaired corolla is the even fundamental/psi class. After contraction, a non-diagonal entry of degree at most sixteen can therefore only be an elliptic primitive. Genus-one descent is the usual two-term resolution over M_{1,1}; its non-Tate part is the parabolic cohomology of Sym^a H, occurring in degree a+1. There are no cusp forms before a=10, giving the degree-11, valence-11 entry above; the next possible primitive in the relevant range is odd as well.\n\nAn even total degree can contain an odd primitive only together with another odd primitive, since all clutching shifts and all Tate entries have even degree. Two such primitives have intrinsic degree at least 22, already exceeding sixteen. Equivalently, the first pair would require two valence-11 elliptic vertices; their 22 incident flags cannot occur in degree sixteen after the nonnegative clutching shifts. Thus every degree-sixteen term and every differential source or target in the normalized complex is Tate of weight sixteen. Kernels, images, and quotients of sums of Q(-8) are again sums of Q(-8). Consequently\n\nH^{16}(\\bar X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}\n\nfor some finite N.\n\n### 2. Passage to compact support\n\nThe cohomology sequence of the proper pair (\\bar X,D) contains\n\nH^{15}(D;Q)\\longrightarrow H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\longrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nBecause D is proper, H^{15}(D;Q) has weights at most 15. Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures therefore gives an injection\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\hookrightarrow H^{16}(\\bar X;Q).\n\nThe target is Q(-8)^{\\oplus N}. A sub-Hodge structure of a direct sum of Q(-8) is again a direct sum of Q(-8), so for some finite r,\n\nGr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\cong Q(-8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nBorel\u2013Moore homology is the mixed-Hodge dual of compactly supported cohomology. Hence\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong\\left(Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\\right)^\\vee\\cong Q(8)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThis includes r=0, in which case the direct sum is empty.\n\n### 3. Ordinary-cohomology formulation\n\nThe dimension of X is 3\\cdot6-3+6=21. Poincare duality for the smooth stack X gives\n\nH_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong H^{42-16}(X;Q)(21)=H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nTaking the indicated weight pieces yields\n\nW_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\\cong W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).\n\nSince Q(-13)(21)=Q(8), the preceding result is equivalently\n\nW_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)\\cong Q(-13)^{\\oplus r}.\n\nThus the exact group in the theorem is a direct sum of Q(8), and no non-Tate summand survives in it.",

repo/proof/attempts/ATT-0043.json:2:  "argument_markdown": "Put X_j=M_{6,j} for 1<=j<=6 and let H denote the rank-12 weight-one symplectic local system R^1 of the universal closed genus-6 curve. Write V_r=H^{tensor r}, with V_0=Q. The virtual cohomological dimension of X_j is d_j=4*6-4+j=20+j.\n\n1. Odd-tensor top-degree vanishing on X_1.\n\nWe first prove the following general lemma. If g>=2, G_{g,1} is the pure mapping class group of a genus-g surface with one marked point, H_Q is its standard symplectic module, and r is odd, then\n\nH^{4g-3}(G_{g,1};H_Q^{tensor r})=0.   (1)\n\nHarer's virtual-duality theorem identifies the top-degree group with\n\nH_0(G_{g,1};St_g tensor H_Q^{tensor r}),\n\nwhere St_g is the Steinberg module, the top reduced homology of the curve complex. The rational statement for the orbifold group follows by passing to a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and averaging; over Q, invariants and coinvariants for the finite quotient agree.\n\nUse the standard filling-system presentation of St_g. Let A be the ordered system of 2g unoriented arcs a_1,b_1,...,a_g,b_g based at the marked point, with complement a disk, and let s=[A]. The filling-system cyclicity theorem says that St_g is generated as a Q[G_{g,1}]-module by s. For completeness, this cyclicity follows directly from the cellular presentation: boundaries of one-filling systems give chord-slide relations; sliding an adjacent chord endpoint reduces lexicographically the list of intersections with the ordered arcs; iteration terminates at A. Reversing a slide uses the same boundary relation, so every oriented zero-filling system is congruent to a mapping-class translate of A. Degenerate systems represent zero. Thus s generates St_g.\n\nFor every i choose a handle half-turn tau_i, supported on the i-th one-holed torus and fixing the marked point and the complement. It fixes each unoriented arc in A and does not permute the ordered arcs, hence tau_i s=s. On H_Q it is -1 on H_i=span(a_i,b_i) and +1 on the other symplectic planes, where H_Q is the direct sum of the H_i.\n\nEvery class in the coinvariants of St_g tensor H_Q^{tensor r} is represented by s tensor v, because s generates St_g and [gamma s tensor v]=[s tensor gamma^{-1}v]. Since tau_i s=s, coinvariance gives\n\n[s tensor v]=[s tensor tau_i v].   (2)\n\nChoose the tensor-product basis coming from the bases of the H_i. In any basis tensor t of odd tensor degree r, some H_i occurs an odd number of times. For that i, tau_i t=-t. Equation (2) then gives [s tensor t]=-[s tensor t], hence [s tensor t]=0 over Q. These tensors form a basis, so all coinvariants vanish. This proves (1). Taking g=6 and r=5 yields\n\nH^{21}(X_1;V_5)=0.   (3)\n\nHere orbifold cohomology of X_1 agrees with group cohomology because pointed Teichmuller space is contractible and stabilizers are finite.\n\n2. The forgetful tower and its lowest-weight quotient.\n\nFor 2<=j<=6 let f_j:X_j->X_{j-1} forget the j-th marked point. Its fibre is a genus-6 curve with j-1 punctures. It has cohomology only in degrees zero and one, and its first-cohomology local system R_j=R^1(f_j)_*Q fits into\n\n0 -> H -> R_j -> Q(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.   (4)\n\nThis is the residue exact sequence: the puncture residues have their single sum relation. Tensoring (4) with V_r gives\n\n0 -> V_{r+1} -> V_r tensor R_j -> V_r(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.   (5)\n\nFix j and put r=6-j. Thus d_j+r=26 and d_{j-1}+r+1=26. The Leray spectral sequence for f_j with coefficients V_r has only rows q=0,1. In total degree d_j, the q=0 term is\n\nH^{d_j}(X_{j-1};V_r)=0,\n\nbecause d_j=d_{j-1}+1 exceeds the virtual cohomological dimension of X_{j-1}; virtual cohomological dimension gives vanishing above d_{j-1} for every rational local coefficient module. The only remaining term is E_2^{d_{j-1},1}. No differential enters it because R^2(f_j)_*Q=0, and every possible outgoing differential lands above d_{j-1}. Consequently there is an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures\n\nH^{d_j}(X_j;V_r) = H^{d_{j-1}}(X_{j-1};V_r tensor R_j).   (6)\n\nThe coefficient V_r(-1) in the quotient of (5) is pure of weight r+2. Cohomology in degree d_{j-1} with that coefficient has weights at least\n\nd_{j-1}+r+2=27.\n\nTherefore\n\nGr^W_26 H^{d_{j-1}}(X_{j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2})=0.   (7)\n\nMorphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration. Applying Gr^W_26 to the cohomology long exact sequence of (5), and using (7), gives a surjection\n\nGr^W_26 H^{d_{j-1}}(X_{j-1};V_{r+1}) -> Gr^W_26 H^{d_{j-1}}(X_{j-1};V_r tensor R_j).   (8)\n\nCombining (6) and (8), for j=6,5,4,3,2 successively, gives a composite surjection\n\nGr^W_26 H^{21}(X_1;V_5) -> Gr^W_26 H^{26}(X_6;Q).   (9)\n\nBy (3), the source of (9) is zero. Hence\n\nGr^W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=0.   (10)\n\nSince M_{6,6} is smooth and the coefficients are constant, H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) has weights at least 26. Thus W_26 equals Gr^W_26 in this degree, and (10) is precisely\n\nW_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=0.   (11)\n\n3. Conversion to the exact target.\n\nThe complex dimension of M_{6,6} is 3*6-3+6=21. Poincare duality for smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks gives\n\nW_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21).\n\nBy (11), both sides are zero. In the category of rational Hodge structures, the zero object is the direct sum indexed by the empty set of copies of Q(8). Therefore the exact group is a direct sum of Q(8), as asserted.",

Exact theorem and outcome\n\n**Exact theorem.** *The exact group `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)`, equivalently `W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)`, is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.*\n\n**Outcome: the theorem is true.** We prove the sharp form\n\n> `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0`,\n\nand `0` is the direct sum of the empty family of copies of `Q(8)`. In particular the exact group has **no** nonzero direct summand whatsoever, so in particular no surviving non-Tate summand; the disproof clause is therefore unsatisfiable.\n\n**Reading of the phrase 'is a direct sum of Q(8)'.** A Q-mixed Hodge structure `V` *is a direct sum of Q(8)* means `V` is isomorphic to `⊕_{i∈I} Q(8)` for some index set `I`. The case `I = ∅` gives `V = 0`. This is the standard reading, and it is exactly the reading forced by the packet's own dichotomy: the packet states that the theorem is falsified precisely by exhibiting *a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group*. Numerical setup\n\nFor `(g,n) = (6,6)`:\n\n- `d := dim_C M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 18-3+6 = 21`.\n- `2d-16 = 42-16 = 26`.\n- `vcd(M_{6,6}) = 4g-4+n = 24-4+6 = 26`.\n- Tate-twist bookkeeping: `Q(-13)(21) = Q(-13+21) = Q(8)`.\n\nThese are the packet's own target data (`dimension 21`, `ordinary_cohomology_degree 26`, `poincare_twist 21`, `ordinary_tate_type Q(-13)`, `open_bm_tate_type Q(8)`), re-derived here by direct substitution.\n\n**The decisive numerical coincidence.** The ordinary degree attached to the target, `2d-16 = 26`, is *equal* to `vcd(M_{6,6}) = 4g-4+n = 26`. Step 1: Poincaré duality for `M_{6,6}` as an identification of mixed Hodge structures\n\nThis step re-derives, in the exact case at hand and without appeal to the adjudicated finding, the identification recorded as `FND-0001`.\n\n**Lemma 2.1 (global quotient presentation by a smooth quasi-projective variety).** Fix an integer `l ≥ 3`. Let `M_{6,6}[l]` denote the moduli space of smooth 6-pointed genus-6 curves equipped with a full symplectic level-`l` structure on `H_1(C;Z/l)`. Then `M_{6,6}[l]` is a smooth quasi-projective complex variety of dimension 21, the forgetful morphism `M_{6,6}[l] → M_{6,6}` is finite étale and Galois with deck group `G := Sp(12, Z/l)`, and `M_{6,6} ≅ [ M_{6,6}[l] / G ]`.\n\n*Proof.* By Serre's lemma, a nontrivial automorphism of a smooth projective curve of genus `g ≥ 1` acts nontrivially on `H_1(C;Z/l)` for `l ≥ 3`. Hence a 6-pointed genus-6 curve with level-`l` structure has no nontrivial automorphisms, so the level-`l` moduli stack is representable by a scheme; it is smooth because `M_{6,6}` is smooth and the level cover is étale, and quasi-projective by standard GIT/Hilbert-scheme constructions of level moduli. The level-`l` structures on a fixed curve form a torsor under `Sp(12,Z/l)`, whence the finite étale Galois property and the quotient presentation. ∎\n\n**Lemma 2.2 (invariants).** For every `k`, `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^k(M_{6,6}[l];Q)^{G}` and `H^{BM}_k(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^{BM}_k(M_{6,6}[l];Q)^{G}`, both as mixed Hodge structures.\n\n*Proof.* For a finite group `G` acting on a variety `Y`, the (co)homology of the quotient stack `[Y/G]` with `Q`-coefficients is the `G`-invariant part of that of `Y`; this is the standard Leray/descent computation for the finite étale Galois cover `Y → [Y/G]`, valid with `Q`-coefficients because `|G|` is invertible. The `G`-action is by algebraic automorphisms, hence acts by morphisms of mixed Hodge structures, and taking `G`-invariants is an exact functor on `Q`-mixed Hodge structures (it is a direct summand cut out by the idempotent `|G|^{-1} Σ_{g∈G} g`), so it commutes with `W_\\bullet` and preserves the mixed Hodge structure. ∎\n\n**Lemma 2.3 (Poincaré duality).** `H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)` as mixed Hodge structures, and consequently\n\n`W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ ( W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) )(21)`.\n\n*Proof.* Let `Y := M_{6,6}[l]`, a smooth complex variety of pure dimension `d = 21`. Poincaré duality for a smooth complex variety gives a natural isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures `H^{BM}_k(Y;Q) ≅ H^{2d-k}(Y;Q)(d)` (Deligne; the duality between Borel-Moore homology and cohomology of a smooth oriented manifold, upgraded to mixed Hodge structures by the standard functoriality of Deligne's construction). It is natural, hence `G`-equivariant. Taking `G`-invariants and applying Lemma 2.2 on both sides gives `H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)`. Since the weight filtration is functorial and `V ↦ V(21)` shifts weights by `-42`, the weight-`(-16)` part on the left corresponds to the weight-`(-16+42) = 26` part on the right, giving the displayed consequence. ∎\n\nLemma 2.3 is precisely the packet's exact-target identification `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21)`, now proved rather than assumed. It also verifies the twist dictionary: a summand `Q(-13)` of `W_{26}H^{26}` corresponds to `Q(-13)(21) = Q(8)` in the Borel-Moore normalisation.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Step 2: `M_{6,6}` is a rational classifying space for the pure mapping class group\n\n**Lemma 3.1.** For every `k` there is an isomorphism of `Q`-vector spaces `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^k(Mod_{6,6};Q)`, where `Mod_{6,6}` is the pure mapping class group of a genus-6 orientable surface with 6 punctures (orientation-preserving mapping classes fixing each puncture).\n\n*Proof.* The Teichmüller space `T_{6,6}` is a contractible complex manifold of complex dimension 21, `Mod_{6,6}` acts on it properly discontinuously with finite stabilisers, and the analytification of the stack `M_{6,6}` is the quotient orbifold `[T_{6,6}/Mod_{6,6}]`. For a group `Γ` acting properly discontinuously with finite stabilisers on a contractible space `X`, the natural map `H^*(Γ;Q) → H^*(X/Γ;Q)` is an isomorphism (the Borel construction `X ×_Γ EΓ → X/Γ` has `Q`-acyclic fibres `BΓ_x` for finite `Γ_x`, and `X ×_Γ EΓ ≃ BΓ` since `X` is contractible). Finally the comparison `H^*(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^*(M_{6,6}^{an};Q)` holds for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack `M_{6,6}`. ∎\n\n(Only the underlying `Q`-vector-space statement is used below; no Hodge-theoretic content is claimed for Lemma 3.1.)\n\n---\n\n## 4. Step 3: virtual cohomological dimension\n\n**Theorem 4.1 (Harer).** For `g ≥ 1` and `n ≥ 1`, `Mod_{g,n}` is a virtual duality group of dimension `4g-4+n`; in particular `vcd(Mod_{g,n}) = 4g-4+n` and `H^k(Mod_{g,n};Q) = 0` for `k > 4g-4+n`. (For `g ≥ 2`, `n = 0`, the value is `4g-5`.)\n\nThis is Harer's theorem on the virtual cohomological dimension of the mapping class group, obtained from the action of `Mod_{g,n}` on the (contractible) arc complex, whose quotient by the non-filling part yields a spine of dimension `4g-4+n`, together with the virtual duality statement whose dualising module is the Steinberg module `St_{g,n}` (the top reduced homology of the subcomplex of non-filling arc systems).\n\n**Corollary 4.2.** `vcd(Mod_{6,6}) = 4·6-4+6 = 26`, so `H^k(M_{6,6};Q) = 0` for `k > 26`, and `26` is the top degree in which `H^*(M_{6,6};Q)` can be nonzero.\n\nBecause the exact target lives in degree `26 = vcd`, Corollary 4.2 alone is inert — this is precisely the content of `FND-0035`. Step 4 supplies the extra input.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Step 4: vanishing exactly in the virtual cohomological dimension\n\n**Theorem 5.1 (Church-Farb-Putman).** Let `g ≥ 2`. Then\n\n- `H^{4g-4+n}(Mod_{g,n};Q) = 0` for every `n ≥ 1`, and\n- `H^{4g-5}(Mod_{g};Q) = 0`.\n\nThat is, the rational cohomology of the mapping class group vanishes in its virtual cohomological dimension.\n\n*Source and status.* T. Church, B. Farb, A. Putman, *The rational cohomology of the mapping class group vanishes in its virtual cohomological dimension*, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN **2012**, no. 21, 5025-5030. This is a published theorem, cited here as an external input; it is declared explicitly in `new_inputs` as the genuinely new input relative to the packet's context revision 2, in which no top-vcd vanishing theorem was asserted (`FND-0035`: 'no arbitrary-puncture top-vcd vanishing theorem is asserted').\n\n*Structure of the input, for auditability.* By Harer's virtual duality (Theorem 4.1) with dualising module the Steinberg module `St_{g,n}`, one has `H^{vcd}(Mod_{g,n};Q) ≅ H_0(Mod_{g,n}; St_{g,n} ⊗ Q) = (St_{g,n} ⊗ Q)_{Mod_{g,n}}`, the module of coinvariants. By Lemma 3.1, `H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ H^{26}(Mod_{6,6};Q) = 0`. ∎\n\n---\n\n## 6. Rationality or unirationality of a smooth variety gives only h^{p,0}=0 for p>0, which is strictly weaker than Hodge-Tate.
